name: 1PointFive
tech_note: Liquid-sorbent (potassium hydroxide) DAC based on Carbon Engineering technology with geologic sequestration in Class VI wells.
description: 1PointFive is Occidental Petroleum's CCUS subsidiary developing the STRATOS Direct Air Capture facility in Ector County, Texas, designed to capture up to 500,000 tonnes of CO2 per year. Phase 1 is in the final stage of startup with Q2 2026 initial operations expected and Phase 2 commissioning beginning the same quarter. The company has signed CDR offtake deals with Microsoft, Amazon, AT&T, Airbus, Bain & Company, and others.

name: 280 Earth
tech_note: 280 Earth operates a solid-sorbent direct air capture system using a continuous-flow granular sorbent process, co-producing water and able to run on industrial waste heat.
description: 280 Earth is a Google X / Alphabet spin-out (2022) headquartered in Mountain View, CA that operates a 500 t/yr DAC commercial demonstration plant in The Dalles, Oregon (online May 2024). It holds a $40M Frontier offtake for 61,571 tons of CDR between 2024-2030, raised a $50M Series B led by Builders VC in 2024, and is scaling to 5,000 t/yr Gen-1 modules with a targeted 20,000+ t/yr site capacity by late 2025/early 2026.

name: 323ppm
tech_note: Consultancy advising on biochar sourcing and application for agricultural, municipal and urban soil uses; does not itself produce biochar.
description: 323ppm is a small French consultancy (bureau d'étude) dedicated to developing the biochar market in France. It does not operate pyrolysis equipment itself; rather, it advises farmers, municipalities and companies on biochar applications and sources material from certified producers. The company reports working on its first pilot project with a regional farmer.

name: 350solutions
tech_note: Independent third-party Validation & Verification Body (VVB) providing project validation, credit verification, and technical due diligence for CDR registries (Puro.Earth, Isometric) and credit buyers/investors.
description: 350Solutions is a Raleigh, NC-based independent Validation & Verification Body (VVB) for CDR projects. They are accredited by ANAB under ISO 17020 for Environmental Technology Verification via ISO 14034 and are approved by both Puro and Isometric as VVBs. Their diligence efforts have been a part of over $200M in CDR purchase agreements and technology investments. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves — they are part of the CDR ecosystem as a third-party verifier.

name: 3Degrees
tech_note: 3Degrees is a climate solutions consultancy, carbon credit project developer, and retailer that aggregates and brokers third-party CDR credits (biochar, BECCS, ERW, IFM/nature-based) for corporate buyers via its CDR Bridge and CDR Catalyst products.
description: 3Degrees is a San Francisco-based Certified B Corporation that helps Fortune 500 companies, utilities, and other organizations achieve renewable energy and decarbonization goals. Its Carbon Removal Suite offers two products — CDR Bridge, which facilitates access to verified, primarily nature-based removals complemented by hybrid and engineered solutions, and CDR Catalyst, which focuses on emerging/innovative removal project types. 3Degrees is both a carbon credit project developer and retailer that helps clients find climate finance opportunities to meet long-term climate goals.

name: 3R-BioPhosphate
tech_note: Zero-emission high-temperature pyrolysis (up to 850°C) of food-grade animal bones to produce animal bone char biofertilizer (phosphorus recovery) with carbon-negative biochar and bio-oil as co-products.
description: 3R-BioPhosphate Ltd. is a Hungary-based pyrolysis engineering company that upcycles food-grade animal bones into ABC BioPhosphate fertilizer and carbon-negative biochar at its 30-hectare 3R-BIOFARM Upcycling Centre in Trans-Danubia. Led by inventor Edward Someus, the company operates EU-permitted, REACH-registered zero-emission pyrolysis systems with 2,000–20,800 t/y throughput capacities and has advanced to TRL9 industrial readiness. Primary products are phosphorus biofertilizer and biochar, with bio-oil and renewable energy as co-products.

tech_note: Injects CO2 dissolved in water into peridotite rock formations to permanently mineralize it into stable carbonate minerals underground.
description: 44.01 is an Omani climate-tech supplier that accelerates natural peridotite mineralization to permanently sequester CO2 captured from DAC or industrial point sources. The company won the XPRIZE Carbon Removal with Project Hajar and operates pilots in Oman and the UAE with partners including ADNOC, Masdar, Aircapture, Mission Zero, and Holcim.

name: 8 Rivers/Calcite
tech_note: Calcite is a calcium-looping DAC technology that uses hydrated lime to absorb atmospheric CO2, forming limestone that is then calcined in an oxygen-fired kiln to release concentrated CO2 for sequestration while regenerating the sorbent.
description: 8 Rivers Capital is a Durham, NC-based decarbonization technology developer whose Calcite process is a calcium-looping direct air capture technology anchoring the DOE-funded Southeast DAC (SEDAC) Hub in Mobile County, Alabama. Project Cardinal, the first commercial Calcite deployment, is planned for the US Gulf Coast with FEED commencing in 2025 (Wood was awarded the FEED in March 2025), backed by a September 2024 investment from JX Nippon (now ENEOS Xplora). The company is majority-owned by SK Group.

name: A Healthier Earth
tech_note: Operates industrial-scale biochar production via PYREG PX6000/PX1500/P500 pyrolysis systems converting local organic waste into stable carbon for sequestration and carbon removal credits.
description: A Healthier Earth (AHE) is the UK climate-tech R&D subsidiary of Pure Data Centres Group (Pure DC) operating the PureBiochar facility in Royal Wootton Bassett, Wiltshire — billed as the UK's largest biochar plant. The £24M site began phased biochar production in November 2025 and at full capacity is designed to produce ~11,500 tonnes of biochar per year, removing up to 18,500 tonnes of CO2, with credits supplied partly to Pure DC's hyperscale data-centre customers.

name: ACT Group
tech_note: ACT Group is an Amsterdam-based environmental commodities trader and climate project developer/broker that intermediates carbon credits (including biochar CDR projects like Freres Lumber–Microsoft), renewable energy certificates, and emission allowances; it does not physically operate removal technology itself.
description: ACT Group is a Netherlands-headquartered decarbonization solutions provider and carbon/environmental commodities broker founded in 2009, with offices in Amsterdam, New York, Shanghai, and Paris. It develops and facilitates climate projects — including biochar-based CDR deals such as the Freres Lumber project sold to Microsoft — but acts as an intermediary/project developer rather than a physical CO2 remover.

name: ADM
tech_note: ADM captures fermentation-origin CO2 from corn ethanol production and permanently sequesters it in deep saline sandstone formations via EPA-permitted Class VI injection wells.
description: ADM (Archer Daniels Midland) is a global agribusiness giant that operates one of North America's only commercial-scale bioenergy-with-carbon-capture-and-storage (BECCS) facilities, capturing CO2 from its Decatur, Illinois corn-to-ethanol plant and injecting it more than a mile underground into the Mt. Simon Sandstone formation. The CCS division has stored nearly 3 million tons of CO2 since 2011 and recently announced partnerships (Super6 Carbon in Oct 2025, Google/Broadwing Energy) to expand carbon management beyond bioethanol, though it also faced a 2024 leak incident that paused operations until August 2025.

name: ADNOC
tech_note: ADNOC, via its investment arm XRG, co-develops megaton-scale DAC facilities with Occidental/1PointFive in both the UAE and South Texas, and is building CO2 sequestration infrastructure including a fully sequestered CO2 injection well in a carbonate saline aquifer in Abu Dhabi.
description: ADNOC is Abu Dhabi's state-owned energy and petrochemicals group that has entered CDR through joint ventures with Occidental and 1PointFive to develop Direct Air Capture facilities and CO2 storage infrastructure. In May 2025, its investment company XRG signed a Strategic DAC Framework Agreement to consider investing up to $500 million in a 500,000 tpa DAC facility in South Texas, alongside an earlier Joint Study Agreement for a 1 Mtpa DAC plant in the UAE linked to ADNOC's CO2 infrastructure. While ADNOC's main business remains hydrocarbons, its active co-development of DAC capacity and dedicated sequestration wells places it as a CDR division/supplier in this directory.

name: AEROC
tech_note: Spreads crushed basalt rock flour on agricultural fields in Germany to accelerate silicate weathering, forming bicarbonates that sequester atmospheric CO2.
description: AEROC (Aeroc GmbH) is a German startup based in Cologne that develops and scales Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) projects by spreading basalt rock flour on agricultural fields to permanently remove CO2 while improving soil quality and crop yields. The company handles procurement, logistics, application, and MRV of the ERW process and works with farmers via a participation model.

name: APChemi
tech_note: APChemi designs and supplies proprietary PYROMAX biomass pyrolysis reactors that convert agricultural and woody biomass waste into biochar for carbon sequestration and CDR carbon credits.
description: APChemi is an Indian pyrolysis technology company offering biomass-to-biochar plants alongside plastic and tire pyrolysis systems. In April 2025 it partnered with PRESPL and Intellecap to set up Biochar India Private Limited (BiocharIND), intended to be India's largest biochar-based carbon credit platform, with a first facility in Punjab-Haryana producing 10,000 MT of biochar per annum and generating ~25,000 tCO2e of carbon credits per annum.

name: APD
tech_note: Operates certified pyrolysis plants converting Swiss green-waste biomass into biochar for soil amendment and animal feed, generating biochar carbon removal credits.
description: APD (Auen Pflege Dienst AG) is a Swiss company based in Flaach, Zürich, that produces biochar via certified pyrolysis plants using local biomass feedstocks. It is one of the earliest biochar carbon-credit projects (operating since 2019) and partners with First Climate for credit issuance, with annual audits by Carbon Standards International (EBC certification).

name: ARC
tech_note: ARC operates the Amager Bakke/CopenHill waste-to-energy plant in Copenhagen with a demonstration CO2 capture unit (~4 t/day) and is developing the full-scale CopenCapture project with E.ON to capture up to 400,000–500,000 tonnes CO2/yr, a portion of which is biogenic and thus qualifies as BECCS negative emissions.
description: ARC (Amager Resource Center) is a Danish inter-municipal waste management company that owns and operates the Amager Bakke (CopenHill) waste-to-energy plant in Copenhagen. It runs a carbon capture demonstration plant and is developing a full-scale CCS facility (CopenCapture, in partnership with E.ON) targeting up to 400,000–500,000 tonnes of CO2 per year, with the biogenic portion counting as BECCS-based carbon removal.

name: ASF GmbH
tech_note: Municipal waste utility that carbonizes regional green-cuttings into biochar via its own on-site pyrolysis unit, selling the resulting char to the agricultural sector.
description: ASF GmbH (Abfallwirtschaft und Stadtreinigung Freiburg GmbH) is the municipal waste management and street cleaning company for the city of Freiburg, Germany, jointly owned by the city (53%) and Remondis (47%). Alongside its core waste-management business, ASF operates its own pyrolysis plant producing biochar from regional green cuttings for agricultural use. Biochar production is a side activity of a ~400-employee municipal utility rather than a dedicated CDR company.

name: AWN
tech_note: Municipal pyrolysis of woody green-waste fraction into biochar used in compost/Terra Preta products and for agriculture and livestock.
description: AWN (Abfallwirtschaftsgesellschaft des Neckar-Odenwald-Kreises mbH) is a municipal waste-management company in Buchen, Germany, which operates the Biomassezentrum at the Sansenhecken disposal center. Among compost and Terra Preta substrates, they pyrolyze the woody fraction of roughly 20,000 tonnes of regional green waste per year into biochar for agricultural and livestock use. While waste management is their core mandate, they physically produce biochar and thus act as a CDR supplier at a small, municipal scale.

name: Abatable
tech_note: Operates an RFP-based carbon credit sourcing platform plus a market intelligence suite (pricing, policy risk, developer database) covering ~8,500 projects across 129 countries.
description: Abatable is a London-based carbon procurement and market intelligence platform for the voluntary carbon market, connecting corporate buyers with project developers via RFP tooling, pricing data, and policy analysis. It does not physically remove CO2; it is a broker/marketplace/intelligence provider that sits in the CDR and broader VCM ecosystem. Recent partnerships (Symbiosis Coalition, BlueLayer, Exroad) in late 2025/early 2026 confirm active operations.

name: Absolute Climate
tech_note: Independent standards-setter and quality-assurance provider for CDR credits; develops the Absolute Carbon Standard (ACS) and MRV methodologies applied across pathways, with credit issuance handled by partner registries such as Evident's C-Capsule.
description: Absolute Climate designs independent quality-assurance standards for CDR that certify whether a project's claims match their atmospheric impacts, with a universal approach where every removal project is evaluated the same way across all pathways. The company separates quality assurance from credit issuance — it builds standards but does not operate its own registry. It partners with registries (e.g., Evident/C-Capsule) and financial infrastructure providers (Northern Trust) and certifies projects such as Cowboy Clean Fuels and Vesta.

name: Accend
tech_note: Consultancy providing LCA/MRV services and credit brokerage for biochar and mass-timber producers pursuing Puro.earth CORC certification.
description: Accend is a Norwegian consultancy/broker (founded 2020, based in Fredrikstad) that helps biochar and mass-timber producers in Europe and North America qualify for Puro.earth CORC certification through LCA services, and then brokers the resulting carbon removal credits to corporate buyers. They do not operate pyrolysis plants themselves — their clients (OBIO, Biopower Tana, Moelven) are the physical CDR suppliers.

name: Actanol Energie
tech_note: Operates and contracts pyrolysis plants (CarboForce/Carbo-CAP-TEC technology) that convert biomass into biochar, heat, and electricity, generating CO2 removal certificates.
description: ACTANOL Energie GmbH is a German (Kempten, Allgäu) company focused on planning, financing and operating pyrolysis plants for renewable energy and biochar production. It offers contracting models for pyrolysis installations and is a member of the German Biochar e.V. network.

name: Adaptavate
tech_note: Adaptavate manufactures carbon-negative plasterboard ("Breathaboard") by binding ligno-cellulosic crop wastes with minerals that absorb CO2 during curing, and incorporates biochar from pyrolysis to lock biogenic carbon into the building material permanently.
description: Bristol, UK-based construction materials company that has developed a drop-in, carbon-storing alternative to gypsum plasterboard. The technology combines CO2 absorption during mineral curing with biochar incorporation to achieve permanent carbon storage in buildings, and the company licenses its platform to global manufacturers.

name: Adsorb Carbon
tech_note: Pyrolyzes wood chips and sawmill/invasive-vegetation biomass at ~1000°C in a self-sustaining converter to produce steam-activated biochar / activated carbon, using the process gas as thermal energy.
description: Adsorb Carbon is a South African manufacturer based in Brakpan that converts wood chips (from pallet repair centers and responsibly managed forests) into activated carbon and steam-activated biochar, supplying fertilizer, animal feed, cosmetics, water treatment, and mine rehabilitation markets. The company reported capturing approximately 750 tonnes of CO2 in 2024 and positions its patented converter technology as a carbon-capture and green-jobs pathway. While the output is sold primarily as activated carbon for industrial use, the pyrolysis process and CO2-capture claims place it within the biochar CDR supplier category.

name: Aemetis
tech_note: Through its Aemetis Carbon Capture subsidiary, the company plans to capture and sequester biogenic CO2 from dairy digesters, ethanol, and renewable jet/diesel production into a Class VI injection well at its Riverbank, California site.
description: Aemetis is a renewable natural gas, renewable fuel and biochemicals company headquartered in Cupertino, California, operating a dairy biogas digester network and a 65-million-gallon-per-year ethanol facility in the Central Valley. Its Aemetis Carbon Capture subsidiary is developing BECCS projects — engineering and permitting two CCS injection well projects to capture, dehydrate, compress, and sequester CO2 from the Aemetis Biogas anaerobic dairy digester projects, the Aemetis biofuel plants, and CO2 from oil refineries in California. In 2023 the subsidiary was awarded the first CO2 sequestration characterization well permit issued by the State of California.

name: Aeon Blue
tech_note: Develops an integrated saltwater-electrolysis ("chloralkali") process that produces green hydrogen and uses the resulting caustic for a pH-swing "cold capture" of atmospheric CO2, combining DAC with eFuel synthesis and storing excess captured CO2.
description: Aeon Blue is a Cape Breton (Sydney, Nova Scotia) startup developing sustainable eFuel production by harnessing wind energy and seawater, integrating hydrogen production with carbon capture technology using atmospheric CO2. The company's saltwater electrolyzer produces synthetic fuel that can replace gasoline or diesel while capturing CO2 and storing it underground, with some configurations capturing up to six times as much CO2 as the eFuel emits when burned. The company has only three employees and is raising a bridge round before a planned $10M seed round to build a pilot reactor.

name: Ag Carbon Solutions
tech_note: Collects clean woody/yard waste and buries it compacted below the water table under topsoil to create anaerobic conditions preventing decomposition, a biomass burial approach they call the "Dry Decay Method" under their patented Agricultural Production System.
description: Ag Carbon Solutions (ACS) is a U.S. (Florida-based) CDR supplier that diverts silvicultural and yard-waste residuals from landfills and buries them below the water table on agricultural land to sequester carbon while creating Permanent Agricultural Land for grazing/cropland. Their methodology (U.S. Patent 11,511,325) is a biomass-burial pathway rather than BECCS; pilot operations have been reported around Orlando.

name: Agri-Tech Producers
tech_note: Agri-Tech Producers licenses NCSU-developed torrefaction technology (Torre-Tech 5.0) to convert cellulosic biomass into bio-coal and biochar, also marketed as a CO2-sequestering "Combined Remediation Biomass and Bio-Product Production" (CRBBP) process.
description: Agri-Tech Producers (ATP) is a provider of torrefaction technology whose process converts cellulosic biomass such as wood chips and bio-crops into a renewable coal substitute, energy pellets feedstock, and gasification feedstock. The company also markets a patented CRBBP Process that plants fast-growing bio-crops to capture CO2 and convert the resulting biomass into biochar to sequester captured carbon, or into a bio-coal co-fire fuel. Agri-Tech Producers was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Columbia, SC.

name: AgroCCS
tech_note: AgroCCS develops biochar projects that convert agricultural waste (rice husks and straw) into biochar via pyrolysis, distributing it to farmers as a soil amendment and selling carbon removal credits under the Puro.earth standard.
description: AgroCCS B.V. is developing a project in the Varanasi region of Uttar Pradesh, India, that converts agricultural waste (rice husks and straw) into biochar using pyrolysis technology, with the biochar distributed to farmers as a soil amendment. The project's financial model is based on revenue from the sale of carbon credits issued under the Puro.Earth carbon removal standard, and it requires carbon credit financing to operate. The company is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates as a small team (3 employees per Coresignal).

name: AiS
tech_note: Operates a slow-pyrolysis plant coupled to a heating center that converts biomass into biochar for agricultural/circular-economy use.
description: AiS (Arbeit in Selbsthilfe gGmbH) is a German non-profit inclusion enterprise based in Bodelshausen that primarily provides employment to people with disabilities across multiple work areas (agriculture, gastronomy, retail, landscaping). As part of its Kastanienhof site it operates a heating center with a pyrolysis plant that produces biochar within a regional circular-economy concept, though biochar is a side activity rather than its core mission.

name: Air View Engineering
tech_note: Early-stage DAC startup developing small-scale modular solid sorbent units with 3D-printed components and regenerative chambers aimed at reducing regeneration energy requirements.
description: Air View Engineering was founded in 2021, is headquartered in Swansea, United Kingdom, and has 4 total employees. The company is developing smaller, cost-efficient solid sorbent Direct Air Capture systems, leveraging additive manufacturing for modular adsorbent units. It has raised $26.5K, with AirMiners and Remove (Netherlands) among its investors, and has participated in the Shell StartUp Engine UK programme and won Innovate UK Smart Grants.

name: Air to Earth
tech_note: Developer of solid-sorbent direct air capture systems integrated with industrial gas separation and purification to produce pipeline/beverage-grade CO2, with the option to sequester the purified atmospheric CO2 for CDR credits.
description: AIR TO EARTH is a developer of industrial gas infrastructure, specializing in purifying atmospheric CO2 to high-grade pipeline and beverage grade specifications, with a flagship 50-ton-per-day Atmospheric CO2 Beverage Grade Factory that combines industrial gas separation, heat recovery and proprietary filter contacting technologies. The company serves both industrial CO2 customers (beverage, food, fertilizer, horticulture) and the CDR credit market via measurement and sequestration of purified atmospheric CO2. It holds US patents on its systems and appears to be a very small US-based outfit (1 employee on LinkedIn).

name: AirMyne
tech_note: Liquid-solvent DAC using a proprietary low-temperature thermal regeneration process that can be powered by geothermal heat, waste heat, or electricity.
description: AirMyne is a next-generation Direct Air Capture company whose patented process uses a liquid capture agent and a low-temperature thermal regeneration process that can integrate with various low-carbon energy sources. The company was selected for two DOE Regional DAC Hub projects, including the Red Rocks DAC Hub led by Fervo Energy and the CALDAC Hub led by UC Berkeley. AirMyne is planning its DeltaDAC initial project for deployment in the Port of Stockton with support from the California Energy Commission.

name: AirZyme
tech_note: Develops engineered Carbonic Anhydrase enzymes as biocatalysts to accelerate CO2 hydration/absorption, enhancing efficiency of Bio-DAC and post-combustion BECCS capture systems.
description: AirZyme is a Stockholm-based early-stage climate tech startup founded in 2022 developing enzymatic biocatalysts (Carbonic Anhydrase) to accelerate CO2-to-bicarbonate conversion for carbon capture, targeting both Bio-DAC (biomimetic Direct Air Capture) and post-combustion BECCS applications. The company was selected for the remove CDR accelerator and Baker Hughes Energy Ideas program, and has received Vinnova funding for enzyme-enhanced biocatalytic DAC. Team size remains very small (~4 employees) with only ~$50K disclosed funding plus EU-Startups listing €1–2.5M total.

name: Airbuild
tech_note: Airbuild deploys solar-powered microalgae biopanels/biopods to bioremediate polluted water bodies and sewer lagoons, then pyrolyzes the harvested algae plus local organic waste into biochar for permanent carbon storage.
description: Airbuild is a US-based (Troy, NY / San Diego) early-stage climate tech startup founded in 2023 that uses microalgae cultivation integrated with solar panels to clean wastewater and capture CO2, then converts the algal biomass via pyrolysis into biochar. The company is pre-commercial, advancing its first deployment on a 37-acre site in Green River, Utah and pitching similar projects to other rural municipalities.

name: Airbus
tech_note: Modular solid amine-based DAC system derived from Airbus Defence and Space's ISS life-support technology, using temperature-swing regeneration with heat-recovery energy loop; first commercial 250 tCO2/year unit deployed at Deep Sky Alpha, Alberta in late 2025.
description: Airbus, through its Defence and Space division, has commercialized a modular Direct Air Capture unit derived from International Space Station life-support technology, using a solid amine-based filter with thermal regeneration. In November 2025, Airbus delivered a 250 ton/year DAC unit to Deep Sky Alpha in Alberta, Canada, marking its first operational deployment. Airbus also purchases DAC credits from 1PointFive (400,000 tonnes pre-purchase) and resells them to airlines via its Carbon Capture Offer.

name: Aircapture
tech_note: Aircapture builds modular, onsite solid-sorbent direct air capture units that produce high-purity CO2 for industrial/beverage utilization and, via partners like 44.01, for permanent mineralized sequestration.
description: Founded in 2019, Aircapture provides modular on-site DAC machines to produce CO2 at the site of industrial demand, and in late 2024 teamed up with 44.01 to launch a DAC-to-sequestration project in Fujairah, UAE, where captured CO2 is mineralised into rock. In June 2025 the company announced a $50 million Series A round led by the Larsen Lam Climate Change Foundation to scale deployment of its modular DAC systems, following its 2025 XPRIZE Carbon Removal win. Most output serves CO2-as-a-Service (beverage, concrete, agriculture), but Project Hajar provides a permanent removal pathway.

name: Airex Energy
tech_note: Airex Energy develops proprietary CarbonFX torrefaction/pyrolysis technology and operates industrial biochar plants that convert forestry biomass residues into biochar, biocarbon, and biocoal for carbon sequestration and industrial use.
description: Airex Energy is a Canadian biochar supplier that uses its patented CarbonFX™ technology to transform biomass into biochar, biocarbon and biocoal, and has operated Canada's first industrial biochar production plant since 2016. Through its Carbonity joint venture with SUEZ and Groupe Rémabec, the Port-Cartier facility is ramping up to 10,000 tonnes/year and will ultimately produce up to 30,000 tonnes of biochar annually, representing roughly 75,000 tonnes of CO₂ permanently removed from the atmosphere each year. The project secured a three-year forward offtake agreement with Microsoft for 36,000 carbon credits, with the first credits delivered in 2025 after Puro.earth certification.

name: Airfix
tech_note: BECCS project developer and CO₂ transport/storage structurer working with biogenic emitters (biogas, waste-to-energy) to deliver permanent geological storage of biogenic CO₂.
description: Airfix is a Swiss subsidiary of South Pole, backed by the Migros Pioneer Fund, focused on activating the European BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) market. It acts as a project developer and CO₂ transport/storage structurer for biogenic emitters, enabling BECCS projects such as the CO2 Energie AG biogas plant near Zurich and a cross-border storage deal with INEOS Greensand announced in January 2026.

name: Airhive
tech_note: Fluidised-bed DAC reactor using a low-cost geochemical metal-oxide sorbent with electric calcination for CO2 release, deployed in modular container-sized 1,000 t/yr units.
description: Airhive, founded in 2022, is a UK-based DAC company developing a low-cost, energy-efficient and rapidly scalable technology to capture carbon from the atmosphere. Its system uses a novel DAC method based on fluidised beds, a proven industrial technology, and the speed and efficiency of this fluidisation-based capture method, combined with heat recovery and reuse, helps Airhive lower costs. Airhive's 1,000-tonne-per-year system is one of the largest operational DAC systems in the world and is operating as part of Deep Sky Alpha, a cross-technology DAC hub in Innisfail, Alberta.

name: Alcom
tech_note: Pyrolyzes agricultural waste (rice husks in Philippines; cotton stalks and invasive tree biomass in India) into biochar, bio-oil, and heat, generating Puro.earth-certified carbon removal credits.
description: Alcom is a Singapore-based renewable energy and carbon project developer that operates biochar production facilities, including the Puro.earth-certified NuevaChar rice husk biochar plant in Nueva Ecija, Philippines, and a joint venture with THL in India converting cotton stalks and invasive tree species. The company oversees end-to-end biochar carbon removal — from feedstock sourcing through pyrolysis to credit issuance — and also sells bio-oil, heat, and bio-fertilisers as co-products.

name: Alithic
tech_note: Liquid-solvent DAC paired with ex-situ mineralization of alkaline industrial wastes into a cement-replacement SCM, with solvent regenerated via the mineralization reaction.
description: Alithic is a University of Wisconsin–Madison spinoff (formerly Earth RepAIR) developing an integrated direct air capture and mineralization process that uses a sodium carbonate aqueous solvent to react CO₂ with industrial wastes like coal fly ash and steel slag, producing a supplementary cementitious material (SCM) as a saleable byproduct. The company received a Frontier prepurchase in fall 2024, operates a demonstration plant in Madison, and is raising funds to build a ton-scale pilot at the National Carbon Capture Center in Alabama.

name: Alkali Earth
tech_note: Carbon mineralization via spreading reactive steel slag aggregates in gravel roadbeds, where CO2 precipitates as carbonate minerals for permanent storage.
description: Alkali Earth was a US-based CDR startup that attempted to commercialize carbon mineralization using steel slag aggregates in gravel roadbeds. The company has wound down operations after finding its approach difficult to commercialize, and is now publishing its learnings openly for the CDR community.

name: Alpine X
tech_note: Solid-sorbent DAC using metal-organic framework (MOF) pellets in a vertical reactor column, designed to operate at high-altitude Alpine sites (>1500m) where cold, dry air and strong solar insolation enhance adsorption efficiency and power the system.
description: Alpine X is a France-based direct air capture startup developing compact, modular DAC units optimized for high-altitude mountain deployment. The company pairs altitude-optimized conditions with MOF materials that work better at low temperatures and low humidity naturally found at high altitude. The technology is currently in an early pilot phase, moving from research into real-world operation with initial modular systems being tested under Alpine conditions.

name: Alt Carbon
tech_note: Spreads waste basalt rock dust on tea estates and croplands, using multi-layer MRV (soil, groundwater, river sampling plus reactive transport and ML models) to quantify CO2 removal.
description: Alt Carbon is an India-based CDR supplier deploying Enhanced Rock Weathering by spreading basalt rock dust from the Rajmahal Traps on tea estates and farm fields in Darjeeling/eastern India. The company raised a $12M seed round in May 2025 (India's largest climate-tech seed), holds a Frontier $500K prepurchase, a NextGen offtake, and a 10,000-ton MOL Group agreement, and is delivering its first credits via Isometric.

name: Altitude
tech_note: CDR financier/offtaker running purchasing facilities (Ascent 1) that procure large volumes of biochar CORCs from suppliers across South America, Southeast Asia and West Africa for resale to buyers.
description: Altitude is a Switzerland-based carbon removal financier that provides structured offtake and financing to CDR suppliers — primarily biochar developers — via its Ascent purchasing facility. Launched in early 2025, Altitude: Ascent 1 was created to provide structured financing for high-integrity removal projects, with an initial commitment of 50,000 t of CDRs, with availability to bring financing to CDR facilities globally, especially in the Global South, and was later expanded to 250,000t. It is named in our guidance as an ecosystem example.

name: Altitude Carbon
tech_note: CDR financier and offtake aggregator that signs forward purchase agreements for Puro-certified biochar CORCs from third-party project developers.
description: Altitude Carbon is a Switzerland-based CDR financier that procures biochar carbon removal credits (CORCs) from project developers globally, including facilities in Argentina, West Africa, and Southeast Asia. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves but operate a purchasing facility (Ascent 1) to provide offtake financing to biochar CDR developers. Their entire business exists to scale the CDR market through capital deployment, placing them squarely in the CDR ecosystem.

name: Alto
tech_note: Corn-ethanol producer partnering with Vault 44.01 to capture biogenic fermentation CO2 at its Pekin, IL plant and inject it into the Mt. Simon sandstone formation for permanent geologic storage.
description: Alto Ingredients (NASDAQ: ALTO), formerly Pacific Ethanol, is a U.S. producer of specialty alcohols and renewable fuels based in Pekin, Illinois. The company is developing a BECCS project with Vault 44.01 to capture ~600,000 metric tons/year of biogenic CO2 from corn fermentation at its Pekin campus and permanently sequester it in the Mt. Simon sandstone formation. The CCS project has been delayed by Illinois SB 1723 (signed Aug 2025) and may not start generating revenue until 2029-2030.

name: American BioCarbon
tech_note: Pyrolyzes sugarcane bagasse (waste from Cora Texas Sugar Mill in White Castle, LA) into biochar soil amendment and renewable fuel pellets using a patented Biomass Separation Unit.
description: American BioCarbon is a Louisiana-based biochar producer that transforms sugarcane bagasse from the co-located Cora Texas Sugar Mill into biochar and fuel pellets. It is Puro.earth-certified, currently generates ~3,000 CORCs/year from a pilot plant, and is building a larger commercial facility slated to go live in 2026.

name: American BioChar Company
tech_note: Produces NAKED Char biochar via fast pyrolysis (550-900°C) of Southern Yellow Pine forestry residues, sold as granular and liquid (VITAL Blend) soil amendments.
description: American BioChar Company manufactures NAKED Char, a pure activated biochar made from 100% recycled Southern Yellow Pine produced through fast pyrolysis at 550-900°C. They produce blended soil amendments combining pure activated biochar with freshwater-sourced Humate, offered in liquid and granular formulations for lawn, agricultural, and arborist applications. Products are OMRI listed and IBI certified, marketed primarily for soil health with carbon sequestration as a co-benefit.

name: Andes
tech_note: Andes applies beneficial microorganisms alongside crop seeds on agricultural fields to accelerate conversion of atmospheric CO2 into stable soil carbonate minerals via microbially-enhanced silicate weathering.
description: Andes is a carbon removal company focused on the generation of inorganic carbon in agricultural soils, headquartered in Alameda, CA. Andes has partnered with Gold Standard to release the world's first CDR methodology based on microbial carbon dioxide mineralization in agricultural fields. The company has raised $38M to date and deploys microbes across tens of thousands of acres of Midwestern US farmland.

name: Anew Climate
tech_note: Anew Climate is a carbon project developer and marketer/trader specializing in Improved Forest Management (IFM) nature-based removals plus a multi-pathway portfolio including BECCS (via Summit Carbon Solutions marketing agreement), climate-smart agriculture, and avoidance credits.
description: Anew Climate was formed through the combination of Element Markets and Bluesource and is a Houston-based carbon project developer and credit marketer majority-owned by TPG Rise. They were the first to develop and transact improved forest management (IFM) carbon dioxide removal credits, with verified credits spanning IFM, grasslands, wildfire mitigation, climate-smart agriculture, and afforestation/reforestation. They also market BECCS credits from Summit Carbon Solutions' bioethanol CCS project and have signed major offtake deals with Microsoft.

name: Anglo American
tech_note: Applies magnesium-rich ferronickel slag (a mining by-product) to Brazilian agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering, drawing down CO2 as bicarbonate while providing fertiliser co-benefits.
description: Anglo American is a major global mining company running Project Earthstone in Brazil, which uses magnesium-rich ferronickel slag from its mining operations as feedstock for Enhanced Rock Weathering on agricultural land. In September 2025 Anglo American partnered with Isometric (registry) and ZeroEx (MRV) to issue verified Enhanced Weathering credits, with stockpiles estimated to have potential for up to 15 million tonnes of CO2 removal.

name: AntMind
tech_note: Gasifies forestry/wood waste to produce hydrogen energy while capturing CO2 (for underground storage) and producing biochar as a stable carbon byproduct.
description: AntMind is a Canadian startup developing a biomass gasification platform that converts wood waste into hydrogen fuel while capturing CO2 for sequestration and producing biochar as a stable carbon byproduct. The company is currently in a funding phase and designing a pilot facility to process waste from a single sawmill.

name: Anvil
tech_note: Anvil uses a low-energy reactor to contact highly reactive alkaline-bearing ores with atmospheric CO2, accelerating mineralization into stable solid carbonate minerals stored durably on-site.
description: Anvil Capture Systems is a US-based (New York/Somerville, MA) carbon dioxide removal company developing direct-air mineralization using alkaline-bearing ores in a proprietary low-energy reactor. The company received a Frontier prepurchase in Fall 2024 and was awarded a MassCEC climatetech grant in 2025, and is a Greentown Labs member.

name: Aperam
tech_note: Aperam BioEnergia pyrolyzes eucalyptus biomass from its FSC-certified plantations in Minas Gerais, Brazil, and applies the resulting biochar to soil as a durable carbon removal, selling CORCs via Puro.earth.
description: Aperam BioEnergia is the Brazilian forestry/renewable-energy subsidiary of global stainless-steel producer Aperam, historically supplying charcoal to Aperam's Timóteo steel plant and, since 2022, marketing biochar-based carbon removal credits. It is Puro.earth-certified and one of the largest biochar CDR suppliers globally, producing ~10,000 t biochar/yr in 2025 with plans to scale further. The company has sold 100,000+ tonnes of CDR credits, mostly through Puro.earth.

name: Applied Carbon
tech_note: Builds a tractor-pulled mobile pyrolyzer that collects agricultural crop residues and converts them into biochar in a single pass in the field, applying the biochar back onto the soil.
description: Applied Carbon (formerly Climate Robotics) is a Houston-based biochar supplier that deploys automated in-field pyrolysis machines to convert crop waste into biochar for durable carbon removal and soil health benefits. The company has raised a $21.5M Series A led by TO VC with participation from Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, Congruent Ventures, and Elemental Excelerator, and is an XPRIZE Carbon Removal finalist and DOE CDR Purchase Pilot semifinalist. It sells biochar carbon removal credits including to Microsoft's portfolio and is registered with Puro.earth.

name: Applied Gaia
tech_note: Applied Gaia designs and manufactures modular, continuous-feed pyrolysis machines (B3 and B5 models) that convert waste biomass into high-carbon biochar, with co-products including wood vinegar, wood tar, and syngas.
description: Applied Gaia Corporation is a pyrolysis CO2 removal business and technology manufacturer offering modular, scalable continuous pyrolysis technologies. Its flagship B3 machine is a continuous process unit with a 3:1 feedstock-to-biochar ratio, producing 80%+ carbon content biochar and eligible CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs). They sell pyrolysis equipment and project engineering services rather than operating removal facilities at scale themselves.

name: Aquafin
tech_note: Pyrolysis of municipal wastewater sewage sludge into biochar for permanent carbon storage, co-developed with partner companies at the RWZI Menen plant.
description: Aquafin is Belgium's Flemish wastewater treatment utility, established in 1990, which treats household wastewater across Flanders. The company is developing a biochar project at its RWZI Menen site, in partnership with Ebema, D-CRBN, and Stadsbader Group, that will pyrolyze sewage sludge into biochar. While wastewater treatment is its core business, the Menen biochar plant represents a CDR-producing division/project within the larger utility.

name: Aquarry
tech_note: Dissolves alkaline minerals (e.g. crushed kimberlite) into flooded post-mining pit lakes to drive CO2 uptake and precipitation of carbonate minerals that sink to the lake bottom for durable storage.
description: Aquarry is a US-based deep-tech CDR startup (founded 2023, Denver/California) applying pit lake alkalinity enhancement — a hybrid of enhanced rock weathering and ocean alkalinity enhancement — to flooded open-pit mines. The process uses alkaline tailings/waste rock to raise lake alkalinity, absorb atmospheric CO2, and form stable carbonates while remediating mine water. The company is partnered with Winsome Resources at the Renard site in Quebec and with Isometric as registry, with limited-scale field trials planned for spring 2026.

name: Arbon
tech_note: Arbon develops a humidity-swing (moisture-swing) solid sorbent Direct Air Capture technology that captures CO2 in dry conditions and releases it when wet, avoiding heat-based regeneration.
description: Arbon is a Brooklyn, NY-based DAC startup spun out of Columbia University, developing humidity-swing sorbent technology for atmospheric CO2 capture. The company has a Frontier Climate offtake contract (2023) and was selected into the Activate Fellows 2025 cohort. It is small (~5 employees) but clearly an early-stage CDR technology supplier.

name: Arbon Earth
tech_note: Cultivates macroalgae on floating bamboo "OceanPods" and "OceanBaskets" that sink to the deep seabed, sequestering carbon as dissolved inorganic carbon and sediment for centuries to millennia.
description: Arbon Earth is a Swedish marine-based Carbon Dioxide Removal company that removes CO₂ from the atmosphere by cultivating and sequestering macroalgae in the deep ocean, using scalable systems where biomass is lowered to the deep sea floor to isolate carbon for centuries to millennia. The company is ONCRA-certified (verification number ARB-O-001, TRL 7) with first credit issuance in 2023. It is a small team (~5 employees) based in Gothenburg, Sweden.

name: Arbor
tech_note: Torrefies and gasifies waste biomass, then oxy-combusts the syngas in a supercritical CO2 turbine to generate baseload power while producing a high-purity CO2 stream for injection into Class VI sequestration wells.
description: Arbor Energy is a US-based BECCS/BiCRS startup founded in 2022 by SpaceX veterans, building a modular oxy-combustion + supercritical CO2 turbine system that converts waste biomass into clean electricity while capturing >99% of CO2 for permanent geologic sequestration. In July 2025 Frontier signed a $41M offtake to deliver 116,000 tons of CDR between 2028-2030, supporting Arbor's first commercial plant near Lake Charles, Louisiana.

name: Arbor Energy
tech_note: Gasifies waste biomass to syngas, combusts it in pure oxygen to produce supercritical CO2 that drives an 18MW turbine, yielding clean baseload electricity plus a near-pure CO2 stream (>99% capture) for permanent geologic sequestration.
description: Arbor is a US-based (El Segundo, CA) carbon-negative power company founded in 2022 by SpaceX veterans, developing a BECCS system that gasifies waste biomass and uses oxy-combustion with supercritical CO2 turbomachinery to generate clean electricity while capturing >99% of CO2 for permanent geologic storage. Its first commercial facility is planned for Lake Charles, Louisiana with operations expected in 2028, backed by a $41M Frontier offtake for 116,000 tons (2028–2030) and a 25,000-ton Microsoft agreement starting 2027.

name: Arca
tech_note: Arca accelerates surficial carbon mineralization in ultramafic mine tailings and other alkaline industrial waste using autonomous Smart Churning rovers and microwave-based mineral activation, with on-site MRV.
description: Arca (Arca Climate Technologies Inc.), headquartered in Vancouver, BC, is a carbon mineralization supplier that repurposes alkaline industrial waste such as ultramafic mine tailings to permanently store atmospheric CO2 as carbonate rock. The company completed an 18-month pilot at BHP's Mt. Keith nickel mine in Western Australia, has an ISO 14064-2 DNV-validated methodology, and signed a 10-year ~300,000-tonne offtake agreement with Microsoft in October 2025.

name: Aries Clean Technologies
tech_note: Aries operates patented fluidized bed and downdraft gasification systems that convert wastewater biosolids and wood waste into syngas energy and biochar, which is used as a concrete additive and soil amendment for carbon sequestration.
description: Aries Clean Technologies, based in Franklin, Tennessee, develops, designs, and builds proprietary fluidized bed and downdraft gasification systems that convert biosolids and biomass into clean thermal and electrical energy plus Aries GREEN biochar or Bio-Fly-Ash. The biochar product is used as an ingredient in green concrete manufacturing and offers permanent carbon sequestration. Their first large plant in Linden, NJ operated intermittently for a year before being idled in late 2025 for drier technology upgrades, while the company advances a new $180M Sanford, Maine facility.

name: Arigna Fuels
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis/torrefaction of biomass residues (including olive stones) at a Roscommon facility, selling Harvest Flame biochar briquettes as a smokeless fuel alternative and biochar for agriculture/horticulture.
description: Arigna Fuels (part of Arigna Group) is an Irish fifth-generation family firm that transitioned from coal mining/smokeless fuel manufacture to biochar production. It operates what has been described as one of Europe's largest biochar production facilities in Co. Roscommon, producing biochar for fuel (Harvest Flame), horticulture, construction and carbon sequestration applications.

name: Arrhenius
tech_note: Grows microalgae in outdoor photobioreactors using sunlight, then buries the biomass geologically for permanent CO2 storage.
description: Arrhenius AG is a spin-off of Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts based in Switzerland that permanently removes CO2 from the atmosphere by growing and burying microalgae biomass. The company is pursuing a pilot plant, identifying sites in Portugal with Algae for Future SA (A4F), with two locations identified in Lisbon and Matacães, and plans to adapt an existing reactor for ~2 years of microalgae cultivation data collection.

name: Arukah
tech_note: Arukah operates biochar pyrolysis plants (claiming the largest in Southeast Asia, in Cambodia) converting agricultural waste into durable biochar, alongside household/industrial biogas digesters, with a proprietary dMRV stack for carbon credit issuance.
description: Arukah has commissioned Southeast Asia's largest biochar plant in Cambodia together with local partners, transforming agricultural by-products into durable carbon removal and climate-smart fertiliser, while allocating 50% of gross carbon credit revenues to participating smallholder farmers. The Singapore-headquartered firm also deploys household biodigesters and operates a digital MRV platform (CarbonCast) using IoT sensors and computer vision to track biomass and issue high-integrity carbon credits.

name: Ashwood Biochar
tech_note: Produces wood-based biochar via pyrolysis from sustainable woody biomass waste, sold in bulk and granulated forms for soil amendment and carbon sequestration.
description: Ashwood Biochar produces carbon-rich biochar from 100% sustainable woody biomass waste in Lexington, Kentucky, used as a soil amendment to improve fertility, water retention, and as a method of permanent carbon sequestration. They supply large volumes of wood-based biochar in the Southeast US, offering both bulk and granulated products. The company is part of Ashwood Trinity, which invests in soil health and biochar projects and operates a farmer sign-up program offering per-acre incentives.

name: AspiraDAC/Corporate Carbon
tech_note: Solar-powered modular Direct Air Capture using Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) solid sorbents; captured CO₂ is slated for permanent geological sequestration.
description: AspiraDAC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Corporate Carbon Group developing Australia's first solar-powered Direct Air Capture project in partnership with Southern Green Gas and the University of Sydney. The company was selected in Frontier's first round of purchases, with Stripe buying CO₂ removal via the Frontier AMC (backed by Alphabet, Meta, Shopify and McKinsey). In 2025 it signed an MoU with Great Carbon Valley in Kenya to deploy modules aiming for 5,000 t CO₂/yr.

name: Atalanta Climate
tech_note: Compact indoor DAC appliance using next-generation solid sorbents that automatically regenerate and convert captured CO₂ into a stable mineral for permanent storage.
description: Atalanta Climate is a Vancouver, Canada-based climate-tech startup that designs compact, plug-and-play direct air capture devices (their first product is called Ovi) for homes and offices. The units use solid sorbents to capture indoor CO₂ and mineralize it into limestone-like rock dust for permanent storage, while also acting as air purifiers.

name: AtmosClear
tech_note: Biomass-fired power plant (sugarcane bagasse and forestry residues) with post-combustion CO2 capture and geologic storage, capturing ~680,000 tCO2/yr.
description: AtmosClear is a Fidelis New Energy portfolio company developing a BECCS facility at the Port of Greater Baton Rouge, Louisiana. In April 2025 it signed a 15-year contract with Microsoft to deliver 6.75 million metric tons of engineered carbon removal — the largest permanent CDR deal announced to date. Construction is planned for 2026 with commercial operation in 2029.

name: Atmosfuture Limited
tech_note: Develops REVFRACC, a fanless cryogenic Direct Air Capture system that uses liquid nitrogen to supercool and liquefy atmospheric gases, capturing CO2 at high purity while generating baseload power from waste heat.
description: Atmosfuture Limited is a UK-based early-stage startup developing REVFRACC, a patented cryogenic DAC technology that liquefies air to capture CO2 and generate zero-carbon power for data centres. The company was selected for Remove's Europe CDR accelerator in early 2025 and has raised approximately $1.93M. It pitches containerised modular units producing up to 30 MW, targeting pilot and demonstration projects.

name: Atoco
tech_note: Atoco develops solid-state sorbent modules based on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for Direct Air Capture and post-combustion capture, alongside atmospheric water harvesting.
description: Atoco is a California-based startup founded by Omar Yaghi in 2020 focused on commercializing advancements in MOF and COF technologies for carbon capture and atmospheric water harvesting. The company develops solid-state DAC and post-combustion capture modules using nano-engineered reticular materials, and its founder won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the development of MOFs. The startup is also targeting data centers in water-stressed regions as customers for its water-harvesting technology.

name: Aurora Sustainable Lands
tech_note: Aurora owns and manages ~1.65 million acres of historically industrial US forestland under a "carbon-first" Improved Forest Management strategy, generating nature-based carbon credits marketed by Anew Climate.
description: Aurora Sustainable Lands (formerly Blue Source Sustainable Forests Company) is a joint venture between Anew Climate and an equity consortium led by Oak Hill Advisors that has enrolled 1.65 million acres of historically industrial American forestlands into carbon-first management projects, shifting land use from timber harvesting to long-term carbon sequestration. The company was established in 2021 and has completed approximately $1.7 billion in acquisitions to date, with investors including Oak Hill Advisors and AB CarVal. Carbon credits from its forest portfolio are marketed by Anew Climate.

name: Avnos
tech_note: Hybrid DAC using moisture-swing solid sorbents that capture CO2 and co-produce clean water without requiring external heat.
description: Avnos is a Los Angeles-based Direct Air Capture company developing its proprietary Hybrid Direct Air Capture (HDAC) technology, which uses moisture-swing sorbents to capture CO2 while co-producing clean water and eliminating the need for external heat input. The company operates a pilot in Bakersfield, CA, an R&D center in Bridgewater, NJ, and in November 2025 announced Project Cedar, a commercial-scale facility backed by $17M from Shell and Mitsubishi, scheduled to come online by end of 2026.

name: Aymium
tech_note: Aymium operates a patented non-combustion pyrolysis process that converts sustainable biomass into high-purity biocarbon (and biohydrogen), used as a drop-in replacement for fossil coal and coke in metals, power, agriculture, and water purification.
description: Aymium is a U.S.-based biocarbon producer operating multiple facilities in North America, headquartered in Minnesota. In December 2025 it announced a joint venture (TerraForge Biocarbon Solutions) with Weyerhaeuser to scale metallurgical-grade biocarbon production to 1.5M tons/year, with the first McComb, Mississippi facility targeted for 2027. The company has raised ~$200M+ from investors including Steel Dynamics, Rio Tinto, Nippon Steel Trading, CIP, and Fortress.

name: B10
tech_note: Pyrolysis of timber/biomass waste in automated continuous kilns to produce biochar sold as agricultural soil amendment, generating carbon removal credits.
description: B10 (B10 Char) is a biochar producer with a Swiss holding (B10 Char Trading AG) and operations in South Africa. Its first pyrolysis plant near Nelspruit became operational in Q3 2025 with capacity of around 6,000-7,000 tonnes of biochar per year from timber waste, equivalent to roughly 15,000 tCO2 sequestered annually. The company plans to generate most of its revenue from carbon credits while distributing biochar to farmers.

name: BAIE Minerals
tech_note: Develops ex-situ carbon mineralization technology that processes asbestos mine tailings from the Baie Verte, Newfoundland site to produce magnesium oxide which absorbs CO2 and forms stable magnesium carbonate, alongside extracting silica and other critical minerals.
description: BAIE Minerals is a Canadian startup extracting critical minerals from mining waste and using what's left over to draw CO2 from the atmosphere, by leveraging magnesium-rich ultramafic tailings that react with atmospheric CO2 to form magnesium carbonate and permanently sequester carbon. Their process produces high-purity magnesium oxide that absorbs 1.1 tons of CO2 per ton of material within hours; the pilot facility currently processes around 200 pounds of tailings an hour and the company aims to build a full-scale facility in 2027. Business model combines carbon removal credits with sales of extracted minerals for cement and fertilizer.

name: BC Biocarbon
tech_note: Uses a proprietary continuous-feed pyrolysis/gasification biorefinery to convert wood residuals into biochar (Black Bear Biochar), generating Puro.earth-certified CORCs.
description: BC Biocarbon is a Canadian biochar producer based in McBride, British Columbia, that transforms forest and sawmill wood residuals into biochar via a proprietary continuous pyrolysis process. Its Black Bear Biochar is sold as an OMRI-listed soil amendment (including through Walmart, Menards and Home Depot soil mixes) and generates Puro.earth-certified carbon removal credits. The company is co-developing a biorefinery in Carrot River, Saskatchewan, through the BioLesna JV with Dunkley Lumber, backed by $10M from Natural Resources Canada.

name: BCHAR
tech_note: BCHAR designs and sells automated, turn-key industrial-scale pyrolysis systems that convert agricultural waste into biochar, bundled with proprietary MRV software for carbon-credit generation.
description: BCHAR is a Zurich-based developer of biochar carbon removal technologies that transforms bio-waste into biochar, and offers services for project setup, technology delivery, MRV, and carbon credit sales. The company launched its first biochar system in Thailand using coconut husks as feedstock as a pilot project, with insights being incorporated into an upcoming full-scale system. Founded in 2023 and based in Zurich, Switzerland, BCHAR has raised $743K from VC investors including Riceberg Ventures, BlueLion Incubator, SICTIC, Rockstart, and Founderful Campus.

name: BIOCHAR GmbH
tech_note: Pyrolytic carbonization of wood chips into biochar at an industrial plant near Leipzig, with syngas-driven process energy recovery.
description: BIOCHAR GmbH & Co. KG is a German biochar producer part of the CONVORIS Unternehmensgruppe, operating a pyrolysis facility at the Reuden/Draschwitz industrial park near Leipzig. They produce biochar from natural wood feedstocks (softwood chips from German forestry) using BEHORE Technology pyrolysis plants, with syngas recovered as process heat and power. Primary market is agriculture (feed additive, soil amendment) and they are listed as a Puro.earth registered producer.

name: BLOCK
tech_note: Operates a Carbo-FORCE partial-oxidation pyrolysis plant converting regional hedgerow cuttings, waste wood and agricultural residues into biochar for soil application and permanent carbon storage.
description: BLOCK Pflanzenkohle (BLOCK Bio Innovationen GmbH & Co. KG) is a family-run German biochar producer in Osterrade, Dithmarschen, Schleswig-Holstein, founded by brothers Mathis and Steffen Block. Their facility is designed to produce roughly 550 tonnes of biochar per year from ~2,000 tonnes of regional biomass, with waste heat feeding a local district heating network. Carbon removal credits from the project are distributed via Klimate.co.

name: Bakz4ever
tech_note: Cryogenic + membrane-separation DAC coupled with long-duration energy storage, producing solid CO2 intended for ocean storage.
description: Founded in 2021, Bakz4ever is an early-stage Indian climate-tech startup (OPC Pvt Ltd) developing cryogenic direct air capture integrated with long-duration energy storage. The business model has two revenue streams: energy-storage-as-a-service for renewable grid operators, and carbon removal certificates generated by capturing CO2 in solid state and placing it in the ocean for permanent storage. The company appears to be at the concept/prototype stage with ~2 employees, no registry-issued credits, and minimal recent public activity.

name: Banyu Carbon
tech_note: Uses sunlight-activated reversible photoacids to release CO2 from seawater, enabling the ocean to reabsorb atmospheric CO2.
description: Banyu Carbon is a Seattle-based company founded in 2022 by Alex Gagnon and Julian Sachs, former University of Washington professors of chemical oceanography, developing a sunlight-driven process to strip CO2 from seawater. The company has raised a $6.5 million seed round from investors including the Grantham Foundation, Propeller, United Airlines Ventures, Carbon Removal Partners and ReGen Ventures. It is an Ocean CDR supplier physically removing CO2 via photochemical reactions.

name: Basic Dust
tech_note: Basic Dust develops enhanced rock weathering projects by applying finely pulverized alkaline rock powder (e.g., basalt) to farmland and water bodies to mineralize CO2 into bicarbonates for permanent removal.
description: Basic Dust is a US-based enhanced rock weathering project developer with team members in Washington State and New York City. They partner with site owners such as farmers, tribal shellfish companies, and water administrators to deploy alkaline rock dust on land and in water for CO2 removal with co-benefits including reduced water acidity and improved soil quality.

name: Basna
tech_note: Basna produces biochar via pyrolysis of wooden biomass at its Čačak, Serbia facility, holding European Biochar Certificate (EBC) for soil amendment and animal-feed applications.
description: Basna d.o.o. is a Swiss-owned company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Čačak, Serbia, producing biochar and heat energy from wooden biomass using pyrolysis. The company sells EBC-certified biochar for agriculture, animal husbandry, and industrial applications, and is listed as a Puro.earth-registered biochar producer. It remains a small operation (~2 employees on LinkedIn) with limited recent public signals specifically about CDR credit sales.

name: BeZero Carbon
tech_note: BeZero is a carbon credit ratings agency that provides independent, risk-based, project-level ratings on an 8-point scale for voluntary and compliance carbon market projects (including DAC, biochar, and nature-based removals).
description: BeZero Carbon is a London-based carbon ratings agency (founded 2020, launched platform 2022) that rates the quality of carbon credits for buyers, investors and intermediaries. The company is strictly a neutral ratings provider — it does not trade, develop, or broker credits — and covers hundreds of projects across voluntary and compliance markets. It raised a US$32M Series C in January 2025 led by GenZero, bringing total funding to ~$105M.

name: Beccs Stockholm
tech_note: Large-scale bioenergy carbon capture and storage (BECCS) facility capturing biogenic CO2 from a biomass combined heat and power plant using Hot Potassium Carbonate solvent technology, with liquefaction and permanent geological storage under the seabed.
description: Beccs Stockholm is Swedish district energy provider Stockholm Exergi's large-scale Bio-Energy Carbon Capture and Storage project at their bioenergy-generation plant in Stockholm's Värtan neighbourhood. It is designed to capture 800,000 tonnes of CO2 per year, with the captured CO2 liquefied and permanently stored under the seabed where it is mineralised, with start-up planned for 2028. Funded by SEK 20 billion Swedish government support, €180 million from the EU Innovation Fund, and long-term carbon removal offtake agreements with buyers including Microsoft.

name: Bella Biochar Corp
tech_note: Bella Biochar manufactures certified organic biochar from landfill-diverted waste wood using a non-pyrolytic thermal conversion unit, applied as a soil amendment with ~1,000-year carbon permanence.
description: Bella Biochar Corporation is an Ontario, Canada-based biochar producer that converts landfill-diverted forest and wood waste into certified organic biochar. The company is Puro.earth CORC-certified and markets its biochar for soil amendment, animal bedding, wetland restoration, and carbon dioxide removal credits. It is a small, founder-led operation targeting ~5,000 tonnes of CO2 removal per plant at scale.

name: Beston Group
tech_note: Beston Group manufactures industrial-scale biomass pyrolysis/carbonization equipment (e.g. BST-50S, BST-06 Max) that converts forestry and agricultural waste into biochar for durable carbon sequestration.
description: Beston Group Co., Ltd., based in Zhengzhou, China, specializes in waste-to-resource pyrolysis solutions covering oil sludge, plastics, rubber, and biomass. On the biochar side, they supply the pyrolysis equipment used by CDR project developers; Beston Group is an official technology provider for Puro.earth and is the first biochar equipment partner of Isometric. Their BST-50 units power Exomad Green's biochar production, with Phase 2 bringing a total of 15 industrial-grade systems online.

name: Beyond Captur
tech_note: Beyond Captur develops battery-based electrochemical direct air capture technology that operates entirely on electricity, avoiding thermal regeneration steps.
description: Beyond Captur is a South Korea-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) company leveraging battery-based carbon capture technology that operates entirely on electricity, eliminating the need for thermal processes. The company signed an MoU with Great Carbon Valley to launch Kenya's first electrochemical Direct Air Capture pilot project, followed by a Definitive Agreement to advance that collaboration. It is a technology supplier building removal hardware rather than a buyer or ecosystem actor.

name: Bhumi Sewa Networks
tech_note: Converts agricultural residues into biochar via farmer-cooperative projects in Nepal, bundled with agroforestry and sold as verified carbon credits.
description: Bhumi Sewa Networks is a Nepal-based (Pokhara) for-purpose company that partners with farmer cooperatives to convert agricultural residues into biochar, generating verified carbon removals while promoting regenerative agriculture. They provide end-to-end biochar project development, from feasibility to implementation, and sell carbon credits to corporate buyers.

name: Bio-Logical
tech_note: Bio-Logical operates a pyrolysis facility in Kabati, Kenya that converts agricultural waste (eucalyptus wood, macadamia husks, Mathenge) into biochar, which is blended with compost into an organic fertilizer (Asili) distributed to smallholder farmers.
description: Bio-Logical is a Kenya-based climate tech company specializing in biochar carbon removal, producing biochar that sequesters carbon dioxide and serves as a soil amendment to improve livelihoods of Kenyan smallholder farmers. Its facility in Kabati, claimed to be Africa's largest biochar plant, can produce up to 5,000 tonnes of biochar and 24,000 tonnes of compost annually. The company signed a significant Microsoft offtake deal in 2023, the largest single purchase of biochar carbon removal from an African project to date.

name: Bio-Restorative Ideas
tech_note: Pyrolyzes bamboo residues into biochar in Puerto Rico using a half-mobile 5-train pyrolysis reactor (installed by ARTi in 2023), generating Puro.earth CORCs.
description: Bio-Restorative Ideas (BRi) is a Puerto Rico-based biochar producer that converts bamboo residues and post-hurricane biomass waste into biochar using a mobile pyrolysis unit installed at the Eureka hacienda site. The project is registered on Puro.earth and managed by carbon developer GECA Environnement, targeting roughly 3,000 mtons of biochar annually from 13,000 mtons of bamboo feedstock. Biochar is applied in soils, building materials, and other sequestration end-uses locally.

name: BioC
tech_note: BioC operates end-to-end pyrolysis plants that convert biomass into engineered biochar, bio-oil, and syngas, using a gravity-fed indirect-heating carbonization process, and sells CDR credits plus biocarbon reductants to metallurgical customers.
description: BioC is a Singapore-based biochar carbon-removal supplier that builds and runs PyroCCS pyrolysis facilities producing certified CDR credits and biocarbon products. They target both carbon-credit buyers (spot and long-term offtake) and industrial customers in steel/metallurgy seeking drop-in replacements for met coal and anthracite. They also offer an in-house MRV software stack ("Sarva Carbon") compatible with Carbon Standards International and Isometric registries.

name: BioCarb Solution
tech_note: Aggregates biogenic CO2 from Danish biogas plants and arranges permanent geological storage in North Sea depleted oil fields (Project Greensand), sold as Puro.earth-certified CDR credits.
description: BioCarb Solution is a Danish biogenic CO2 aggregator based in Hirtshals that collects CO2 from biogas plants, waste incinerators and biomass-fired district heating, and arranges permanent underground storage in depleted North Sea oil fields via Project Greensand. The company sells Puro.earth-certified CDR credits and is owned by a consortium of Danish biogas investors (Agri Energi, GrønGas, Sindal Biogas, Vrejlev Bioenergi, Bioman) under Danish Bio Commodities.

name: BioCarbon
tech_note: Proprietary pyrolysis technology converts woody agricultural waste into biochar and co-products (wood vinegar, bio-oil, syngas) primarily for use as renewable charge carbon in EAF steelmaking.
description: BioCarbon is an Australian climate-tech company using proprietary pyrolysis technology to convert woody agricultural waste into biochar ("GreenChar"), bio-oil, wood vinegar, and syngas. Their primary application is replacing metallurgical coke in Electric Arc Furnace steelmaking, with a first commercial-scale plant under development at Bulahdelah, NSW. They also pursue ACCU-verified carbon credits from the biochar production process.

name: BioCirc
tech_note: BioCirc operates eight biogas plants in Denmark and is installing CO2 liquefaction/capture at five of them, with captured biogenic CO2 to be permanently stored subsea via Project Greensand.
description: BioCirc Group, founded in Denmark in 2021, is one of the largest biomethane producers globally, operating eight biogas plants. A Nordic Investment Bank loan is financing infrastructure to clean and liquefy captured CO2 for delivery to Project Greensand, which will store the CO2 underground in the Danish part of the North Sea. CCS implementation is underway across five biogas plants, with operations ramping from 2026 to 2032, aiming to capture and store up to 1 million tonnes of CO2.

name: BioFlux
tech_note: BioFlux is a Netherlands-based consultancy that helps biochar project developers with feasibility, pyrolysis tech selection, MRV, LCA, certification (EBC, Puro.earth, Verra), and carbon credit commercialization.
description: BioFlux helps organizations design, certify, and deploy biochar projects and builds the operational infrastructure that connects biochar production to carbon markets, integrating feedstock networks, production logistics, and verification systems. They are a consultancy/enabler rather than a biochar producer themselves — a consultancy firm focused on project development and optimisation with a focus on biochar carbon removal, guiding project developers and biochar producers on biomass waste streams, pyrolysis, and carbon credits.

name: Biocarbon Tech Asia
tech_note: Biocarbon Tech Asia is a Malaysian biochar producer listed on the Puro.earth registry pursuing CORC 100+ carbon removal certificates.
description: Biocarbon Tech Asia is listed as a biochar supplier on Puro.earth with a production facility in Malaysia, targeting CORC 100+ durability credits. According to the Puro listing, the project appears to be in early development stage with 0 CORCs in stock and feasibility/implementation work ongoing. There is limited independent public information about the company beyond its Puro supplier page.

name: Biocare
tech_note: Biocare develops, finances, and delivers biochar CDR projects globally, converting waste biomass (almond shells, forestry residues, fire-damaged timber) into biochar via pyrolysis with third-party-verified removal credits.
description: Biocare is an engineering-focused developer of biochar carbon removal projects, bringing deep technical expertise and project delivery capability across Asia, Australia, North America and South America. They are developing 10+ projects, representing more than 300,000 tonnes of annual CO2e removal. The company is a registered supplier on Puro.earth with the Kangaroo Island Biochar Project.

name: Biochar Byte
tech_note: Produces biochar via industrial-scale pyrolysis (and Kon Tiki kilns) of agricultural biomass/crop residues in Maharashtra, India, for soil amendment and carbon sequestration.
description: Biochar Byte is an unfunded company based in Pune, India, founded in 2024 by Udaykumar Mathapati and Vinayak Patil, operating as a provider of industrial-scale biochar production and carbon credit generation. The startup transforms agricultural biomass into carbon-rich material through pyrolysis, integrating geospatial imaging and technology-driven logistics to collect crop residues and prevent open-field burning.

name: Biochar Earth
tech_note: Produces biochar via controlled pyrolysis of coconut shell waste sourced from smallholder farmers in the Philippines, selling durable Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) credits.
description: Biochar Earth sells premium carbon dioxide removal at $199 per metric tonne of CO2 removed, grounded in controlled pyrolysis and conversion into durable biochar designed for long-term storage, representing CO2 taken from the atmosphere and stored as a material. The company's BCR operations are currently centered in the Philippines, using coconut biochar to also support the local economy in the Global South. They also offer separately-priced avoided-emissions credits tied to diverting coconut waste from open burning.

name: Biochar Life
tech_note: Distributed smallholder-farmer biochar production via flame-curtain/Kon-Tiki and improved Aom kilns, certified under the EBC Global Artisan C-Sink standard with dMRV.
description: Biochar Life is a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation and impact venture of nonprofit Warm Heart Worldwide that trains smallholder farmers in Thailand and Africa to convert crop waste into biochar using low-tech kilns (including the new Aom Kiln). The company issues carbon-sink credits under the Global Artisan C-Sink / EBC Tropical Farmer standard and has generated over 21,000 tonnes of verified carbon removals since founding.

name: Biochar Now
tech_note: Biochar Now operates patented kilns that pyrolyze waste wood into high-quality biochar sold for agriculture, reclamation, odor control, and use as a filler in plastics, concrete, and asphalt.
description: Biochar Now is a biochar producer focused on production and sale of biochar, with products serving specialty agriculture, reclamation, oil and gas, odor control, and nutrient removal; it was founded in 2011 and is based in Berthoud, Colorado. The company has spent years developing patented manufacturing and emissions-compliance technologies that turn waste wood into high-quality carbon for a diverse customer base. It is a physical CDR supplier operating at manufacturing scale.

name: Biochar Production and Carbon Removal Company
tech_note: Develops low-capex on-farm pyrolysis kilns that convert wood chips into biochar for soil application, plus a chain-of-custody software platform for issuing Biochar Carbon Units.
description: CapChar is a UK-based biochar startup (founded 2021) offering on-farm pyrolysis kiln technology and a software platform for tracking and verifying Biochar Carbon Units (BCUs). They have operational plants in Cornwall and North Wales and developed their own Biochar Carbon Code for UK biochar quantification.

name: Biochar Rendsburg
tech_note: Operates a commercial Carbo-FORCE partial-oxidation pyrolysis plant that carbonizes organic residues into biochar for soil and material applications.
description: Biochar Rendsburg GmbH is a German company based in Borgstedt (Schleswig-Holstein) that operates the first commercial Carbo-FORCE pyrolysis plant on the site of the AWR waste-disposal region. The facility converts organic residues into biochar via partial oxidation, producing a durable carbon material and removing CO2 from the atmosphere. It is affiliated with the Carbo-FORCE technology brand (Bauer group ecosystem) and listed on the biochar-zero marketplace.

name: Biochar: a scalable carbon sink solution
tech_note: Pyrolysis of forest biomass residues (via Airex Energy CarbonFX torrefaction) and sewage sludge (via PYREG Pyrolis S2B) into stable biochar used for soil amendment and carbon sequestration credits.
description: SUEZ is a global water and waste management company that operates a dedicated biochar carbon-removal business line through joint ventures. It co-owns Carbonity, Canada's largest biochar plant in Port-Cartier (Québec), with Airex Energy and Groupe Rémabec, and partners with PYREG to produce biochar from sewage sludge. SUEZ targets 350,000 tonnes of biochar production per year by 2035.

name: Bioenergie Frauenfeld
tech_note: Operates a SYNCRAFT wood-fired CHP plant in Frauenfeld, Switzerland that pyrolyzes regional residual wood into EBC-certified biochar while co-producing renewable electricity and district heat.
description: Bioenergie Frauenfeld AG, a joint venture between Energie 360° AG and Schweizer Zucker AG, operates a climate-positive wood-fired power plant in Frauenfeld that has been in operation since spring 2022, converting regional residual wood via pyrolysis into durable carbon (biochar). The carbon-negative plant removes 9,000 metric tons of CO2 annually and was built in collaboration with IWK Integrierte Wärme Kraft AG and SYNCRAFT. Carbonfuture has signed a partnership with Bioenergie Frauenfeld to enable large-scale carbon removal deliveries.

name: Biofine
tech_note: Biofine uses patented acid-hydrolysis biorefinery technology plus a Verenovo slow-pyrolysis reactor to convert lignocellulosic waste into carbon-negative biofuels (ethyl levulinate), renewable chemicals, and biochar for soil amendment and CDR credit generation.
description: Biofine Developments Northeast (BDNE Inc.) is a Maine-based biorefinery developer commercializing patented Biofine Technology to produce ethyl levulinate biofuel, renewable chemicals, and biochar from forestry residues and cellulosic waste. Its Phase I facility in Lincoln, Maine aims to produce ~20,000 tons of biochar annually alongside fuels, and the project has a Puro.earth preliminary biochar methodology assessment, positioning it as a CDR supplier.

name: Biokol
tech_note: Aggregates small-scale Swedish producers using Brachio pyrolysis boilers to convert FSC-certified forestry residues and crop residues into EBC-certified biochar, with heat byproduct fed into local heating networks.
