description: Biokol.se is a Swedish biochar company founded in 2018 that builds pyrolysis boilers (via sister firm Brachio AB) and aggregates small-scale producers who convert forestry residues into high-carbon biochar. In September 2025 the project became the first to have biochar credits validated under the Rainbow Standard for a 1,000-year permanence horizon, with roughly 2.6 tCO2e sequestered per tonne of biochar produced. In early 2026 Biokol.se announced a scale-up partnership with ZeroMission to distribute Swedish biochar carbon credits.

name: Bioman
tech_note: Bioman captures biogenic CO2 from its biogas production plants and sends it to permanent geological storage, under an 8-year Danish NECCS contract.
description: Bioman ApS is a Bigadan-owned Danish biogas company that bid to capture and store 25,000 tonnes of CO2 annually at a support price of DKK 1,175.5 per tonne under the Danish Energy Agency's NECCS fund. As of August 19, 2025, Bioman merged into its parent group and now operates legally as Bigadan Sourcing & Commodities, covering the full value chain from biomass and biogas to CO2 storage.

name: Biomass Projects
tech_note: Pyrolyzes invasive mesquite and other Weeds of National Significance in Western Australia into biochar for permanent carbon storage and soil amendment.
description: Biomass Projects is developing the Mardie char project in Western Australia, one of the largest biochar initiatives globally, which by 2028 is expected to reach an annual carbon removal volume of 500,000 tonnes. Biomass Projects is an accredited supplier of Carbon Removal Certificates (CORCs) with puro.earth. Carbonfuture provides dMRV services for the project, with support from Residual.

name: Biopower Tana
tech_note: Pyrolysis of local residual biomass (wood waste, agricultural, and animal-processing residues) to produce biochar used in fertilizer pellets and animal feed, with carbon credits issued via Puro.earth.
description: Biopower Tana AS is a Norwegian biochar company, founded in 2020 and based in Austertana, Finnmark, that plans to convert residual biomass (from forestry, dairy, slaughterhouses, and fish farms) into biochar for animal feed and agricultural fertilizer. The company is listed on Puro.earth as an early-development supplier with 0 CORCs in stock, and its first plant was planned for commissioning in 2025 following a feasibility study.

name: Biorecro
tech_note: Biorecro is a global BECCS project developer that integrates bioenergy-with-carbon-capture systems at existing biomass power, CHP, pulp/paper, ethanol, and biogas facilities, commercializing the resulting Puro.earth-certified CORC removal credits.
description: Biorecro is a global project developer with over 15 years of experience focusing on BECCS, integrating BECCS operations into existing industrial facilities such as biomass power, CHP, pulp and paper, and bioenergy facilities including ethanol and biogas, to bring carbon removal to market at scale. In September 2025 Gevo's subsidiary Net-Zero Richardton signed a carbon removal sales agreement that strengthens Biorecro's BECCS project portfolio with an in-operation project. In November 2025, Gevo announced its first delivery of Puro.earth-certified CORCs to Biorecro North America, fulfilling a multi-year agreement expected to generate approximately $26 million in revenues over five years.

name: Biosorra
tech_note: Biosorra operates a patented pyrolysis system that converts tropical agricultural crop residues into biochar ("Biochar Bora") applied to farmland in Kenya, sequestering carbon while improving soil.
description: Biosorra is a female-led Kenyan biochar producer aiming to remove at least one megaton of CO2 per year by 2030 via deployment of 150+ reactors. It runs what it describes as the largest industrial biochar facility in East Africa at Thika/Murang'a and supplies Kenya Nut Company and smallholder farmers. In October 2025 the company secured $3.5 million in seed funding to scale its biochar operations in Kenya.

name: Black Bull Biochar
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of forestry co-products (sawdust, woodchip) and deploys it on UK farms, particularly in dairy manure management systems, for long-term soil carbon storage.
description: Black Bull Biochar is a UK-based biochar producer that operates pyrolysis units (using PYREG and BioMaCon technology) to convert forestry co-products into biochar for UK agriculture, particularly dairy manure management. The company raised £4 million in late seed funding in December 2025 to scale operations in the North West of England and expand into Denmark, and has previously secured £3.2 million from the UK's Net Zero Innovation Portfolio.

name: Bloomineral
tech_note: Uses algae-driven biomineralization in seawater-filled open basins (leveraging cement-kiln waste for alkalinity) to convert atmospheric CO2 into calcium carbonate crystals used as carbon-negative additives for cement, paint, paper, and cosmetics.
description: Bloomineral is a French climate deeptech startup spun out of the Marble studio in 2024 and hosted at the LSCE laboratory in Saclay. It is developing a biomineralization process in which algae-like organisms combine CO2 with alkaline industrial waste to produce calcium carbonate powder, permanently storing carbon while replacing high-emission construction materials.

name: Blue Flint Ethanol
tech_note: Corn ethanol biorefinery capturing biogenic fermentation CO2 and permanently sequestering it in an on-site Class VI injection well in the Broom Creek formation.
description: Blue Flint Ethanol is a wholly owned subsidiary of Harvestone Low Carbon Partners (HLCP) located near Underwood, North Dakota, that generates, captures, and sequesters biogenic CO2, and was the first CCS entity to commence carbon capture operations following the August 2022 passage of the Inflation Reduction Act. Using CCS, Blue Flint captures 100% of its CO2 emissions from fermentation, injecting approximately 600 metric tons of CO2 per day permanently stored about one mile below the surface in the Broom Creek formation. As a CDR-tech operating subsidiary of HLCP, it qualifies as a "division" supplier for the directory.

name: Blue Planet
tech_note: Mineralizes CO2 with calcium-rich industrial wastes (geomass) to produce synthetic limestone (CaCO3) aggregate for carbon-negative concrete, permanently storing CO2 in the built environment.
description: Blue Planet Systems is a Los Gatos, California-based company that uses its patented Geomimetic® mineralization technology to convert CO2 from industrial flue gas (or DAC) into synthetic limestone aggregates for use in carbon-negative concrete. The company operates its San Francisco Bay Aggregates facility in Pittsburg, CA, and demonstrated the world's first net-zero embodied carbon concrete slab in February 2025. Much of their feedstock is point-source CO2 (CCUS), though the technology is pathway-agnostic and can accept DAC CO2.

name: Blue Sky Biochar
tech_note: Produces and distributes pelletized biochar and related soil amendments (rock dust, mycorrhizae, sea minerals) for home gardeners, landscapers, and farmers as a soil amendment.
description: Blue Sky Biochar is a small Ventura, California-based biochar and soil amendment retailer founded in 2011 by Michael Wittman. They sell biochar-based garden starter kits and soil enhancement products primarily to home gardeners and farmers, with a focus on regenerative soil health rather than carbon credit issuance. The company is not listed on any CDR registry and operates as a niche consumer/agricultural biochar supplier.

name: BlueGreen
tech_note: BlueGreen applies proprietary Lake Guard® algaecide formulations to remediate harmful algal blooms in lakes and reservoirs; they claim the killed algal biomass sinks to sediment, locking away sequestered carbon, and they sell verified Net Blue™ credits under the SOCIALCARBON® methodology.
description: BlueGreen Water Technologies (netbluezero.com / bluegreenwatertech.com) is a US-headquartered (R&D in Israel) water-restoration company that treats harmful algal blooms and monetizes the resulting carbon sequestration as Net Blue™ credits. In April 2024 the Social Carbon Foundation issued 12,913 tCO2e of credits from their Mantua Reservoir (Utah) project at $100/credit, and in November 2025 the company announced a peer-reviewed study in Phycology validating the approach. They raised a Series B2 round led by TAU Capital with OurCrowd in 2024 to scale the CDR business unit.

name: BlueShift
tech_note: Uses a membrane-free electrochemical process to extract CO2 from seawater (as limestone via mineralization with calcium/magnesium from industrial waste) while co-producing critical minerals and rare earths from mine tailings and coal fly ash.
description: BlueShift is a Boston/Cambridge-based startup founded in 2024 developing membrane-free electrochemical direct ocean removal (DOR) co-located with coal plants and desalination facilities. The company exited stealth in March 2025 with $2.1M pre-seed funding from ConocoPhillips, Ridgeline, and MassCEC, and is building a Boston Harbor pilot. It is an independent supplier, not a division of a larger firm.

name: Bluefield Renewable Energy
tech_note: Uses proprietary pyrolysis/thermo-chemical conversion to transform waste biomass into biochar, generating carbon removal credits and supplying biochar for applications including green concrete.
description: Bluefield Renewable Energy is a Singapore-headquartered biochar producer whose operations officially started in 2023. Using proprietary advanced pyrolysis technology, it converts waste into biochar — a stable, carbon-rich material — with applications including integration into green concrete for lower-embodied-carbon construction. It states it is the sole Asia firm certified by the European Biochar Certificate (EBC) and International Biochar Initiative (IBI), and partners with SembWaste in Singapore to generate carbon removal credits.

name: Blusink
tech_note: Deploys engineered "Blusinky" substrates on the seabed that increase local alkalinity and act as attachment surfaces for calcifying rhodolith (coralline algae) beds, sequestering carbon via biogenic carbonate formation.
description: Blusink is a UK-based marine CDR startup pioneering seabed-deployed substrates that restore rhodolith (coralline algae) beds while enhancing local ocean alkalinity. Their dual approach combines materials engineering, chemistry and biology, with MRV based on total alkalinity measurements and calcification rates validated through a mesocosm experiment with Plymouth Marine Laboratory. Early deployments have been conducted off the coast of Colombia.

name: Boomitra
tech_note: Boomitra develops large-scale soil carbon projects with farmers/ranchers using AI and satellite-based MRV, and recently launched a biomass burial (BiCRS) project in Botswana.
description: Boomitra is a US-headquartered carbon project developer that works with over 100,000 farmers and ranchers across 10+ countries on soil carbon and grassland restoration, using proprietary AI and satellite remote sensing for MRV. In 2025 it expanded beyond soil carbon with the Oasis BiCRS project in Botswana, burying encroaching woody biomass for 100+ year storage. It won the 2023 Earthshot Prize and has issued record-scale Verra-verified credits.

name: Brimstone
tech_note: Brimstone's patented Rock Refinery process replaces limestone with calcium silicate rock to co-produce ordinary portland cement and alumina, with magnesium byproducts that absorb atmospheric CO2 via mineralization.
description: Brimstone is a U.S. industrial innovator whose patented Rock Refinery produces portland cement, smelter-grade alumina, and supplementary cementitious materials, with a roadmap to co-produce steel, aluminum, magnesium, titanium, and other critical minerals from abundant silicate rocks. Chemically extracting calcium oxide from silicate avoids CO2 release, and the process yields a magnesium byproduct that absorbs CO2 from the atmosphere. Amazon signed a commercial agreement in August 2025 to reserve annual volumes from Brimstone's forthcoming plant, which is being engineered near Reno, Nevada.

name: Brineworks
tech_note: Electrochemical DAC using a patented saltwater electrolyzer that co-produces hydrogen and can run on intermittent renewable power, targeting sub-€100/ton CO₂ capture costs.
description: Brineworks is an Amsterdam-based climate tech startup founded in 2023 that is developing low-cost electrochemical Direct Air Capture. Its patented saltwater electrolyzer captures CO₂ from the atmosphere while co-producing green hydrogen, with outputs targeted at both carbon removal and e-fuels (SAF, e-methanol) for aviation and shipping. The company raised a €6.8M seed round in September 2025 and was awarded a €1.8M EIC Accelerator grant, aiming for pilot-scale commercial readiness by end of 2026.

name: Brodie Biomass
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of locally sourced woody biomass on a Surrey farm using a Woodtek Bibi C1000 unit; sells biochar and biochar-compost blends and registers carbon credits under Puro.earth.
description: Brodie Biomass is a UK-based (Brockham, Surrey) biochar producer that launched its production facility in 2024 and holds European Biochar Certificate (EBC) Animal Feed Plus grade status. It sells biochar and biochar composts for agriculture and gardens, and registers the associated carbon removal credits under Puro.earth. In March 2025 it acquired the SoilFixer brand, expanding its soil-improvement product range.

name: Bureau of Economic Geology
tech_note: State geological survey and university research institute conducting science on geological CO2 storage, subsurface characterization, MRV, and CCS/CDR policy.
description: The Bureau of Economic Geology (BEG) is the State Geological Survey of Texas, a research unit within the University of Texas at Austin's Jackson School of Geosciences. Its Gulf Coast Carbon Center (GCCC) has been a global leader since 1999 in geological CO2 storage research, monitoring, site characterization, and CCS/CDR science. BEG is a research institution that supports the CDR/CCS ecosystem rather than a commercial supplier of removals.

name: Bussme Biochar
tech_note: Pyrolysis of biomass to produce EBC-certified biochar for agricultural soil amendment, certified under Puro.earth's Biochar methodology.
description: Bussme Biochar AB is a Swedish family-run biochar producer based in Svedala, Skåne, operating since 2020 and producing EBC-certified biochar primarily for agriculture and soil applications. The company is registered on Puro.earth (project Bussme-01-Svedala) with 2,332 CORCs issued and 1,811 retired under the Biochar 2022 methodology, with a crediting period running through 31 Aug 2025. Its sister company Bussme Energy divested district-heating plants to Solör Bioenergi in 2020 and 2024, but the Biochar AB entity remains a distinct operating biochar producer.

name: Bygen
tech_note: Bygen uses a proprietary low-temperature activation (LTA) pyrolysis process to convert nut shells and sustainable forestry residues into activated carbon, with the durable carbonized product functioning as a biochar-like carbon sink.
description: Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, Bygen produces sustainable activated carbon from renewable agricultural and forestry by-products. Their novel 'low-temperature activation' (LTA) technology converts carbon-rich materials like nut shells and wood into activated carbon, optimising pyrolysis and activation to improve energy efficiency and reduce emissions. At a North American production plant, Bygen's technology was independently validated as carbon-negative via a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) in accordance with ISO 14040, 14044, and 14067 standards.

name: C-Crete
tech_note: C-Crete produces cement-free concrete using pulverized non-carbonate rocks (granite, basalt, zeolite) as binders, which avoids Portland cement emissions and absorbs atmospheric CO2 during and after curing via mineralization.
description: C-Crete Technologies is a California-based materials science company commercializing Portland-cement-free concrete in which pulverized natural rocks like granite, basalt and zeolite replace cement. Their binder emits no CO2 during manufacturing and the cured concrete absorbs CO2 from the air over time, resulting in a carbon-negative building material. The company has poured thousands of tonnes across commercial, government and residential projects and received over $10M in grants from the US DOE and California Energy Commission.

name: C-Fix
tech_note: Solar-powered direct air capture concept using alkaline metal sorbents with electrolytic regeneration.
description: C-Fix is developing a solar-powered Direct Air Capture concept using alkaline metal sorbents and electrolytic regeneration, and is currently raising seed money to hire a team and develop the technology. The website is minimal (essentially a single landing page) with no evidence of deployed pilot plants, deliveries, or team presence. No LinkedIn company page or recent press coverage was found.

name: C2X/SunGas Renewables
tech_note: Uses SunGas's S1000 biomass gasification technology to convert sustainably-sourced forestry residues into bio-methanol while capturing and geologically sequestering ~1 million tonnes/year of biogenic CO2 at the Beaver Lake project in Louisiana.
description: C2X (majority-owned by A.P. Moller Holding, with ENEOS as minority shareholder) is the majority owner of SunGas Renewables, which is developing the Beaver Lake Renewable Energy biomethanol plant in Pineville, Louisiana on a former paper mill site. The project will produce 500,000+ tonnes/year of bio-methanol for shipping/aviation while capturing and permanently storing biogenic CO2, and has signed a 3.6 million-tonne, 12-year CDR offtake with Microsoft (December 2025). FEED is underway with Kiewit and Jacobs; FID targeted for 2026 and operations for 2029.

name: CDR.fyi
tech_note: CDR.fyi is a market-data and analytics platform that tracks durable CDR transactions, prices, suppliers, purchasers, and projects, providing leaderboards, reports, and a subscription-based data portal.
description: CDR.fyi is a trusted source for durable carbon removal market data that tracks CDR transactions, prices, and supplier rankings, and is used by buyers, suppliers, investors, and policymakers worldwide. Originally a volunteer effort, it structured as a Delaware public benefit corporation (PBC) in 2024 with a "give to get" model, keeping website content free while offering subscription plans for companies to access comprehensive datasets and insights. It is a CDR-ecosystem reporter/analytics provider, not a physical CO2 remover.

name: CHAR Technologies
tech_note: Uses proprietary high-temperature pyrolysis (HTP) to convert woody biomass and organic waste into biocarbon (biochar, CleanFyre biocoal) and renewable gases (RNG, green hydrogen, syngas).
description: CHAR Technologies Ltd. (TSXV:YES) is a Toronto-based cleantech company operating high-temperature pyrolysis facilities that transform woody biomass and organic waste into biochar/biocarbon products and renewable energy. Its biochar qualifies for CORC carbon removal credits, and the company also supplies biocoal to replace pulverized coal in steel blast furnaces via a partnership with ArcelorMittal. Recent activity includes the Thorold Renewable Energy Facility commissioning and a Québec biocarbon pellet facility acquisition with a 62,500-tonne offtake agreement.

name: CO2 Sink
tech_note: Purported biochar producer; no verifiable public information found about operations, products, or customers.
description: CO2 Sink (co2sink.co) is listed as a US-based biochar company, but web research returned no substantive information about the firm — no press, no projects, no registry listings, and no distinguishing operational footprint. LinkedIn shows only 4 employees and the entity appears to have minimal public presence. Note: co2sink.org is an unrelated defunct EU geological storage research project completed in 2010.

name: CO280
tech_note: CO280 develops, finances, and operates BECCS retrofit projects at pulp and paper mills, installing modular post-combustion liquid amine capture units (via partner SLB Capturi) on recovery boilers to capture biogenic CO2 and permanently store it in geologic formations.
description: Vancouver-based CO280 develops biomass carbon removal and storage projects in the pulp and paper industry, including financing, developing, owning and operating large-scale CDR projects in partnership with pulp and paper companies, and is currently developing more than 10 projects including 5 high-priority projects anticipated to be active by 2030. Microsoft signed one of the largest-ever engineered CDR purchase deals, agreeing to offtake nearly 3.7 million tonnes of carbon removal over 12 years from a CO280 project at a U.S. Gulf Coast pulp and paper mill.

name: CO2CO
tech_note: Grows microalgae at scale and pyrolyses the biomass into biochar for soil, afforestation, or construction aggregate applications.
description: CO2CO is a UK carbon-removal start-up that has developed a process of growing microalgae and converting the biomass into biochar, used for agricultural or afforestation purposes to embed carbon into the soil carbon reservoir, with the aim of delivering the process at scale. The company is a spin-out involving founders from the energy and infrastructure sectors and academics from Imperial College London, and has received an Innovate UK feasibility grant to develop microalgal biomass as a bitumen alternative.

name: CO2CirculAir
tech_note: CO2CirculAir develops SMART-DAC, a membrane-based direct air capture system using wind-driven membrane gas absorption with KOH solution and membrane electrolysis/electrodialysis for regeneration.
description: CO2CirculAir is a Dutch R&D and innovation start-up formed by a group of membrane technology experts developing a direct air capture system. Funded under the UK DESNZ Greenhouse Gas Removal Programme, SMART-DAC is a passive wind-driven DAC system using a two-step process with KOH-based absorption and membrane electrolysis/electrodialysis regeneration. The pilot first captured CO2 in September 2023 and operated at over 80% uptime through April 2025.

name: CO2Rail
tech_note: Develops specialized railcars that capture CO2 from ambient air using regenerative braking energy from trains in regular service, eliminating the need for fans via the train's slipstream.
description: CO2Rail Company is a Houston, Texas-based climate tech company whose main service is a proprietary rail-based system that captures carbon dioxide from ambient air and diesel locomotive emissions using energy generated by train regenerative braking. Its purpose-built rail cars capture energy from regenerative braking to charge onboard batteries while leveraging the slipstream of the moving train in a ramjet-type process to avoid the need for fans, directing air into a cylindrical CO2 collection chamber. The company remains pre-commercial, with no deployed railcars or registry-issued credits; it is still fundraising from venture capital as of recent LinkedIn activity.

name: CO2Zero
tech_note: Modular, tech-agnostic DAC integrator that combines third-party capture technologies with power-to-heat and clean water co-production to reduce energy demand and cost per ton.
description: CO2Zero is a Rotterdam, Netherlands-based Direct Air Capture startup that was incubated through the YES!Delft accelerator program. The company describes its approach as a tech-agnostic modular integrator that combines multiple DAC technologies with power-to-heat and water co-production, targeting capture costs below €150/ton. They are an independent startup (not a division of a parent company — YES!Delft is an incubator, not a parent).

name: CORMETECH
tech_note: Designs and manufactures honeycomb-structured, amine-based sorbent adsorbers/contactors that serve as the core capture component of third-party DAC systems, and also develops point-source capture monoliths.
description: CORMETECH is a North Carolina-based emissions-control manufacturer (SCR catalysts) that has extended its ceramic-extrusion and honeycomb-substrate expertise into CO2 capture, producing custom-designed amine adsorbers for DAC developers and point-source capture systems under its PATHWAY product line. They collaborate with leading DAC developers, supplying the adsorber hardware at the core of those systems, and have received multiple DOE/NETL awards to advance their DAC contactor and NGCC point-source capture technology.

name: CREW Carbon
tech_note: Doses municipal wastewater with finely crushed limestone/alkaline minerals during biological treatment, converting biogenic CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate that is discharged to the ocean for long-term storage.
description: CREW Carbon is a US-based CDR supplier that adds alkaline minerals like limestone to municipal wastewater treatment streams, converting CO2 into stable bicarbonate ions that are eventually discharged to the ocean. In 2025 the company delivered the first-ever Wastewater Alkalinity Enhancement credits under its $32.1M offtake agreement with Frontier for 71,878 tonnes between 2025-2030. In early 2026 CREW also secured a $2.35M award from the Colorado Energy Office to deploy at a Colorado wastewater facility.

name: CTRL + Z
tech_note: Pyrolyzes agricultural waste into graphene derivatives, aiming for carbon-negative conversion of biomass into durable carbon-rich materials.
description: CTRL Z is an India-based early-stage startup converting agricultural waste into graphene derivatives through a process they describe as carbon-negative. The company positions itself as a biochar-to-graphene carbon removal supplier and was selected for the remove accelerator Phase 2. With only ~3 employees and limited recent public signals, operational status is uncertain.

name: CUR8
tech_note: Intelligence, due diligence, portfolio construction, and offtake financing platform that aggregates third-party CDR credits for corporate buyers.
description: CUR8 is a UK-based carbon removal intelligence and portfolio platform that helps corporate buyers procure, finance, and manage CDR credits across pathways including DAC, enhanced weathering, and biochar. They act as a market-maker/broker rather than a removal supplier, providing due diligence, portfolio construction, and offtake financing for clients such as British Airways, Standard Chartered, and Coca-Cola HBC.

name: Caligenia
tech_note: Caligenia pyrolyzes organic waste (including chicken manure) into BACTERCHAR, a biochar-based biofertilizer combined with plant-growth-promoting microorganisms applied to degraded agricultural soils.
description: Caligenia is an Argentine biotechnology startup that leverages scientific knowledge in biochar, microorganisms, and soil management practices to restore degraded soils and remove CO2 from the atmosphere. The company is building the first biochar production plant in Argentina, located in Luján. The Argentina-based firm transforms chicken manure into "bacterchar" to turn degraded soils into farmable land, and is seeking to relocate/expand to Tulsa and test in U.S. fields.

name: Cap Clean
tech_note: Develops biofuel/bioenergy facilities (SAF, renewable diesel) using oxy-fuel biomass combustion with CO2 capture routed to geologic storage, structured as BECCS with CCS-as-a-service.
description: Cap Clean Energy Corp. is a Calgary, Alberta-based clean energy development company (subsidiary of Aether Catalyst) developing biofuel and bioenergy facilities with carbon capture and geologic storage. It signed a 2023 MOU with Raven SR to co-develop BECCS-style SAF and renewable diesel projects in Canada, and in May 2025 announced a proposed facility in Beaver County, Alberta near existing carbon capture infrastructure. Their published technology covers oxy-fuel CO2 capture from biomass combustion with permanent geologic storage.

name: Capital Link
tech_note: Capital Link Green (CLG) produces biochar via controlled pyrolysis of organic waste biomass and issues carbon removal credits verified through Isometric.
description: Capital Link Green (CLG) transforms waste into premium biochar, while removing carbon, restoring ecosystems, and generating credits backed by science and measurable results. Verified Carbon Credits are issued via Isometric, backed by peer-reviewed methodology. Credits are insurable against reversal through Oka, via Lloyd's of London.

name: Captur Tower
tech_note: Develops Direct Air Capture units designed to retrofit existing industrial cooling towers, using their airflow and waste heat to lower DAC capital and operating costs.
description: Captur Tower was founded in 2023, is headquartered in Madrid, Spain, and has 5 total employees. The company's system integrates direct air capture (DAC) units with existing cooling towers, leveraging waste heat for efficient CO2 removal directly from the atmosphere. It is an early-stage supplier building DAC removal technology rather than a broker or buyer.

name: Captura
tech_note: Uses proprietary bipolar-membrane electrodialysis to strip CO2 from seawater for permanent storage or reuse, restoring the ocean's capacity to absorb atmospheric CO2.
description: Captura is a Pasadena, California-based Direct Ocean Capture company spun out of Caltech in 2021 that uses high-performance bipolar-membrane electrodialysis to extract CO2 from seawater, allowing the ocean to reabsorb additional atmospheric CO2. The company operates a 1,000 t/yr pilot in Kona, Hawaii (with Equinor) and is designing its first 30,000–50,000 t/yr commercial facility, with a 30,000-credit offtake signed by MOL.

name: Capture6
tech_note: Capture6 pairs direct air capture with water treatment facilities, using an electrochemical process to convert waste brine into a sodium hydroxide solvent that binds atmospheric CO2 into solid mineralized carbonates while producing freshwater as a co-product.
description: Capture6 is a US-based DAC supplier that integrates carbon removal with desalination and water treatment infrastructure, turning waste brine into a CO2-capturing solvent while recovering freshwater. Active projects include Project Wallaby in Western Australia (with Pilot Energy), Project Monarch in Los Angeles County (with Palmdale Water District), and a partnership with K-Water in South Korea.

name: CarStorCon
tech_note: CarStorCon produces a biochar-based additive (Clim@Add®) from pyrolyzed woody biogenic residues that is incorporated into concrete and asphalt, permanently embedding biochar carbon in building materials and generating CO2-sink certificates.
description: CarStorCon Technologies GmbH, founded in 2022 in Marienhafe, Germany, develops the Clim@Add® additive — a modified technical carbon derived from biochar pyrolysis — that turns concrete and asphalt into permanent carbon sinks. The company classifies its approach as Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) and works with construction-industry partners across the DACH region and Europe. As of 2025 it reports over 5,000–6,500 m³ of climate concrete realized and participates in EU-funded biochar research consortia.

name: Carba
tech_note: Autothermal low-temperature pyrolysis of waste biomass into biocarbon, followed by anoxic burial in landfills for permanent CO2 storage.
description: Carba is a Minneapolis-based CDR supplier that converts waste biomass into stable biocarbon via a patented autothermal low-temperature pyrolysis process and sequesters it through anoxic burial in landfills for 1,000+ year durability. The company has a 44,000-ton offtake with Microsoft, a $7M DOE Carbon Negative Shot grant, and recently raised $6M led by Rusheen Capital and Canopy Generations Fund. Its first project in Burnsville, MN is commissioning with Isometric-certified deliveries starting Q1 2026.

name: Carbex
tech_note: Carbex GmbH produces biochar and biochar-based products (animal feed charcoal, soil amendments) via pyrolysis at its Dischingen, Germany site, co-located with technology provider Carbon Technik Schuster GmbH.
description: Carbex GmbH is a manufacturing company of biochar-based products located in Dischingen, Germany, offering a range of biochar and biochar-based products for a variety of applications. The company's registered purpose covers R&D, production, trading and distribution of carbon-containing products, especially biochar, as well as energy and emissions trading. It operates at the same address as technology provider Carbon Technik Schuster GmbH, with managing director Vanessa Schuster.

name: Carbfix
tech_note: Injects CO2 dissolved in water into basaltic bedrock where it reacts with divalent cations to form stable carbonate minerals, providing permanent in-situ mineral storage.
description: Carbfix is an Icelandic company that permanently stores CO2 by dissolving it in water and injecting it into basaltic rock formations, where it mineralizes into stable carbonate minerals within approximately two years. It operates point-source mineralization at the Hellisheiði and Nesjavellir geothermal plants and partners with DAC providers like Climeworks (Orca/Mammoth) for storage. It is developing the Coda Terminal, a large-scale transport-and-mineralization hub.

name: CarbiCrete
tech_note: Mineralizes CO2 into cement-free concrete blocks/pavers made with steel slag binder, replacing Portland cement and locking CO2 in the product via carbonation curing.
description: CarbiCrete is a Montreal-based carbon removal technology company that licenses a patented process for producing cement-free concrete by replacing cement with steel slag and mineralizing CO2 into the concrete for permanent storage. They license their technology to block and paver manufacturers in Canada, the northeastern US, and (from 2026) France via Saint-Gobain's POINT.P brand.

name: Carbo Culture
tech_note: Uses patented Carbolysis™ pyrolysis reactors to convert waste biomass into stable biochar while generating renewable energy.
description: Carbo Culture is a Finland-based climate technology company that uses patented Carbolysis™ reactors to take waste biomass and convert it into stable biochar, locking carbon away for centuries while generating renewable energy. In 2025 the company announced ARC Middenmeer, a new biochar plant at the ECW Energy site in Middenmeer, North Holland, expected to remove more than 20,000 tonnes of CO2 annually while producing 40,000 m³ of biochar and 16 MW of sustainable energy. The company produces premium biochar for carbon removal, horticulture, and industrial decarbonization.

name: Carbo-FORCE
tech_note: Carbo-FORCE manufactures Carbo-CAP-TEC pyrolysis plants that convert organic residues (wood chips, manure, sewage sludge) into biochar at 650-900°C using partial oxidation, while also producing useful heat.
description: Carbo-FORCE GmbH was founded by Malte Graf and Kai Alberding at the end of 2017 in Preetz, northern Germany, and has developed a pyrolysis system for carbonizing biomass. BAUER Resources GmbH acquired 50% of the company's shares as of January 1, 2023. The company sells modular pyrolysis plants (e.g., CF-250) that produce biochar and renewable heat, with deployments in Germany and Dubai.

name: CarboHeroes
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis of biomass residues to produce biochar that is incorporated into agricultural soils for permanent carbon storage, financed via carbon credits.
description: CarboHeroes GmbH is a Berlin-based biochar developer establishing a circular economy based on organic waste and pyrolysis, aiming to remove 500 million tons of CO2 by 2050. Starting with pilot projects in Costa Rica, they aim to build a global enterprise with local partners, focused on Latin America. Listed on Puro.earth as a biochar supplier in early development with no CORCs currently in stock.

name: CarboVerte
tech_note: CarboVerte operates a pyrolysis plant in Eibenstock, Germany to produce biochar from biomass, selling plant-charcoal and biochar-based soil amendments and feed additives for agriculture, livestock and horticulture.
description: CarboVerte is a German company specialized in producing biochar and biochar-based products using a modern pyrolysis plant. Based in Eibenstock, its focus is the agricultural and livestock industry as well as urban green spaces. Products are sold via their own store and Amazon, marketed as permanent atmospheric CO2 sinks for soil, composting and animal feed applications.

name: Carbofex Oy
tech_note: Continuous pyrolysis of PEFC-certified spruce thinnings at ~700°C producing biochar with >90% carbon content, plus renewable heat for district heating.
description: Carbofex Oy is a Finnish biochar producer based in Nokia, operating a continuous pyrolysis plant that converts PEFC-certified spruce thinnings into high-carbon-content biochar while generating renewable heat. The company sells CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs) via Puro.earth and has signed multi-year forward offtake deals including one with Shopify. It was an XPRIZE Carbon Removal Top 60 finalist.

name: Carbogenics
tech_note: Pyrolyzes difficult-to-recycle organic waste and secondary biomass into CreChar® biochar, primarily sold as an additive to anaerobic digestion and wastewater treatment plants, with carbon sequestration as a co-benefit.
description: Carbogenics is an Edinburgh-based University of Edinburgh spinout (2016) producing CreChar®, an engineered biochar made from paper waste and secondary biomass via pyrolysis. Its primary market is enhancing biogas yields in anaerobic digestion plants, with the stable carbon in the biochar providing durable CDR. The company is expanding into the US (New Mexico) following a $3M funding round in early 2026.

name: Carboliva
tech_note: Pyrolysis of olive pits and pulp to produce biochar as soil amendment and construction material additive, with clean thermal energy as co-product.
description: Carboliva is a Spanish biochar producer based in Osuna (Seville) that converts olive grove biomass (pits and pulp) into high-quality biochar via pyrolysis, while also generating clean thermal energy. Its biochar is used as a soil amendment in olive groves and tomato greenhouses and is being explored as a low-carbon additive in concrete and asphalt.

name: Carbon 1.5
tech_note: France-based Direct Air Capture startup developing solid-sorbent DAC technology aimed at low-energy-consumption CO2 removal from ambient air.
description: Carbon 1.5 is a French direct air capture company focused on developing sorbent-based DAC systems with significantly lower energy consumption than incumbents. Public information on the company is limited, and independent corroboration of recent milestones, funding, or deployments was not found in search results.

name: Carbon America
tech_note: Develops end-to-end CCS projects at corn-ethanol plants (biogenic fermentation CO2 → Class VI geologic storage) and builds proprietary cryogenic point-source capture technology (FrostCC).
description: Carbon America is a Colorado-based vertically integrated CCS developer focused on capturing biogenic CO2 from ethanol plants (Yuma, Sterling, Bridgeport) and sequestering it in Class VI geological storage wells. It is also developing a proprietary cryogenic point-source capture technology (FrostCC) for industrial emitters. The ethanol CCS projects qualify as BECCS removal; the FrostCC technology applied to fossil point sources would be emissions-avoidance rather than CDR.

name: Carbon Bank
tech_note: Carbon Bank operates an enhanced rock weathering project in Northumberland, UK, spreading finely crushed basalt rock dust from local quarries onto arable farmland, with planned afforestation projects under the Woodland Carbon Code.
description: Carbon Bank is a UK-based CDR project developer and part of the Green Britain Group (sister company to Ecotricity). They run an enhanced rock weathering project in Northumberland using basalt from Breedon quarries spread on local farmland, and plan afforestation/nature recovery projects aligned with BSI Flex 701 and the Woodland Carbon Code.

name: Carbon Blade DAC
tech_note: Develops a distributed, containerized Direct Air Capture system using a rotating blade contactor, alkaline absorption solvent, and electrodialysis bipolar membrane (EDBM) regeneration powered by onboard solar/wind.
description: Carbon Blade is a California-based climate technology company that develops hardware solutions to capture CO2 directly from the air as a climate mitigation strategy. The company acquired foundational DAC IP from RoCo® in 2023. It is currently collaborating with UC San Diego to construct a pilot carbon capture plant on campus capable of both capturing and storing CO2.

name: Carbon Capital
tech_note: Produces certified biochar from invasive encroacher bush (Acacia spp.) using retort kiln pyrolysis at Farm Gai Kaisa 159 in the Grootfontein/Otjozondjupa region of Namibia, with carbon removal credits issued via Puro.earth.
description: Carbon Capital is a Namibian biochar producer operating Farm Gai Kaisa 159, reportedly the largest industrial biochar project in Africa, developed in partnership with biochar developer Planboo. The project has produced over 16,000 tonnes of certified biochar, issued 19,500+ CORCs on Puro.earth, and earned a Sylvera A rating, with buyers including Boeing.

name: Carbon Capture Company
tech_note: Swedish certification scheme/body that issues forest-based carbon removal credits under its proprietary Carbon Forestry Standard – Sweden, using national forest inventory data and owners' digital forest plans.
description: Carbon Capture Company (CCC) is a Swedish certification body that developed the Carbon Forestry Standard – Sweden, a methodology for certifying carbon credits from actively managed Swedish forests. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves; they certify, verify, and issue credits for forest owners and maintain a certification registry, aligning with the EU Carbon Removal Carbon Farming regulation.

name: Carbon Cell
tech_note: Carbon Cell combines pyrolysis-derived biochar with natural bio-based polymers to make an expandable, moldable rigid foam that replaces EPS/EPP/PUR/PIR in packaging and building insulation, locking biochar carbon into durable products (and ultimately soil at end-of-life).
description: Carbon Cell, founded by Imperial College alumni Elizabeth Lee, Ori Blich, Eden Harrison and Juan Ignacio Rion, produces a patent-pending, plastic-free foam with a low or negative carbon footprint that replaces conventional plastic foams in packaging and insulation. The company estimates nearly a kilogram of CO2 is removed per kilogram of foam produced. At end of life the natural polymer composts away, leaving biochar that keeps carbon sequestered for generations while enriching soil.

name: Carbon Centric
tech_note: Develops, owns and operates amine-based carbon capture plants on biogenic flue gas from waste-to-energy and bioenergy sites in Norway, liquefying and sending CO2 to permanent geological storage.
description: Carbon Centric, established in 2021, develops, builds and operates carbon capture plants for industry and the energy sector, aiming to make carbon capture scalable for small and medium-sized emission sources in Norway and the Nordic region. Its Rakkestad plant at Østfold Energi's waste-to-energy facility began operations in September 2025 as a CCU demonstrator, while its flagship BECCS project at Kirkenær with Solør Bioenergi targets ~32,000 t/yr of biogenic CO2 removal and has completed the Puro.earth Preliminary Assessment, backed by a long-term offtake agreement with DNV.

name: Carbon Collect
tech_note: Carbon Collect develops the MechanicalTree™, a passive direct air capture (PDAC) system using vertically stacked sorbent disks and low-temperature vacuum-steam regeneration (~85°C), based on Klaus Lackner's ASU research.
description: Carbon Collect, formerly Silicon Kingdom Holdings Limited, specializes in carbon capture technology and offers the MechanicalTree, a passive, scalable system designed to capture CO₂ from ambient air without energy-intensive processes; it was founded in 2018 and is based in Dublin, Ireland. In 2025, Carbon Collect installed its Gen-II MechanicalTree™, which doubles CO₂ capture per cycle and uses lightweight, non-metallic, recyclable materials.

name: Carbon Containment Lab
tech_note: A 501(c)(3) research nonprofit that designs, tests, and supports pilots of novel carbon containment methods (BiCRS, mineralization, refrigerant abatement, methane measurement) but does not itself develop credit projects or operate removal facilities.
description: Carbon Containment Lab is a 501(c)(3) climate nonprofit supporting the design, testing, and implementation of novel and neglected climate solutions, working to bring research from laboratories into pilot and commercialization across anthropogenic, biologic, and geologic emissions pathways including BiCRS, carbon mineralization, fluorocarbon recovery, and low-concentration methane measurement. CC Lab is explicitly not a carbon credit registry, validator, verifier, or project developer, engaging market stakeholders only as an independent nonprofit without financial interest. It spun out of the Yale School of the Environment in early 2024 to operate as an independent nonprofit.

name: Carbon Cycle
tech_note: Pyrolysis of locally-sourced untreated wood chips into biochar (Pflanzenkohle) for soil amendment, animal feed, and concrete additive applications.
description: Carbon Cycle GmbH & Co. KG is a German biochar producer based in Rieden, Bavaria, producing Pflanzenkohle from PEFC-certified untreated wood chips via pyrolysis for agricultural soil improvement and animal feed applications. The company is EBC-certified and Puro.earth-listed (CORC 100+), with biochar production starting in 2019 and a larger second production system commissioned in 2023. They export to Norway and Switzerland and are exploring biochar-in-concrete pilots and district heating networks.

name: Carbon Direct
tech_note: Science-led carbon management advisory and software platform providing supplier due diligence, procurement, portfolio construction, and emissions accounting for corporate and government buyers of carbon removals.
description: Carbon Direct is a US-based carbon management firm combining a science advisory team with software to help large buyers procure, verify, and monitor high-quality carbon removal and reduction credits. It does not physically remove CO2 itself but sits in the CDR ecosystem as a broker/advisor/diligence provider, working with Fortune 500 clients including Microsoft, Shopify, and Alaska Airlines. A sister firm, Carbon Direct Capital, invests growth equity in carbon management technologies.

name: Carbon Drawdown Initiative
tech_note: Philanthropic funder and research operator running enhanced rock weathering (basalt/dunite on agricultural fields) field experiments and investing in early-stage CDR startups.
description: Carbon Drawdown Initiative is a German (GmbH), philanthropically-funded organization founded in 2019 by Dirk Paessler that supports the emerging CDR industry through early-stage investments in 30+ CDR startups, scientific research partnerships, and policy work. They also run "Project Carbdown," a field research program on enhanced rock weathering in partnership with universities and institutes across Europe. Their primary role is as a CDR ecosystem funder/research organization rather than a commercial removal supplier.

name: Carbon Energy
tech_note: Electrochemical direct air capture pilot that co-produces sodium carbonate (soda ash) alongside atmospheric CO2 removal.
description: Carbon Energy (CarbonEnergy Inc.) is a seed-stage Daegu, South Korea-based DAC startup founded in 2022. It is piloting an electrochemical direct air capture process that simultaneously produces renewable energy/soda ash while removing CO2, with plans to scale and either sequester or recycle the captured CO2. Small team (~4-10 employees).

name: Carbon Engineering/Occidental Petroleum
tech_note: Liquid-solvent (KOH/Ca(OH)2) Direct Air Capture technology deployed at megaton scale via Oxy's 1PointFive subsidiary, with the STRATOS plant in West Texas as the flagship commercial facility.
description: Carbon Engineering is a Squamish, BC-based DAC technology developer that became a wholly owned subsidiary of Occidental's Oxy Low Carbon Ventures in 2023 after a $1.1B acquisition. Its liquid-solvent DAC technology powers 1PointFive's STRATOS plant in West Texas (expected startup mid-2026) and the South Texas DAC Hub, with Occidental targeting ~100 DAC plants by 2035.

name: Carbon Gap
tech_note: Carbon Gap is a UK-registered non-profit advocacy and research NGO focused on advancing EU policy to scale carbon dioxide removal; it produces policy analysis, a CDR Policy Tracker, and country readiness assessments.
description: Carbon Gap is Europe's leading carbon dioxide removal (CDR) advocacy and research NGO, based in the UK and focused on shaping EU policy frameworks to enable the scale-up of permanent carbon removal. Carbon Gap LTD is a registered charity (charity number 1200562) and a private company limited by guarantee, registered in England and Wales. It does not itself remove CO2 — it produces policy briefs, a Policy Tracker, the CARE Calculator, and country readiness assessments to guide European decision-makers.

name: Carbon Gold
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis and sells enriched biochar-based composts, fertilisers, soil improvers and tree care products for agricultural and horticultural applications.
description: Carbon Gold was founded in 2007 by Craig Sams, founder of Green & Blacks Chocolate, and Dan Morrell, founder of the Carbon Neutral Company. The UK-based B Corp produces enriched biochar products (composts, fertilisers, soil improvers, tree care) that sequester carbon in soil while improving plant health. Retail products have moved to Marshalls Garden, while the company continues trade sales directly.

name: Carbon Hill
tech_note: Family-run biochar producer using proprietary low-emission pyrolysis systems to convert underutilized biomass (hedgerow trimmings, green waste) into biochar, certified under Puro.earth.
description: Carbon Hill is a family-run biochar producer at Caebardd farm near Welshpool in mid-Wales, UK, operated by the Jones family alongside their Woodtek engineering arm. It produces biochar from locally sourced biomass such as hedgerow trimmings and municipal green waste using in-house pyrolysis systems, and is expanding via Biodynamic Carbon Ltd — a joint venture with Shropshire Council and Onnu — which aims to be the UK's largest biochar facility.

name: Carbon Impact
tech_note: Carbon Impact is a French CDR project developer that retrofits biomass and biomethane plants with CO2 capture, liquefaction, and offshore geological sequestration (partnering with South Pole and Airfix) to generate BECCS carbon removal credits.
description: Carbon Impact is a French carbon removal project developer, cofounded by energy experts, that leads the implementation of CO2 capture infrastructure in partnership with local biomethane unit owners. Together with South Pole and Airfix, the company is launching France's first biogas-based BECCS project near Nancy, with captured CO2 liquefied on-site and transported to Norway for subsea storage under the North Sea.

name: Carbon Instead
tech_note: Produces pyrolysis-derived biochar from biogenic waste and functionalizes it as an additive/replacement for cement and sand in concrete and mortar, creating durable carbon storage in the built environment.
description: Carbon Instead is a Berlin-based startup (founded 2020) that produces a biochar-based additive for construction materials like concrete and mortar, made via pyrolysis of biogenic waste streams. The biochar partially replaces cement and sand, turning building materials into long-term carbon stores. They operate across the value chain from biomass sourcing to carbonization technology to application.

name: Carbon Kapture
tech_note: Cultivates sugar kelp on rope farms, harvests and dries it, and pyrolyzes the seaweed into biochar that is applied to agricultural soil for carbon sequestration.
description: Carbon Kapture is a UK-based CDR supplier that grows kelp (sugar kelp) on rope farms in partnership with shellfish farmers across Europe, then pyrolyzes the harvested seaweed into biochar that is applied to farmland. As of 2025 the company had expanded from its first Mulroy Bay (Ireland) farm to around a dozen farms across Ireland, UK, France, Spain and Portugal, and was scouting additional sites in Singapore, Newfoundland and the Seychelles.

name: Carbon Lockdown
tech_note: Carbon Lockdown buries sustainably-sourced coarse woody biomass in engineered underground "Wood Vaults" capped with low-permeability clay to create anoxic conditions that prevent decomposition for 1,000+ years.
description: Carbon Lockdown Project is a US public benefit corporation spun out of University of Maryland research by Dr. Ning Zeng, developing wood-vault biomass burial for durable carbon removal. Its flagship 5,000 tCO2e Potomac Project is considered the world's first commercial-scale wood vault, with CORC credits issued under the Puro.earth Terrestrial Storage of Biomass methodology, and the company has delivered tonnes to buyers including Kinnevik via Climate Vault.

name: Carbon Neutral Initiative
tech_note: CNI deploys olivine/silicate-enriched substrates in urban green (sedum) roofs to drive Enhanced Rock Weathering, producing durable CO2 removal via bicarbonate formation.
description: Carbon Neutral Initiative develops green roofs that remove CO2 through the addition of olivine, expecting net removal of 1,804 tonnes of CO2 over 25 years from its flagship project. The Netherlands-based company runs the Carbon Green Roof project as part of its bio-enhanced silicate weathering programme and collaborates with TNO, Utrecht University, Hasselt University, and Spanish universities. It is also initiating similar Enhanced Weathering projects in Suriname and Spain using other suitable rock types beyond olivine.

name: Carbon Plus
tech_note: Carbon Plus converts biomass waste (bamboo, palm kernel shell) into biochar, wood vinegar, and bio-oil via high-temperature (>850°C) gasification, issuing CORCs under the Puro.earth methodology.
description: Carbon Plus is a Malaysia-based biochar project developer that operates the Bukit Selar Carbon Station in Kelantan — described as Malaysia's first industrial biochar facility — through its subsidiary Carbon Zero. The demo plant has a nameplate capacity of 500 tonnes of biochar and ~1,200 tCO2e removed annually, with dMRV provided by CrystalTrade and credits issued under the Puro.earth standard.

name: Carbon Reform
tech_note: Decentralized direct air capture via HVAC-retrofit "Carbon Capsule" units that remove CO2 from indoor air in commercial buildings and mineralize it on-site into limestone for reuse in construction materials.
description: Carbon Reform is a Philadelphia/Wilmington-based climate tech startup (founded 2020) that retrofits commercial building HVAC systems with modular hardware that captures indoor CO2 and contaminants while lowering ventilation energy use. Captured CO2 is mineralized on-site into limestone byproduct for use in concrete and paint. The company raised a $5.5M seed-plus round in January 2025 (bringing total to ~$9M) and has active customer deployments with utilities such as Baltimore Gas & Electric and New Jersey Natural Gas.

name: Carbon Removal AS/Nordic DAC Group
tech_note: Project developer deploying Phlair's electrochemical pH-swing liquid-solvent DAC technology at Kollsnes, Norway, with captured CO2 piped to Northern Lights for offshore geological storage.
description: Carbon Removal AS is a Norwegian project development company developing a large-scale Direct Air Capture facility at Kollsnes in Øygarden, adjacent to the Northern Lights CO2 storage terminal. In July 2025, via subsidiary NorDAC Kollsnes AS, it signed an agreement with German DAC technology provider Phlair to deploy an electrochemical liquid-solvent DAC plant targeting 60,000 tpa initially and scaling to 500,000 tpa. Nordic DAC Group AB is a Swedish affiliate/minority shareholder that sells the resulting removal certificates.

name: Carbon Remove
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of biomass for soil application and carbon removal credit generation in Brazil.
description: Carbon Remove is a small Brazilian biochar producer based in Anhembi, São Paulo state, founded and led by Thomas Britze. The company produces biochar from biomass via pyrolysis to generate carbon removal credits while providing soil fertility benefits for Brazilian agriculture.

name: Carbon Sequestration Inc
tech_note: Buries woody biomass debris in engineered, clay-capped underground vaults excavated within the Lissie Formation in Texas to permanently sequester carbon, with secondary biochar production.
description: Carbon Sequestration Inc. offers carbon removal methods including wood vaulting, biochar production, and carbon farming, founded by CEO Christopher Knop who began experimenting with biomass burial in the mid-2010s. Each vault is excavated within the low-permeability clays of the Lissie Formation, where woody debris is stacked and compacted, then sealed with a 6–12 foot compacted clay cap to create an oxygen-limited barrier. The project is described as compliant with TCEQ, Puro.earth, and ICROA/ICVCM standards.

name: Carbon Square
tech_note: Carbon Square (CarbonSQR) is developing a liquid-solvent Direct Air Capture facility, planning India's first pilot DAC plant near Hyderabad, selling DAC-based carbon removal credits.
description: Carbon Square specializes in carbon removal and reuse strategies aiming to sequester carbon permanently or repurpose it for beneficial applications, and markets itself as delivering affordable Direct Air Capture credits. CarbonSQR is planning India's first pilot DAC facility near Hyderabad, expected to capture up to 8 tonnes of CO₂ per day. The company is an early-stage Indian DAC supplier.

name: Carbon Time
tech_note: Carbon Time develops Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) approaches — primarily olivine-based rock weathering and electrochemical alkalinization — to increase seawater alkalinity and sequester atmospheric CO2 as dissolved inorganic carbon.
description: Carbon Time is a Paris, France–based company founded in 2021 that operates as a developer of ocean alkalinity enhancement for carbon dioxide removal. Its initial focus is alkalinization via rock weathering using olivine, alongside electrochemical approaches compatible with coastal industries like desalination or water treatment. The company was financed by the Team for the Planet citizen-investor movement.

name: Carbon To Stone
tech_note: Reactive crystallization process that combines CO2 (from air or point-source) with alkaline industrial residues (steel slag, fly ash, mine tailings) to form solid carbonates while recovering energy-critical metals.
description: Carbon To Stone is a Cornell University spinout developing a low-energy carbon mineralization technology that couples CO2 capture with reactive crystallization using alkaline industrial waste streams. The process produces solid carbonates for construction use and recovers valuable metals (Li, Co, Ni, Mg, etc.) as co-products, targeting hard-to-abate sectors like iron and steel.

name: Carbon Universe
tech_note: Develops carbon-negative concrete prefabrication via CO2 mineralization, plus CO2 capture reactors and air filtration products.
description: Carbon Universe Sp. z o.o. is a small Polish carbontech firm based in Elbląg that produces architectural and structural concrete using CO2-mineralization technology, alongside CO2 capture reactors and particulate air filters. Their CDR-relevant activity is permanent CO2 binding in concrete products. No registry credits or delivery evidence found, and public footprint is limited.

name: Carbon to Sea Initiative
tech_note: Non-profit philanthropic funder and convener supporting scientific research, field trials, MRV development, and policy advocacy for ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE).
description: Carbon to Sea Initiative is a non-profit philanthropic program (a project of the Windward Fund) dedicated to advancing ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) research through grant-making, field research network-building, policy advocacy, and convening. It is the largest philanthropic funder in the OAE space but does not itself remove CO2 or sell credits. It sits squarely in the CDR ecosystem as a funder, field-builder, and policy advocate.

name: Carbon180
tech_note: Nonprofit policy advocacy think tank focused on advancing U.S. federal policies, funding, and environmental justice frameworks for carbon dioxide removal across DAC, soil carbon, and other pathways.
description: Carbon180 is a nonprofit environmental organization headquartered in Washington, D.C., co-founded in 2015 by Giana Amador and Noah Deich at UC Berkeley (formerly known as Center for Carbon Removal). Its main activities include federal policy advocacy, the New Carbon Economy Consortium, and the Leading with Soil Initiative, and it publishes fact sheets and deep dives on various carbon removal approaches. CDR is its entire mission, making it part of the CDR ecosystem rather than a physical supplier.

name: Carbon2H
tech_note: Carbon2H designs and sells modular, container-mounted biomass gasifiers that convert organic residues into syngas/electricity and biochar as a carbon-sequestering byproduct.
description: Based in Berlin, Germany, Carbon2H specializes in advanced biomass gasification systems, converting biomass into clean syngas using modular, customizable gasifiers housed in shipping containers for easy deployment and scalability. Their mobile biomass gasification systems convert waste into renewable energy and biochar, which enhances soil health and sequesters carbon. They sell equipment rather than directly operating removal facilities, but their technology enables biochar-based CDR.

name: CarbonBlue
tech_note: Extracts dissolved CO2 from seawater/brackish water using a fluidized-bed reactor that precipitates CO2 into solid calcium carbonate via calcium hydroxide, integrated into desalination plants.
description: CarbonBlue is an Israeli climate-tech startup (founded 2022, based in Haifa/Tel Aviv) that develops water-based direct CO2 removal technology using a proprietary calcium-looping reactor to mineralize dissolved CO2 into calcium carbonate. In May 2025 it deployed its "Midway" pilot integrated into the Ma'agan Michael desalination plant, targeting 40 tCO2/yr in Phase 1 scaling to 400 tCO2/yr in Phase 2. Backed by Frontier and a $10M seed round (2024).

name: CarbonBuilt
tech_note: CarbonBuilt retrofits concrete masonry plants with its Reversa® binder process that replaces most Portland cement with low-carbon industrial byproducts and cures blocks by mineralizing CO2 (including biogenic/DAC sources) into permanent calcium carbonate.
description: CarbonBuilt is a Torrance, California company that produces ultra-low-carbon concrete masonry units using its proprietary Reversa® binder, which replaces up to 50% of Portland cement with upcycled industrial byproducts and chemically mineralizes CO2 during the curing process for permanent storage. It won the NRG COSIA Carbon XPRIZE, has a commercial deployment at Blair Block in Alabama using biogenic CO2 from forestry waste, and sold carbon removal credits to Stripe Climate. In 2024 the company announced a scale-up partnership with Meta.

name: CarbonCapture Inc.
tech_note: CarbonCapture Inc. develops modular solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture systems (Leo Series) that filter CO2 from the atmosphere for permanent underground storage.
description: CarbonCapture's DAC systems use solid sorbents that soak up atmospheric CO2 when cooled and release it when heated, capturing CO2 from the air and permanently storing it underground. Through its Canadian subsidiary True North Carbon, the company is deploying Project Tamarack at Deep Sky Alpha in Alberta, designed to remove up to 2,000 tonnes of CO2 annually, which achieved "First Capture" on October 22, 2025.

name: CarbonChip
tech_note: Operates a Tigercat 6050 mobile pyrolysis unit that converts eucalyptus and pine forestry residues into biochar in situ at Queensland plantations, generating Puro.earth-certified carbon removal credits.
description: Carbonchip is a Brisbane-based biochar manufacturer established in 2020 that processes sustainable forestry residue through a mobile pyrolysis machine to produce biochar for Queensland farms and larger national projects. The Carbonchip Mobile Carboniser Project uses a Tigercat 6050 mobile pyrolysis unit to process eucalyptus and pine residues from Queensland plantations in situ under Puro.earth's Biochar Methodology. As one of Biocare's earliest issued CDR projects (2023), Carbonchip has issued 579 carbon removal credits.

name: CarbonCure
tech_note: Injects captured CO2 into fresh concrete and reclaimed wash water where it reacts with calcium to form permanently embedded calcium carbonate minerals, with a Verra-approved methodology; supports both industrial-sourced CCU and atmospheric (DAC-sourced) permanent CO2 storage.
description: CarbonCure Technologies, headquartered in Halifax, Canada, licenses carbon mineralization systems that inject CO2 into ready-mix concrete, precast concrete, and reclaimed wash water at concrete plants. While primarily marketed as a carbon utilization solution, the company partners with DAC providers like Heirloom to deliver verified atmospheric CO2 removal via permanent mineralization, and has a Verra-verified methodology generating carbon credits.

name: CarbonFields
tech_note: Pyrolysis of biomass waste (wood waste and agricultural residues) into biochar for soil amendment and industrial bioproducts.
description: Carbon Fields is a Spain-based biochar producer that transforms biomass waste (e.g. wood waste) into biochar and sustainable bioproducts for agriculture and industry. The company physically removes CO2 via pyrolysis and markets carbon-negative soil amendments and biochar-based products. Team members (e.g. Eric Suñol, Yann Mercier) are publicly active on LinkedIn through late 2025.

name: CarbonMeld
tech_note: Automated LLM-based pipeline that scores carbon credit projects across registries and marketplaces on integrity, transparency, claim safety, and documentation quality.
description: CarbonMeld provides quality scores for 650+ carbon credit projects across 9 marketplaces, with daily updates on integrity, transparency, and claim safety. It applies a standardized evaluation pipeline to public documents from registries such as Verra, Gold Standard, CDM, and CORSIA, using an LLM-based system to evaluate four dimensions: registry integrity, transparency, claim safety, and documentation quality. CarbonMeld is not a marketplace but an independent analysis tool used before negotiation to screen projects.

name: CarbonRun
tech_note: Adds powdered limestone to acidified rivers (River Alkalinity Enhancement), converting CO2 into bicarbonate that is transported to the ocean for long-term storage.
description: CarbonRun is a Nova Scotia-based CDR supplier that deploys River Alkalinity Enhancement (RAE), adding finely ground limestone to rivers to reduce acidity, restore fish habitat, and permanently sequester CO2 as bicarbonate delivered to the ocean. In January 2026 the company issued the world's first Isometric-certified RAE credits (76 tonnes from its Kvina River project in Norway), delivered under a $25.4M Frontier offtake covering ~55,442 tonnes between 2025-2029.

name: CarbonZero
tech_note: Pyrolysis of almond shell agricultural waste into biochar, applied to farmland soils for long-term carbon storage and soil improvement.
description: CarbonZero.Eco is a Silicon Valley-based biochar startup founded by Harper Moss that converts California almond shells into biochar via pyrolysis, partnering with almond growers in Colusa and Yolo Counties. In December 2025 it commissioned its first commercial biochar facility in Colusa County and announced a carbon removal credit purchase agreement with Climeworks. The company is registered as a biochar supplier on the Puro.earth registry.

name: Carbonaide
tech_note: Carbonaide mineralizes biogenic/captured CO₂ into precast concrete via ex-situ carbonation curing, permanently storing ~100 kg CO₂ per m³ of concrete.
description: Carbonaide is a Finnish spin-out from VTT Technical Research Centre that enables manufacturing of carbon-negative concrete. It uses ex-situ mineralization based on carbonation, where calcium ions from cement react with biogenic CO₂ during curing to form stable carbonate minerals for permanent storage. Carbon removals are certified by Isometric, enabling verified durable carbon removal credits.

name: Carbonapp
tech_note: Carbonapp is a French mission-driven carbon project developer/mandataire that helps third-party project owners (biochar producers, foresters, farmers, construction firms) structure and certify credits under Label Bas-Carbone, Puro.earth, Riverse and CSI standards.
description: Carbonapp is a France-based multi-sectoral carbon project developer and offset platform founded in 2020, operating as a mandated developer (mandataire) that sources projects and shepherds them through certification under standards such as Label Bas-Carbone, Puro.earth, Riverse and CSI. It does not itself produce biochar or physically remove CO2; its sister company DEMIO produces biochar, while Carbonapp structures and markets the resulting credits to corporate buyers. It sits in the CDR ecosystem as a developer/intermediary rather than a supplier of removals.

name: Carbonaught
tech_note: Applies finely crushed basalt (often sourced from quarry waste) to agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering, delivering permanent CO2 removal alongside soil-health benefits for farmers.
description: Carbonaught is a Brisbane-based startup founded by former mining professionals Andrew Pedley, James Lyons and Rhys Heffernan to turn mining waste into a farm input that delivers measurable carbon removal. Its enhanced rock weathering technology is deployed in trials across Queensland, New South Wales, Western Australia and California, with initial focus on sugarcane and expansion into horticulture, grains, cotton, beef, dairy and rice. The company is also developing a digital platform connecting quarry operators, farmers and carbon credit buyers, with GPS-based application tracking and carbon-removal verification.

name: Carbonauten
tech_note: Carbonauten uses a proprietary modular batch retort pyrolysis system to convert woody biomass residues into biochar, pyrolysis oils and renewable heat, embedding the biochar into plastic compounds and building materials for long-term carbon storage.
description: Carbonauten GmbH is a German biochar producer based in Giengen an der Brenz that operates the "Minus CO2 Factory" in Eberswalde (~3,000 tonnes biochar/year) and is building a larger plant in Chibi, China, designed to process 100,000 tonnes of bamboo annually. The company produces technical biocarbons, pyrolysis oils and renewable energy, and locks biochar into CO2-negative plastic granulates used by partners such as Deutsche Bahn and Arburg.

name: Carbondrop
tech_note: Applies micronized basalt in hydrogel pellets to agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering and sequester CO2 as bicarbonate/carbonate.
description: Carbondrop is a Vienna, Austria-based climate-tech startup developing enhanced rock weathering (ERW) for carbon removal. They produce a carbon-removing fertilizer made of micronized basalt in hydrogel-based pellets that can be spread on cropland with standard farm equipment, providing soil nutrients and pH buffering alongside CO2 sequestration. The company is very small (≈2 employees) and early-stage, with no registry-issued credits yet, but the website is live and technically detailed.

name: Carboneers
tech_note: Carboneers develops decentralized biochar projects with smallholder farmers in the Global South, converting agricultural biomass waste (rice, cotton, maize, cocoa residues) into biochar via small-scale pyrolysis kilns.
description: Carboneers works with farming communities across the Global South to develop biochar and carbon sequestration projects, with a mission to remove 1 million tons of CO2 by 2028. The company (originally Dutch Carboneers) operates projects in India and Ghana, and is listed as a supplier on Isometric with a buffer pool for reversal protection, partnering with Terrafront Ventures and Together for Restoration.

name: Carboneyes
tech_note: Carbonises waste sugarcane bagasse via pyrolysis into biochar, which is donated to smallholder sugarcane farmers for soil application, generating durable carbon removal credits.
description: Carboneyes is a UK-based biochar carbon removal project developer that converts waste bagasse from sugarcane processing into biochar and donates it to smallholder sugarcane farmers, generating carbon credits from the resulting soil carbon storage. The company states it aims to remove over 500,000 tonnes of CO2 and donate over 200,000 tonnes of biochar by 2030.

name: Carbonfuture
tech_note: Carbonfuture operates a digital MRV+ platform and marketplace that connects durable CDR suppliers (biochar, BECCS, DAC, mineralization) with corporate buyers, handling certification, tracking, and credit sales.
description: Carbonfuture is the Trust Infrastructure for durable carbon removal, centered on Carbonfuture MRV+, a fully integrated, end-to-end solution for monitoring, reporting, and verification of carbon removal projects. They operate as a marketplace/broker rather than a physical remover, aggregating supply from biochar, BECCS, DACCS, and mineralization projects across five continents. Clients include Microsoft, Swiss Re, Boeing, and the WEF First Movers Coalition.

name: Carboniferous
tech_note: Carboniferous develops Marine Anoxic Carbon Storage (MACS), sequestering densified terrestrial crop residues (e.g., sugarcane bagasse) in deep hypersaline anoxic brine pools like the Orca Basin in the Gulf of Mexico for long-term carbon preservation.
description: Carboniferous is a U.S. CDR startup pioneering Marine Anoxic Carbon Storage, which places terrestrial biomass bales in oxygen-free deep ocean brine basins where decomposition is inhibited for thousands of years. The company applied for an EPA MPRSA research permit in 2024 for a 20-tonne field test in the Orca Basin, which advanced to public comment in 2025. It is aligned with the Puro.earth MACS methodology released in early 2025.

name: Carbonified
tech_note: Small Canadian carbon project developer focused on biochar, regenerative agriculture, and afforestation/reforestation/revegetation (ARR) carbon removal projects.
description: Carbonified is a Canadian company providing high-integrity carbon solutions aimed at reversing climate change with measurable impact. They focus on biochar, regenerative agriculture, and ARR as scalable carbon sequestration solutions. They are a small (~3 employees) project developer listed in Carbon Removal Canada's directory.

name: Carbonis
tech_note: Carbonis operates two PYREG P500 pyrolysis plants to produce certified biochar from regional hardwood/softwood forest chips for animal feed, biogas, soil improvement, and industrial applications.
description: Carbonis GmbH & Co. KG is a German biochar producer based in Garrel, Lower Saxony, founded in 2016 as part of the Voßmann agricultural group. The company produces GMP+ certified biochar via dry pyrolysis and sells it across agricultural, livestock, biogas, and industrial segments, with the agricultural application delivering durable carbon storage.

name: Carbonity
tech_note: Carbonity operates an industrial-scale biochar plant in Port-Cartier, Quebec that pyrolyzes forestry residues using Airex Energy's DryFX and CarbonFX technologies to produce biochar for soil, construction, and carbon sequestration applications.
description: Carbonity is a joint venture between Airex Energy, Groupe Rémabec, and SUEZ that inaugurated Canada's first industrial-scale biochar plant in Port-Cartier in May 2025, starting at 10,000 tonnes/year and planning to triple capacity by 2026 to become the largest such facility in North America. Carbonity generates certified carbon credits offered on the voluntary market via First Climate and has secured a deal with Microsoft to purchase 36,000 credits over the first three years of operations.

name: Carbonloop
tech_note: Deploys on-site modular biomass thermolysis (HYNOCA, Haffner Energy) to co-produce renewable hydrogen/syngas and biochar, with the biochar serving as the permanent carbon sink.
description: Carbonloop is a French startup (launched 2021, part of the Kouros Group) that offers industrial customers turnkey on-site biomass pyrolysis units producing renewable hydrogen/syngas and biochar, using Haffner Energy's HYNOCA technology. The biochar co-product is sold to the agricultural sector and generates carbon removal credits, while the renewable gas/hydrogen substitutes for fossil fuels in industry and heavy mobility.

name: Carbono Capital
tech_note: Chilean company producing biochar from biomass pyrolysis for soil amendment, compost, and durable carbon removal credits.
description: Carbono Capital SpA is a Chile-based biochar producer whose website emphasizes soil enrichment, carbon sequestration, and promoting healthier ecosystems through biochar. The company operates as a CDR supplier producing biochar-based compost and carbon credits, though public activity signals and news coverage are limited.

name: Carbons Finland
tech_note: Produces biochar via low-oxygen pyrolysis of Finnish wood (particularly willow) for applications in stormwater filtration, landscaping substrates, and organic agriculture.
description: Carbons Finland Oy is a production company of biochar-based products located in Kouvola, Finland, selling products under the Carbons brand, with focus on urban green spaces as well as filtration and decontamination. The company was founded in 2014 to develop biochar solutions for stormwater treatment, landscaping, composting, nutrient recycling and organic farming. They are registered as a biochar supplier on Puro.earth.

name: Carbonsate
tech_note: Carbonsate selectively harvests encroaching bush biomass and stores it in engineered oxygen-limited dry underground pits to prevent decomposition, issuing Puro.earth-certified CORCs under the Terrestrial Storage of Biomass methodology.
description: Berlin-based Carbonsate (founded 2023) is a carbon removal supplier operating biomass storage projects in Namibia, Cameroon, Colombia, and Bulgaria. Its flagship Otjiwarongo Project in Namibia harvests invasive bush biomass and stores it in engineered oxygen-free pits, and the company issued its first 799 Puro.earth-certified credits in January 2026 as the 100th certified facility on the Puro Registry.

name: Carbonway
tech_note: Tech-agnostic project developer capturing biogenic CO2 from biomethane plants and mineralizing it into construction materials (bottom ash, recycled concrete aggregates, industrial waste) for permanent storage.
