description: Carbonway is a France-based CDR project developer that captures biogenic CO2 from biomethanization plants and mineralizes it in construction and backfill materials such as bottom ash and construction debris. They describe themselves as the first tech-agnostic project developer in the space, building local industrial hubs and licensing mineralization technologies rather than owning a proprietary process.

name: Carbony
tech_note: Carbony deploys Enhanced Rock Weathering by spreading finely ground silicate rock on managed forest land in Central and Eastern Europe to accelerate natural mineral weathering and sequester CO2.
description: Carbony is an Austria-based CDR project developer focused on Enhanced Rock Weathering, uniquely targeting managed forests in Central and Eastern Europe rather than cropland. The company is a member of the Enhanced Weathering Alliance and has corporate partnerships (e.g., Refurbed). Live website and active LinkedIn presence confirm operational status.

name: Carborok
tech_note: Carborok develops industrial reactors that mineralize biogenic CO2 into recycled concrete, ashes, and alkaline industrial wastes for permanent sequestration.
description: Carborok is a Nantes-based French startup, a spin-off of engineering firm Voltigital, founded in 2021. It designs, builds and operates CO2 mineralization units that sequester biogenic CO2 in recycled concrete and alkaline industrial wastes, and also sells reactors and licenses. The company runs a pilot reactor at Chauvé (Ocaapi project) backed by France2030 and GRDF's bioCO2 sequestration call.

name: Carbuna
tech_note: Carbuna AG processes and refines biochar sourced from EBC-certified producers into soil, agricultural, and building-material products, and sells biochar carbon removal (BCR) credits via Carbonfuture.
description: Carbuna AG is a Germany-based company founded in 2015 that focuses on the processing and sale of biochar in various forms and products, active in several European countries, positioning itself as a platform that links biochar production and demand. It is one of the pioneering companies trading biochar-based carbon removal certificates, working closely with MRV provider Carbonfuture, and voluntary-market BCR certificates have become a major driver of its growth.

name: Carbyon
tech_note: Fast-swing sorbent-based DAC using thin-film sorbents that saturate in ~90 seconds, deployed in small modular units designed for mass manufacturing.
description: Carbyon is a Dutch deep-tech startup (TNO spin-off, founded 2019) developing a "fast swing" direct air capture technology that uses thin-film sorbents to capture CO2 in seconds rather than hours. The company unveiled its Carbyon GO outdoor demonstrator at High Tech Campus Eindhoven in September 2025 and raised a €15.3M Series A in 2025, positioning itself as a modular DAC equipment supplier targeting ~€100/tonne.

name: Cardinal Ethanol
tech_note: Corn ethanol producer hosting a CCS project that captures fermentation CO2 and injects it into a Class VI well for permanent geologic storage via the One Carbon Partnership JV with Vault 44.01.
description: Cardinal Ethanol and Vault 44.01 formed a 50/50 joint venture, One Carbon Partnership, LP, to design, implement, and operate a CO2 capture and sequestration project at Cardinal's ethanol facility near Union City, Indiana. In March 2026 EPA issued the Class VI permit allowing One Carbon Partnership to inject up to 450,000 metric tons of CO2 per year for 30 years (13.5 million tons total) at the Cardinal Ethanol facility. The biogenic fermentation CO2 from corn ethanol production, paired with permanent underground storage, qualifies the operation as BECCS.

name: CarpeCarbon
tech_note: Develops a proprietary energy-efficient Direct Air Capture system that avoids the high energy demands and critical-raw-material dependencies of traditional DAC, targeting permanent geologic storage or utilization of captured CO2.
description: CarpeCarbon is a Turin-based Italian climate-tech startup founded in 2022 that is developing a proprietary, energy-efficient Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology, positioned as the first Italian DAC company. They raised a €1.75M pre-seed round in 2023 from Tech4Planet (CDP Venture Capital), 360 Capital, Club degli Investitori and PiemonteNext to design Italy's first domestically-developed DAC plant in Piedmont.

name: Cascade Climate
tech_note: Nonprofit coordinating science, standards (Community Quantification Standard), policy, and digital tools to accelerate enhanced rock weathering and other open-system CDR pathways.
description: Cascade Climate is a philanthropically-backed US-based nonprofit (launched June 2023) that accelerates open-system CDR pathways, with an initial focus on enhanced rock weathering (ERW). It does not remove CO2 itself — instead it runs market-shaping initiatives, develops a Community Quantification Standard, builds tools like the Weathering Potential Explorer and ERW-MAC, and drives science and policy coordination across the ERW field.

name: Catch 23
tech_note: Nordic broker/retailer that sells Carbon Removal Certificates (CRCs) from Stockholm Exergi's planned BECCS facility in Värtan, Stockholm.
description: Catch 23 was founded in 2020 as a Nordic retailer of captured carbon dioxide, working on the brokerage of captured carbon dioxide and communication about the benefits of carbon capture. The company sells CRC (Carbon Removal Certificate) credits for negative emissions from Stockholm Exergi's planned BECCS facility in Värtan, Stockholm, targeting Nordic corporate customers. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves but operate as a sales channel for Stockholm Exergi's removals.

name: Ceal
tech_note: Ceal uses an electrochemical process applied to seawater at the intake/outfall of seawater-cooled thermal power plants to crystallize dissolved calcium and carbon into precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC), simultaneously reducing scale/biofouling and producing a sellable mineral.
description: Ceal was founded in April 2024 after receiving a grant under Israel's "Blue Economy" Program, and its technology is built on an electrochemical mineralization process that applies a gentle electric current to seawater to crystallize dissolved calcium and carbon as calcium carbonate, yielding precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) used in paints, plastics, paper, pharmaceuticals, and food. The company was co-founded by Mati Shani with Prof. Charlotte Vogt of the Technion, whose lab produced the scientific foundation. Its roadmap starts with a pilot project with the Israel Electric Corporation. Note: because the captured CO2 is sold as an industrial mineral rather than permanently buried, there is some CCU ambiguity, but the company self-identifies as a CDR firm and claims permanent sequestration of CO2 in calcium carbonate.

name: Ceezer
tech_note: Digital enterprise platform and B2B marketplace for sourcing, vetting, procuring, and managing carbon credit portfolios (including CDR pathways such as biochar, DAC, and ERW) with integrated MRV data.
description: CEEZER is a Berlin-based B2B enterprise platform and marketplace that connects corporate buyers with carbon credit project developers across removal and avoidance pathways. It provides risk assessment, MRV data integration, and portfolio-management tools rather than physically removing CO2 itself. It belongs in the CDR ecosystem as a marketplace/enabler, not as a supplier.

name: Cella Mineral Storage
tech_note: In-situ carbon mineralization via CO2 injection into basalt formations in Kenya's Rift Valley, paired with DAC partners and powered by geothermal/solar.
description: Cella Mineral Storage is a New York-based startup operating carbon mineralization storage in Kenya's Rift Valley, injecting captured CO2 into basaltic volcanic rocks for permanent sequestration. They partner with multiple DAC companies (Octavia, Sirona, RepAir, Greenlyte, Carbon Atlantis) to provide storage services and have sold credits to Frontier (Stripe/Shopify).

name: Char2Cool
tech_note: Char2Cool developed a low-cost pyrolysis kiln (C2C-Kiln) that local partners in Africa use to convert harvested invasive water hyacinths into biochar, which is then applied to depleted soils as a carbon sink and soil amendment.
description: Char2Cool e.V. is a registered German non-profit association, run by a two-person core team (Walter and Katharina) based in Reisbach, Lower Bavaria, focused on climate protection through the use of water hyacinths. They work with communities across Africa to turn the invasive weed into biochar as a permanent carbon sink, with the Char2Cool team providing know-how while local partners set up and run production and sell the biochar locally as a soil enhancer.

name: CharLine
tech_note: Produces EBC-certified biochar products (feed charcoal, manure charcoal, plant biochar) from pyrolysis of biomass, primarily for livestock and agricultural applications.
description: CharLine GmbH is an Austria-based (Riedlingsdorf, Burgenland) producer of biochar-based products, particularly feed charcoal, manure charcoal, and plant biochar for the livestock and agriculture sectors. The company works in cooperation with Sonnenerde GmbH and certifies its biochar to the European Biochar Certificate (EBC) standard. Note: the DB snapshot lists Germany, but the company is actually headquartered in Austria.

name: Charm Industrial
tech_note: Charm converts waste biomass (corn stover, forestry residues) into bio-oil via fast pyrolysis and injects it into deep EPA-regulated wells for permanent geological sequestration, with biochar as a co-product.
description: Charm Industrial is a San Francisco-based CDR supplier that uses mobile pyrolyzers to convert agricultural and forestry biomass into carbon-rich bio-oil, which is then injected underground into EPA-regulated wells where it solidifies in place. The company also produces biochar as a secondary removal pathway and has delivered carbon removal to Frontier, Google, JPMorgan, and others.

name: Chestnut Carbon
tech_note: Afforestation and improved forest management (IFM) developer planting native, biodiverse forests on marginal crop/pasture lands in the Southeastern U.S. to generate Gold Standard-verified removal credits.
description: Chestnut Carbon is a U.S. developer of nature-based carbon removal credits, founded in 2022 with support from asset manager Kimmeridge, that develops forest carbon projects on family-owned forestland and marginal crop and pastureland. The company has planted over 17 million trees across 30,000+ acres of marginal land in the Southeastern U.S., spanning states like Arkansas, Mississippi, Alabama, Louisiana, Texas and Oklahoma, and operates the largest U.S.-based afforestation project listed on the Gold Standard. It also signed a 25-year, 7 million-ton offtake with Microsoft and closed a $210M non-recourse project finance facility led by J.P. Morgan in 2025.

name: China Energy Engineering Corporation
tech_note: A CEEC subsidiary (CEEC Shanghai System Engineering) co-developed "CarbonBox" with Shanghai Jiao Tong University — a containerized sorbent-based direct air capture module producing 99% pure CO2 with ~100 tpa per module and 600 tpa total pilot capacity.
description: China Energy Engineering Corporation (CEEC / Energy China) is a Chinese state-owned power and infrastructure EPC conglomerate (~RMB 453B revenue in 2025, 115,000+ employees) whose core business is engineering, procurement and construction for power, renewables, grid and infrastructure projects. A CEEC subsidiary, together with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, developed CarbonBox, described as Asia's largest DAC module, which passed reliability testing in July 2024 with intended applications in green methanol, green aviation fuel and carbon trading. CarbonBox remains a pilot-scale R&D effort inside a much larger non-CDR parent, and the envisioned uses lean toward CCU rather than permanent removal.

name: Chooose AS
tech_note: SaaS/API platform for emissions calculation, SAF environmental-attribute management, and a marketplace of third-party carbon removal and offset credits.
description: Chooose AS is an Oslo, Norway-based climate-tech SaaS company that provides software and APIs for enterprises — particularly airlines, travel, and logistics — to manage SAF programs, calculate emissions, and access a vetted marketplace of carbon removals and offsets. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves; instead they operate as an ecosystem platform connecting SAF producers, registries (RSB, SAFc), airlines, and corporate scope-3 buyers. Founded in 2017, backed by GenZero, SOUNDWaves, Shell Ventures and Amadeus.

name: Circonomy
tech_note: Circonomy develops industrial and artisanal biochar carbon removal projects in the Global South, converting agricultural residues into biochar via pyrolysis and tracking removals with a proprietary digital MRV system.
description: Circonomy is a biochar carbon removal project developer that partners with agricultural firms to convert biomass into high-quality biochar. Since 2022, the company has developed a digital MRV tool and biochar technologies, and is growing into a network across 10 countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Credits are verified and issued under frameworks like Puro.earth and Carbon Standards International.

name: Circular Carbon
tech_note: Designs, builds, and operates industrial-scale pyrolysis plants ("CarbonHubs") that convert biomass residues (e.g. cocoa shells) into biochar plus renewable process steam for host industrial partners.
description: Circular Carbon is a Hamburg-based company founded in 2018 that operates a first-of-its-kind industrial biochar plant on the Peute site in Hamburg-Veddel, carbonizing cocoa shells from a neighbouring cocoa producer and feeding the co-produced steam back into the partner's factory. The facility is designed to deliver roughly 5,800 tCO2e/yr of carbon removal alongside ~5,000 t/yr of fossil-gas displacement, and the company generates CDR credits from its CarbonHubs while selling certified biochar for soil, animal feed, and industrial uses.

name: Circular Carbon Pathways
tech_note: Biochar production from agricultural residues in Zambia, intended to generate Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) credits.
description: Circular Carbon Pathways (CCP) is a Zambia-based company that aims to produce Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) certificates through nature-based decarbonization. The website is minimal with just a tagline, and no recent press, funding, or registry-listed issuances were found. With only 1 employee on LinkedIn and no public signals of operational activity, the company appears to be very early-stage or stalled.

name: Circularity2
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of woody biomass residuals (forestry/sawmill by-products) at industrial scale for soil, water, and carbon-removal applications.
description: Circularity2 announced plans in August 2025 to construct a biochar facility in Cross City, Dixie County, Florida, producing biocarbon from woody biomass by-products such as forestry and sawmill residuals. The company positions itself as a supplier of biochar and biochar-based carbon removal credits, operating from Minneapolis, MN.

name: Clairity Technology
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC using alkali carbonate coated on ceramic honeycomb monoliths, with captured CO2 mineralized into carbonated materials/concrete for permanent storage.
description: Clairity Technology is a Los Angeles-based DAC startup founded in 2022 by Glen Meyerowitz, developing a low-cost solid-sorbent direct air capture system that produces a "good enough" ~80% pure CO2 stream rather than chasing high purity. Its Project Juniper in Nevada is undergoing validation by Isometric and expected to be among the first US-issued DAC credits. Backed by a $6.75M seed round from Lowercarbon Capital and Initialized Capital.

name: Clargreen
tech_note: Pyrolyzes agricultural waste (palm kernel shells, insect frass) into biochar, blended into a branded soil amendment/bio-fertilizer (CO₂ Savior™) for smallholder farmers in Nigeria.
description: Clargreen Technologies is a Nigeria-based climate-smart agribusiness that converts palm kernel shells and insect frass into biochar-based organic fertilizer sold to smallholder farmers. The company aims to monetize carbon removal via Verra and Puro.earth standards, and the founder is a 2025 Founder Institute alumnus actively engaging with the CDR community (e.g., AirMiners).

name: Clean Air Tech
tech_note: Clean Air Tech's patented ZAP-C³ (Zero-Air-Pollution-Carbon-Capture-Capsule) process uses water-catalyzed reaction of basic oxygen steel (BOS) slag with CO2 to form CaCO3 and carbonated recycled concrete aggregate (C-RCA) for construction use.
description: Clean Air Tech is a UK-based mineralization company that captures CO2 from emission sources and permanently sequesters it by reacting it with basic oxygen steel slag to produce calcium carbonate and carbonated aggregates for the concrete/construction industry. Their core technologies are the ZAP-C³ capsule and the ZAP-Microbubbler. Because the CO2 is captured from point sources and stored in construction materials, the activity sits at the boundary of CCS/CCU with permanent mineralization.

name: Clean Energy Systems
tech_note: CES develops proprietary oxy-fuel combustion technology (derived from rocket engine principles) that enables zero-emission power plants with full CO2 capture, deployed for BECCS (Mendota project using agricultural waste biomass) and oxy-fuel CCS for steel, oil & gas, and offshore power.
description: Clean Energy Systems (CES) is an independent California-based technology developer that commercializes oxy-fuel combustion systems for carbon-negative power and industrial decarbonization. It leads the Mendota BECCS project (converting agricultural waste biomass into syngas with ~99% CO2 capture for geologic storage) and has partnerships with PETRONAS/MISC/Aker Solutions (ZEUS offshore demo) and Metal One (green steel).

name: Clean Maine Carbon
tech_note: Operates a rotary-kiln pyrolysis facility in Greenville, Maine, converting low-value Northeastern hardwood biomass into biochar for agriculture, concrete, and remediation applications.
description: Clean Maine Carbon purchased the Greenville Steam Biomass facility in Maine in 2017 and started its first biochar facility in July 2023, transforming low-value discarded woody biomass into biochar. The company transforms locally sourced woody biomass into premium biochar, repurposing waste and sequestering carbon. It has issued biochar CORCs on the Puro.earth registry via Flowcarbon as carbon developer.

name: CleanCapture Tech
tech_note: Solid-sorbent direct air capture with a novel plate/heat-exchanger reactor design targeting low-temperature, fully-electric regeneration.
description: CleanCapture Tech is an early-stage U.S. DAC startup founded in 2021 by MIT engineers, developing a solid-sorbent gas/solid reactor for low-cost, mass-producible atmospheric CO2 capture. The company has demonstrated a first-generation design at lab scale with DOE support and is seeking investors/partners to scale up to a commercial unit module.

name: Cler-Verts
tech_note: Cler Verts operates multi-filière organic waste valorization platforms in Occitanie, France, producing biochar via wood pyrolysis alongside compost, biomass fuel, and biogas via methanization.
description: Cler Verts is a French group established in Occitanie since 2003 that collects, treats and valorizes organic matter for communities and professionals, with activities including wood recycling, biomass fuels for boilers, green waste composting, biodéchets valorization, methanization/renewable energy, and biochar and organic soil amendment production. The company claims to produce the first CE-certified biochar in France. A new pyrolyzer installation was planned for August 2024.

name: Climate Impact Partners
tech_note: Voluntary carbon market retailer, broker, and project developer that creates and manages portfolios of carbon credits (both avoidance and removals) and energy attribute certificates for corporate buyers.
description: Climate Impact Partners is a UK/US-based voluntary carbon market specialist formed from the merger of Natural Capital Partners and ClimateCare, offering carbon credit sourcing, portfolio development, MRV support and project origination across 600+ projects in 56 countries. They are a carbon market intermediary rather than a physical CDR supplier — their business is trading and developing credits from third-party projects, including nature-based removals.

name: Climate Vault Solutions
tech_note: Curates a portfolio of third-party CDR projects via an expert-led RFP and sells those credits (alongside compliance-market allowance retirements) to corporates through its software platform.
description: Climate Vault Solutions is a Chicago-based CDR ecosystem company (spun out of a University of Chicago nonprofit) that combines compliance-market carbon allowance vaulting with a curated portfolio of carbon removal credits sourced via its Tech Chamber RFP program (chaired by former U.S. Energy Secretary Ernest Moniz). It resells CDR credits from vetted suppliers (e.g., Octavia Carbon, Carbon Lockdown) through its sales channel and Climate Solutions Platform software to corporate clients. It does not itself remove CO2; it is a curator/broker/platform.

name: ClimateCarbon
tech_note: Operates a pyrolysis/carbonization plant in Eberswalde, Germany that converts forestry and agricultural residual wood into biochar (Biokohlenstoff), with renewable energy and bio-oil as co-products.
description: ClimateCarbon Eberswalde GmbH & Co. KG is part of the ForestFinance Group and is building a carbonization facility in Eberswalde, Germany, with carbonauten GmbH as technology partner responsible for constructing the production plant and marketing the biochar. The plant uses three modules each with two carbonization retorts and is designed to produce 4,800 tonnes of biochar per year. The company is a genuine biochar CDR supplier funded through limited-partner investor participation.

name: ClimatePartner Impact
tech_note: Develops nature-based climate projects (reforestation/revegetation like Spekboom thicket restoration in South Africa, soil organic carbon, blue carbon, biochar) plus avoidance projects such as improved cookstoves, and structures carbon finance and impact-investing vehicles around them.
description: ClimatePartner Impact GmbH is a Munich-based subsidiary of ClimatePartner GmbH, founded in 2022, that develops voluntary carbon market projects with a focus on nature-based removals (afforestation, reforestation, revegetation, soil/blue carbon, biochar) and improved cookstoves. It provides project development, due diligence, portfolio management, and carbon/impact investing opportunities, with a Kenya subsidiary (Sand River Carbon) and projects including Spekboom thicket restoration in South Africa.

name: ClimeFi
tech_note: Buyer-side CDR portfolio manager providing market intelligence, project ratings, RFP/procurement services, and ongoing portfolio monitoring for corporate and institutional purchasers of durable carbon removal.
description: ClimeFi is a Zurich-based CDR portfolio manager and procurement intermediary founded in 2022, with offices in Paris, London, New York, and Singapore. It exclusively represents corporate buyers, structuring RFPs, sourcing projects, and managing diversified portfolios across durable CDR pathways (DAC, BECCS, ERW, mineralization, marine CDR). Notable milestones include facilitating the first CDR-backed Article 6.2 ITMO transfer (Switzerland–Norway), the first publicly announced EU CRCF transaction, and over 500,000 tonnes of contracted durable CDR.

name: ClimeRock
tech_note: Spreads finely ground basalt from nearby quarries onto French agricultural fields to accelerate silicate weathering, converting atmospheric CO2 into stable bicarbonate.
description: ClimeRock is a French ERW (Enhanced Rock Weathering) startup founded in 2023 and based near Paris, with operations in the Massif Central. It spreads finely ground basalt on agricultural fields to sequester CO2 as bicarbonate while improving soil health, selling removal credits to corporate buyers.

name: Climeworks
tech_note: Solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture using modular collectors paired with geologic mineralization storage via Carbfix in Iceland; also curates multi-pathway removal portfolios.
description: Climeworks is a Swiss-based pioneer in Direct Air Capture, operating the Orca (4,000 tCO2/yr) and Mammoth (36,000 tCO2/yr) DAC plants in Iceland with solid sorbent technology. The company also offers blended carbon removal portfolios combining DAC with nature-based and other engineered solutions for corporate buyers.

name: Climitra
tech_note: Climitra operates controlled pyrolysis units that convert agricultural and invasive biomass into high-spec biochar used as a drop-in replacement for PCI coal in steelmaking and for soil-based carbon sequestration with dMRV.
description: Climitra Carbon Private Limited is a Delhi-based biochar startup founded in February 2025 that engineers feedstock-specific pyrolysis machinery and a geospatial biomass-intelligence platform to supply industrial-grade bio-coal to Indian steelmakers while generating CDR credits. The company raised $1.8M pre-seed in June 2025 and is deploying its first project in Kutch (Gujarat) plus projects in Punjab and Uttarakhand.

name: Clo Carbon Cymru
tech_note: Produces laboratory-verified biochar on Welsh farms and issues traceable Carbon Lock Origin Certificates (CLOCs) for each tonne of CO2e stored.
description: Clo Carbon Cymru is a Welsh (UK) company based in Llandeilo that produces biochar on agricultural land and issues Carbon Lock Origin Certificates (CLOCs), each representing one tonne of CO2e removed and stored in biochar. It targets Welsh farmers as an alternative to the Sustainable Farming Scheme, integrating biochar production with biodiversity enhancement. The company combines physical biochar removal with its own registry/certification framework.

name: Co-reactive
tech_note: Ex-situ CO2 mineralization of silicate minerals and steel slags into supplementary cementitious materials that permanently sequester CO2 as stable carbonates.
description: Co-reactive is a Düsseldorf-based climate-tech startup, spun out of RWTH Aachen University in 2024, that converts CO2 with silicate minerals (olivine) or metallurgical slags into CO2-negative supplementary cementitious materials (CO-SCMs) via a continuous mineralization process. In January 2026 the company closed a €6.5M seed round led by HTGF to scale from pilot to a 1,000-ton/year demonstration plant in Q2 2026, with industrial-scale plants planned from 2027. CO2 is permanently bound as stable carbonates within the SCM product.

name: Coal Products Limited (CPL)
tech_note: CPL uses hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) and high-temperature torrefaction to convert organic/biowaste feedstocks into biochar suitable for sequestration, alongside its legacy solid-fuel briquette business.
description: CPL Industries produces smokeless solid fuels and operates within the energy sector, providing solid fuel heating solutions, secondary biomass technologies, filtration solutions, and refractory repair services. The company is diversifying into carbon removal via a BEIS-funded biowaste-to-biochar project at its Immingham site, which is set to remove 6,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions annually by 2025, and also contributes biochar R&D to the EU ReSolute biorefinery project.

name: Cotierra
tech_note: Cotierra builds and operates decentralized, mobile biochar reactors that convert coffee-tree pruning residues into biochar applied to soils on Colombian coffee farms, with an IoT-enabled MRV system.
description: Cotierra is a Swiss-Colombian, Zurich-headquartered company focused on decentralized biochar production for carbon removal and emission reduction. In partnership with Volcafe and its Colombian entity Carcafe, Cotierra has issued the first biochar-related carbon removal credits under an external carbon standard within Colombia's coffee value chains. It sells these credits on the voluntary carbon market and partners with myclimate as an exclusive project developer.

name: Cowboy Clean Fuels
tech_note: Injects sugar beet molasses into depleted coalbed methane wells in Wyoming's Powder River Basin, where indigenous microbes convert the biomass into renewable natural gas and CO2 that is permanently sequestered onto coal surfaces (BiCRS+RNG).
description: Cowboy Clean Fuels (CCF), founded in 2020 and spun out of the University of Wyoming's Center for Biogenic Natural Gas Research, commercializes a patented Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage plus Renewable Natural Gas (BiCRS+RNG) process. Its Triangle Unit project in the Powder River Basin uses agricultural residues injected into deep coal seams to produce RNG while permanently sequestering CO2, and CCF sells durable CDR credits alongside renewable gas.

name: Cquesta
tech_note: Uses gene editing to engineer deeper, larger root systems in commodity crops so that more plant carbon is deposited and stabilized in subsoil layers.
description: Cquesta is a US-based agricultural biotech developing gene-edited crop traits that produce deeper, larger root systems so that carbon is deposited further down in the soil profile where it is more stable. The company licenses its deep-root traits to seed companies and aims to generate carbon credits for farmers with no change in agronomic practices. Crops being developed include cover crops (CoverCress), soybean, canola, sorghum, corn and rice.

name: Cquestr8
tech_note: Reactor-based accelerated carbonation of magnesium-rich silicate minerals to convert CO2 into solid carbonates and stable ocean bicarbonate for permanent storage.
description: Cquestr8 is a UK-based startup (Durham) developing a reactor-based accelerated mineral carbonation process using magnesium-rich silicates to sequester CO2 from industrial sources (biogas, fermentation, cement, lime, steel) as stable carbonates and ocean bicarbonate. Founded in 2020, it raised $300K seed from Counteract in 2021 and was a 2023 SOSV Climate Tech Summit finalist. No significant public news or follow-on funding since 2023, though the UK entity remains registered as Active.

name: Ctrl-S
tech_note: Acquires, diligences, and licenses IP, experimental data, and engineering knowledge from failed or pivoting DAC companies to accelerate development and train materials-discovery AI.
description: Ctrl-S is a US startup founded by Jason Hochman that acquires intellectual property, experimental data, and engineering know-how from distressed or failed direct air capture companies. It plans to license this archive (including "negative learnings") to remaining DAC developers, large energy firms, and AI-driven materials discovery companies via subscriptions, licensing fees, and royalties. It does not physically remove CO2 itself.

name: Cula
tech_note: Digital MRV platform that automates sensor/machine data capture from CDR projects (mainly biochar pyrolysis) and pushes verified data to crediting registries.
description: Cula Technologies is a digital MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification) software platform for carbon removal projects, founded in 2023 by Hasso-Plattner-Institut and HHL Leipzig alumni. The company integrates machine, IoT, and sensor data from CDR producers (primarily biochar) and transfers it via API directly into registries like Puro.earth and Carbon Standards International. Cula does not physically remove CO2 — it is an enabling-tech/ecosystem player whose entire business depends on the CDR market.

name: Cultivo
tech_note: Cultivo is a nature-based carbon project developer using an AI/geospatial platform to originate, finance, and operate large-scale land restoration projects (primarily U.S. grasslands soil carbon, plus afforestation, agroforestry, improved forest management, mangrove restoration, and biochar) that generate removal credits.
description: Cultivo is a platform for developing and operating natural assets, partnering with institutional investors and multinational corporations, with a model that generates returns through payments for services, primarily carbon removal, unlocked by land regeneration activities. They focus heavily on U.S. grasslands but also cover afforestation/reforestation, agroforestry, improved forest management, mangrove restoration, and biochar. Cultivo acquired Kateri, a U.S.-based carbon grasslands project developer, effective December 1, 2025, strengthening its vertically integrated model; combined projects aim to remove over 9 million tonnes CO₂e over 30 years.

name: DAC Labs
tech_note: Electrochemical direct air capture using earth-abundant materials, developed as a University of Sydney spinout.
description: DAC Labs (Dac Laboratories) is an Australian University of Sydney spinout based in Brookvale, NSW, developing electrochemical direct air capture technology aimed at earth-abundant materials and low-cost equipment. Founded by Dr Sam Wenger, the company is building a ~10 tonne/year demonstration unit with plans to scale to a kilotonne-scale pilot plant, and was backed by the University of Sydney's Pre-Seed Launch Fund.

name: DACLAB
tech_note: Solid-sorbent DAC using a decoupled moving-bed Temperature Vacuum Swing Adsorption (TVSA) architecture with ultra-low-temperature regeneration, packaged as modular container-sized "Kelvin" units.
description: DACLab is a Palo Alto-based climate-tech startup developing modular solid-sorbent direct air capture (DAC) systems using a patent-pending Temperature Vacuum Swing Adsorption (TVSA) cycle that regenerates at ultra-low temperatures (~70°C) and under 1,800 kWh/ton. It launched out of stealth in September 2025 with a $3M seed round and its first commercial "Kelvin" product line aimed at e-fuels and CO2 sequestration markets.

name: DACMA GmbH
tech_note: DACMA manufactures modular solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture systems, delivering plants for CCS and CCU in diverse climate zones.
description: DACMA GmbH, headquartered in Hamburg, Germany, is a pioneering DAC manufacturer for high-quality DAC systems and carbon credits. The company has deployed its first industrialized Direct Air Capture System with a capacity of capturing 300 tons CO2 per year, the largest DAC system running in South America, handed over to the customer in October 2024, and recently signed a long-term joint development agreement with Deep Sky to scale DAC in Canada, including the first DACMA deployment in North America.

name: DACworx
tech_note: Develops modular, standardized direct air capture systems using ambient-condition solid sorbent filters, licensed to project developers and operators for CO2 removal or synthetic fuel/chemical production.
description: DACworx is a European DAC technology developer offering cost-efficient, scalable carbon capture for project developers, contractors, and operators aiming for permanent CO₂ removal or production of sustainable chemicals and fuels, via modular standardized designs. The process uses ambient operating conditions and readily available CO₂ filter materials, backed by in-house manufacturing and partnerships across Europe and the U.S.

name: Dair Capture
tech_note: Early-stage U.S. direct air capture developer claiming a solid-sorbent-style DAC system with a novel regeneration method that produces clean water as a byproduct, targeting both sequestration and CO2 utilization in industries like cement, healthcare, and beverages.
description: Dair Capture is a U.S.-based direct air capture startup developing a DAC technology it claims is roughly 10x cheaper than incumbents, marketed for both carbon sequestration and supply of clean CO2 to industrial users. The company's public footprint is minimal — website only, 0 employees reported on LinkedIn, no registry listings, no funding announcements, and no evidence of deployed hardware or delivered tonnes.

name: Danube Carbon Storage
tech_note: Full-chain bioCCS project capturing ~500,000 tonnes/year biogenic CO2 from Pannonia Bio's fermentation/anaerobic digestion processes and injecting into an onshore saline aquifer in the Pannonian Basin, Hungary.
description: Danube Carbon Storage is a Budapest-based project developer building a full-chain BECCS operation in Central Hungary, backed by ClonBio Group (owner of Pannonia Bio biorefinery) and EMOV Limited. Its flagship Danube Removals project, selected for €48.4M EU Innovation Fund support in October 2024, will generate 5.6 million tonnes of EU-CRCF-certified carbon removal credits over 10 years. Operations are carried out via OGD Green Storage, a subsidiary of Hungary's third-largest hydrocarbon producer.

name: Dark Earth Carbon
tech_note: Operates a rotary kiln pyrolysis plant in Iringa/Mafinga, Tanzania, converting forestry and agricultural residues into biochar that is applied to smallholder farmland for carbon sequestration and soil improvement.
description: Since 2024, atmosfair and Tanzanian company Dark Earth Carbon (DEC) produce biochar in a large pyrolysis plant in Iringa, Tanzania, and use it as fertiliser on Tanzanian farmland. DEC has delivered the first industrial biochar carbon removals in East Africa, with credits issued via the CSI Registry. atmosfair and Dark Earth Carbon are planning a second pyrolysis plant in Mafinga to leverage existing infrastructure.

name: Decarbon
tech_note: Builds solid-sorbent fiber adsorbents and modular structured contactor hardware for DAC and point-source CO2 capture, using low-grade waste heat for regeneration.
description: Decarbontek (decarbon.tech) is a Massachusetts-based climate tech startup founded by Dr. Yong Ding that develops proprietary solid fiber adsorbents and modular structured capture systems for both point-source CO2 capture and direct air capture. The company manufactures its own MOF-based sorbent (DCF-1) and a patent-pending fiber-winding platform, selling both cartridges/modules and managed capture services. They announced a major product launch in September 2025.

name: Deep Sky
tech_note: Tech-agnostic DAC project developer operating a multi-technology carbon removal hub (Deep Sky Alpha) in Alberta with permanent geological storage.
description: Deep Sky is a Montreal-based carbon removal project developer that builds and operates DAC facilities in Canada, aggregating multiple third-party DAC technologies under one roof for permanent underground CO2 storage. Their flagship Deep Sky Alpha facility in Innisfail, Alberta began operations in August 2025 as North America's first DAC-to-storage site, and they have partnerships with Airbus, GE Vernova, Skyrenu, Mission Zero, Airhive, DACMA, Skytree, and others. They have $130M in funding plus a $40M Breakthrough Energy Catalyst grant and founding offtakers including Microsoft and RBC.

name: Deepsink
tech_note: Fractional sales/commercial service for engineered CDR project developers — helps connect supply with buyers and market makers (a broker/sales-agency ecosystem role).
description: Deepsink is a UK-based fractional sales and commercialization service for engineered carbon dioxide removal projects, helping project developers connect with buyers and market makers. The team (co-founder Oliver Erb, partnerships lead Oliver Grogono, and others) was active in 2025, including attending DeCarbon Tokyo 2025. The actual operating domain is deepsink.co.uk, not deepsink.com as listed in the DB snapshot.

name: Desired Future Conditions
tech_note: Produces in-woods biochar by pyrolyzing forest slash, logging residues, and cull timber in air curtain burners with continuous biochar production features, delivering physical biochar and CDR credits.
description: Desired Future Conditions, PBC is a U.S. public benefit corporation that partners with North American landowners to produce biochar from woody forest residues at in-woods production sites. The company sells physical biochar (primarily for agricultural soil amendment) and associated carbon removal credits, while aiming to improve forest health and wildfire resilience.

name: Diacarbon Energy
tech_note: Slow-pyrolysis / torrefaction of woody biomass waste (forestry and sawmill residues) to produce biochar, biocoal (torrefied pellets), bio-oil and syngas.
description: Diacarbon Energy is a privately-held British Columbia company incorporated in 2009 that operates a thermal biomass refinery converting forestry and agricultural waste into biochar, wood pellets and torrefied biocoal. Its primary commercial focus has shifted toward wood pellets and coal-replacement biocoal for industrial fuel markets, with biochar as a co-product for soil amendment. There is no public evidence of recent CDR credit issuances or carbon-removal offtake deals.

name: Dotz Nano
tech_note: Dotz Nano develops proprietary amine-modified polymer (AMP) and carbon-based solid sorbents for Direct Air Capture and low-concentration flue-gas CO2 capture, supplying sorbent material to DAC system developers.
description: Dotz Nano (ASX-listed, operating via its Dotz Earth/DOTZearth carbon capture division) is a materials company engineering solid sorbents — including its AMP polymer sorbent — tailored for DAC and point-source CO2 capture. They do not operate DAC plants themselves but supply the core removal-enabling material to DAC developers such as CarbonCapture Inc. Activity remains strong with a first commercial order and new sorbent generation announced in late 2025.

name: Douglas County Forest Products
tech_note: Oregon sawmill that pyrolyzes waste wood chips and sawdust into biochar and sells the resulting carbon removal credits via Puro.earth.
description: Douglas County Forest Products is an independently owned sawmill in Roseburg, Oregon that produces biochar from its wood residues (chips, sawdust) as a side stream. It sells CDR credits on the voluntary market and was listed among the top North American biochar CDR sellers as of early 2025.

name: Dowmann
tech_note: Dowmann builds and operates factories that pyrolyse waste biomass (forestry/hedgerow/grass residues) into biochar, bio-oil and renewable electricity, with the biochar applied to soil for long-term carbon storage.
description: Dowmann is an Irish carbon removal company that transforms waste biomass into biochar, renewable fuel and clean electricity through pyrolysis. They work with remove as a strategic partner and Puro.earth to verify their carbon removal. The company is very lean, with three full-time individuals and two remote workers.

name: Drax
tech_note: Drax operates the UK's largest biomass power station and is developing Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) projects at Selby (UK) and in the US South via its Elimini carbon removals subsidiary.
description: Drax Group is a UK-listed energy company that generates electricity from wood pellets and is developing BECCS projects to deliver engineered carbon removals. Its Elimini business markets CDRs from planned BECCS plants, though the flagship UK Selby BECCS project has been scaled back amid regulatory and cost uncertainty, and Drax announced staff cuts to its carbon capture division in late 2025.

name: Drax/Elimini
tech_note: Elimini develops bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) projects that generate renewable power while permanently sequestering biogenic CO2 from biomass combustion.
description: Elimini is a wholly owned US-based subsidiary of UK energy group Drax, launched in September 2024 at Climate Week NYC to develop BECCS projects in North America and internationally and to market carbon removals from Drax Power Station. Its first 300 MW greenfield BECCS project (3Mt CO2/year) is under development with Sargent & Lundy, and in July 2025 it signed a joint development agreement with Copenhagen utility HOFOR for a Danish BECCS facility.

name: E-quester
tech_note: Electrochemical liquid-solvent Direct Air Capture: air is scrubbed in an alkaline capture solution and the dissolved carbonate is regenerated via an electrochemical cell powered by renewable electricity, avoiding the high-temperature calcination step of conventional liquid-solvent DAC.
description: E-quester is a University of Toronto spinout (founded 2021) developing electrochemical Direct Air Capture technology. Based in Toronto, Ontario, the team is using electrochemistry to lower the cost of a carbon capture technique known as Direct Air Capture. The team previously earned an XPRIZE Carbon Removal Student Award with US $250,000 in seed funding, which the team has used to further develop their prototype, and was later named an XPRIZE Milestone finalist.

name: EAD
tech_note: EAD operates a pyrolysis/carbonization plant in Darmstadt-Kranichstein that converts urban green-waste biomass into EBC-certified biochar used on municipal green spaces.
description: EAD (Eigenbetrieb für kommunale Aufgaben und Dienstleistungen) is the 100% city-owned municipal services utility of Darmstadt, Germany, responsible for waste management, street cleaning, and composting. As a division of the municipality, it runs a biochar carbonization plant producing EBC-certified biochar products from urban green-space biomass. The biochar activity is a small CDR-relevant operation within a much larger municipal utility.

name: EDAC Labs
tech_note: Develops an electrochemical "electrosynthesizer" that splits brine into acid and base at roughly half the energy of conventional processes, supplying reagents for liquid-solvent DAC, ocean alkalinity enhancement, enhanced weathering, and carbon-negative mining (metal extraction + CO2 mineralization).
description: EDAC Labs is a Baltimore-based Johns Hopkins spin-out (founded July 2022) commercializing an exclusively-licensed electrochemical salt-splitting technology that produces low-cost acid and base for carbon removal applications. Its technology serves both as an enabling input for third-party DAC/OAE/ERW developers and as the basis for an in-house carbon-negative mining project that combines metal recovery with permanent CO2 storage as carbonates. Raised a $3M seed from the Grantham Foundation in Aug 2023 and received a $500K Frontier prepurchase the same year.

name: EGoS
tech_note: Operates an industrial pyrolysis plant converting FSC/PEFC-certified wood chips into biochar, feed carbon, and Terra Preta, with co-generation of green electricity and heat from syngas.
description: EGoS GmbH (trading as Pflanzenkohle24) is a German biochar producer based in Bottrop-Kirchhellen that operates a BImSchG-permitted pyrolysis plant producing biochar, feed charcoal, and Terra Preta for agriculture and livestock. The plant also generates CO2-negative electricity and heat from synthesis gases, and the company reports absorbing roughly 10,000 tonnes of CO2 per year as fixed carbon.

name: EM-Süd
tech_note: Produces EBC-certified biochar from hardwood biomass (pyrolysis) sold for agricultural, livestock, biogas, and concrete applications, primarily as a soil amendment paired with Effective Microorganisms.
description: EM-Technologie Zentrum Süd GmbH (EM-Süd) is a German family business based in Haldenwang, Allgäu, that produces biochar under the "Pflanzenkohle Allgäu" brand alongside Effective Microorganisms (EM) products for agriculture, animal husbandry, and soil improvement. Their biochar is EBC-certified and FiBL-listed, made from hardwood (beech), and marketed for uses including soil improvement, biogas fermenters, livestock bedding/manure, and concrete additives. They are members of German Biochar e.V. and operate an active online shop and farm shop.

name: Earth Foundries
tech_note: Operates mobile pyrolysis units (Tigercat Carbonators, branded "Slash Attack") to convert unmerchantable woody forest waste from California hazardous fuels reduction projects into biochar on-site.
description: Earth Foundries is a funded company based in Saratoga, California, founded in 2021 by Dorothea Dede Smullen and Roger Smullen, operating as a developer of carbon-negative products from forest waste. Its mission is to reduce the cost and carbon footprint of landscape-scale forest health projects by processing unmerchantable forest material from hazardous fuels reduction projects into biochar on site and at scale with its Slash Attack service. The biochar is sold into compost, stormwater bioswale, and manure management applications.

name: Earthcare Solutions
tech_note: Patented thermal gasification of high-ash organic feedstocks (biosolids, manure, MSW digestate) to produce stable biochar while destroying PFAS and microplastics.
description: Earthcare Solutions is a U.S.-based circular waste management company that operates patented thermal gasification systems to convert biosolids, manure, and other organic wastes into biochar (marketed as Ecochar). The company is registered on Puro.earth and sells its biochar for agronomic, remediation, filtration, and animal-bedding uses while also destroying PFAS and microplastics during processing.

name: Earthly
tech_note: Earthly is a UK-based marketplace and platform that curates and resells high-integrity nature-based carbon and biodiversity credits (reforestation, mangroves, regenerative agriculture) to corporate buyers.
description: Earthly is a nature-based carbon credit marketplace that helps businesses invest in vetted reforestation, mangrove, and biodiversity projects via instant purchases, subscriptions, or bespoke portfolios. They assess projects using 106 data points and partnerships with BeZero and Google Earth Engine, acting as a broker/curator rather than a project developer.

name: Earthly Biochar
tech_note: Produces biochar from waste wood via pyrolysis and sells it as a soil amendment, plus manufactures smokeless biochar kilns for gardeners to make their own biochar.
description: Earthly Biochar is a small UK-based biochar producer (incorporated 2018, Salisbury) that makes organic biochar from waste wood and sells it, along with purpose-built smokeless biochar kilns, to gardeners, horticulturists, and land managers. A related entity, Earthly Biochar Industries Ltd (2023), appears aimed at scaling production. The company positions biochar as a negative-emission technology and soil amendment.

name: Earthshot Labs
tech_note: Tech-enabled carbon project developer for nature-based projects (ARR, REDD+, IFM, agroforestry), operating the LandOS platform that uses remote sensing, AI, and ecosystem modeling to streamline project development, MRV, and financing.
description: Earthshot is a tech-enabled carbon project developer and due diligence provider focused on ARR, REDD, and IFM, having supported more than 60 carbon projects globally, with a LandOS platform that helps assess land eligibility, carbon potential, and technical risk. The company closed a $5.5M Series A in 2024 to expand its platform for nature-based carbon project development and financing, and has directed over $55 million in financing across projects. They develop and co-finance projects with partners like BirdLife International and Tree Aid, earning revenue via credit share, commissions, and carbon development services.

name: Ebb Carbon
tech_note: Electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement using bipolar membrane electrodialysis integrated with desalination plant brine streams to generate NaOH returned to seawater.
description: Ebb Carbon is a US-based marine CDR supplier using electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement (bipolar membrane electrodialysis) to convert desalination brine into alkaline seawater that draws down atmospheric CO2 as stable bicarbonate. The company operates Project Macoma in Port Angeles, WA and runs a demonstration system at PNNL-Sequim. Recent commercial traction includes a 350,000-tonne Microsoft offtake, a 3,500-tonne Google prepurchase (Dec 2025), and a partnership with the Saudi Water Authority.

name: Echo Tech Carbon Corporation
tech_note: Develops biochar production projects via pyrolysis (and gasification) of crop waste, primarily in equatorial regions like Senegal and Uganda, selling durable biochar CDR credits.
description: Echo Tech Carbon Corporation is a Vancouver, Canada-based biochar project developer operating primarily in Africa, converting agricultural residues into biochar for soil amendment and construction materials while generating permanent carbon removal credits. The company is certified/listed via Puro.Earth and Carbonfuture and has inaugurated multiple biochar plants, including a Senegal partnership with rice farmers.

name: EcoAct
tech_note: Climate consultancy and nature-based carbon project developer (afforestation, reforestation, mangrove restoration) supporting corporate net-zero strategies.
description: EcoAct is an international climate and sustainability consultancy and carbon project developer, founded in France in 2006, acquired by Atos in 2020 and then by Schneider Electric in 2023. As of 2025 it has been rebranded as SE Advisory Services, Schneider Electric's global consulting branch, focused on net-zero strategy, carbon accounting, reporting, and nature-based carbon project development (e.g., mangrove restoration, reforestation). They are a consultancy/project-developer in the CDR ecosystem rather than a removal technology supplier.

name: EcoChar
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis units to convert vegetable/biomass waste into biochar for soil regeneration and green charcoal briquettes as a wood-charcoal substitute.
description: EcoChar is a France-based company developing agroforestry and regenerative agriculture projects that produce biochar as an agricultural bio-stimulant and green charcoal briquettes via pyrolysis of biomass waste. They position biochar both as a soil amendment and as a carbon sink. The firm is very small (≈3 employees) with limited recent public signals.

name: EcoFix
tech_note: Pyrolysis of nut-processing agricultural waste into biochar for carbon sequestration and soil amendment, with the facility developed under Terraton's full-stack biochar platform.
description: EcoFix is a nut processor in Kenya whose agricultural waste is being converted to biochar through a partnership with Terraton Biochar Platform. The "EcoFix Kenya Biochar" facility is listed as a future supplier on Puro.earth and is under review by Isometric, and is expected (together with a Ghana cocoa project) to deliver over 20,000 tonnes of annual CO₂ removal. The biochar project carries the EcoFix name and the host is the operational site for CDR.

name: Ecoera
tech_note: Ecoera pyrolyzes pelletized agricultural residues into biochar at the Skånefrö/Hammenhög facility in southern Sweden, selling Puro.earth-verified CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs).
description: Ecoera is a Swedish biochar CDR company founded at Chalmers Ventures in collaboration with Skånefrö AB, and started Sweden's first large-scale biochar carbon removal work in 2009. Biochar is produced in Hammenhög, South Sweden, at one of the largest biochar production facilities in the EU using PYREG P500 and P1500 carbonization systems. Output is third-party verified under the European Biochar Certificate and the Puro.earth Biochar methodology, and sold as CORC removal credits on carbon marketplaces.

name: Ecomerit Technologies
tech_note: Uses wind energy to electrolyze sea salt into alkaline constituents that precipitate atmospheric CO2 as mineral carbonates, which sink to ocean depth, combining ocean alkalinity enhancement with mineralization.
description: Ecomerit Technologies is a Santa Barbara-based marine-renewable product design studio and laboratory founded in 2010 by Jim and Brent Dehlsen, developing the Precipitor CDR system alongside Aquantis marine current turbines, Anacapa wave energy generators, and SeaWell desalination buoys. The CO2 Precipitor project pursues atmospheric CDR via mineralization and OAE with durable carbon sequestration at ocean depth, mounting systems on offshore wind turbines, ships, and platforms. They are a CDR technology developer (supplier) operating at early/R&D scale.

name: Econew
tech_note: Continuous slow-pyrolysis of certified eucalyptus forestry residues producing high-fixed-carbon biochar for carbon removal credits.
description: Econew is a Brazilian clean bioenergy company based in northern Minas Gerais that produces biochar via continuous pyrolysis of FSC®/PEFC-certified eucalyptus residues. Their continuous pyrolysis process converts FSC®/PEFC-certified eucalyptus residues into biochar with a high fixed-carbon content, with each ton of confirmed CO₂ removal corresponding to one carbon credit available in the voluntary market. They align with Puro.earth standards for permanent carbon removal credits.

name: Ecotree
tech_note: EcoTree acquires, plants, and sustainably manages mixed-species, continuous-cover forests across France and Europe, issuing Bureau Veritas-certified carbon removal credits under its own methodology aligned with Label Bas-Carbone.
description: EcoTree is a French nature-based solutions company that directly manages forests across France, Denmark, the UK, Germany and Belgium, generating third-party verified carbon credits from afforestation/reforestation and peatland projects. It sells tree ownership to individuals and carbon credits to corporates for CSRD/SBTi reporting, operating its own forestry teams rather than brokering credits from third parties.

name: Eion
tech_note: Eion applies pulverized olivine to US farmland as a replacement for agricultural lime, using a patented direct soil-sampling MRV method to measure CO2 removed via enhanced rock weathering.
description: Eion is a US-based enhanced rock weathering supplier that deploys olivine (sourced from Sibelco's Norwegian quarry) across farmland in the US Midwest and South via partnerships with ag cooperatives like Growmark. The company has delivered credits to Stripe and signed offtakes with Microsoft and a $33M Frontier agreement covering 78,707 tons between 2027-2030. It holds a patent on direct soil-sampling MRV for ERW.

name: Eion Carbon
tech_note: Applied pelletized olivine to cropland to accelerate silicate weathering, with patented soil-based tracer MRV to quantify CO2 removal as bicarbonate.
description: Eion was a U.S.-based enhanced rock weathering (ERW) carbon removal company that applied crushed olivine on agricultural fields to permanently sequester atmospheric CO2 while improving soil pH. It pioneered olivine-based deployments and a patented soil-tracer MRV approach, delivering ERW credits to Stripe and contracting removal with Microsoft. In February 2026, Terradot acquired Eion's assets, contracts (100,000+ tons), IP, and team, effectively ending Eion as a standalone entity.

name: Ekovilla
tech_note: Ekovilla manufactures carbon-negative cellulose-fiber insulation from recycled wood fiber/paper, which durably stores biogenic carbon in buildings and is credited under Puro.earth's Wooden Building Elements methodology.
description: Ekovilla is the insulation brand of Finnish parent EcoUp Oyj, known for carbon-neutral insulation manufactured from recycled wood fibres. They recycle wooden-building-element waste into carbon-negative cellulose fiber insulation (CFI) under Puro.earth's Wooden Building Elements methodology, storing carbon for roughly 50 years. EcoUp has sold vintage 2022 Puro.earth CORCs from the Ekovilla net-negative cellulose insulation project on Xpansiv's CBL spot exchange.

name: Electrocean
tech_note: Develops electrochemical seawater processing that removes CO2 while producing carbon-negative calcium carbonate and hydrogen, with co-benefits for shellfish aquaculture and coastal defense.
description: Electrocean is an early-stage marine CDR supplier deploying electrochemical technology to sequester CO2 from seawater while co-producing carbon-negative calcium carbonate and hydrogen, and enhancing shellfish aquaculture. The company's approach won Purdue Innovates' Spring 2026 Moonshot Pitch Competition.

name: Eleryc
tech_note: Eleryc uses a low-voltage electrochemical process to produce hydroxide that reacts with atmospheric/dissolved CO2 to form stable bicarbonate/carbonate solutions for durable ocean storage — an electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement approach.
description: Eleryc, Inc. is a US-based CDR startup that acquired electrochemical hydroxide-generation patents from Arelac/Fortera in October 2023 and submitted a Frontier Climate Summer 2025 prepurchase application. Their technology uses low-energy electrochemistry to generate alkalinity that converts CO2 into stable bicarbonate/carbonate species for long-term storage, placing them in the ocean alkalinity enhancement / electrochemical OAE category rather than liquid-solvent DAC as previously recorded.

name: Enable Earth
tech_note: Enable Earth converts agricultural residues (primarily corn stalks and rice straw) into biochar via pyrolysis kilns in northern/central Thailand, sequestering carbon in soils while reducing open-field burning and PM2.5 pollution.
description: Enable Earth is a biochar project developer based in Wiang Pa Pao District, Chiang Rai Province, Thailand that targets local corn residues otherwise openly burned and transforms them into stable carbon via pyrolysis. The company has passed Puro.earth's Preliminary Assessment as a CO2 Removal Supplier and commissioned an imported CharMaker pyrolysis system at the end of 2025 as the first stage of a multimillion-dollar project in Thailand.

name: EnergieWerk Ilg GmbH
tech_note: Operates wood-fired SYNCRAFT gasifier CHP plants in Dornbirn, Austria producing biochar and green heat/power, with a newly commissioned Bright Renewables CO2 capture & liquefaction system (BECCS) added in 2025.
description: EnergieWerk Ilg GmbH is a family-owned regional energy company in Dornbirn, Vorarlberg, Austria that runs wood-chip gasification CHP plants producing biochar alongside renewable electricity and district heat. In 2025 it commissioned a Bright Renewables carbon capture and liquefaction unit on its gasifier, moving it from pure biochar production into BECCS-style biogenic CO2 capture.

name: Energnist CaptureCo
tech_note: Post-combustion carbon capture on a municipal waste-to-energy (incineration) plant in Esbjerg, Denmark; the biogenic fraction of the flue gas yields negative emissions when permanently stored.
description: Energnist is West Denmark's largest waste-to-energy company, owned by 16 municipalities and operating waste-energy plants in Esbjerg and Kolding. Energnist CaptureCo A/S is its dedicated carbon-capture subsidiary developing a CCS facility at the Esbjerg plant to capture over 200,000 tonnes of CO2 per year, with transport via pipeline to an Esbjerg Harbour CO2 terminal for liquefaction and permanent storage. It is one of 10 companies prequalified by the Danish Energy Agency to compete for DKK 28.7 billion in CCS funding, and signed a letter of intent with Carbon Circle in April 2026 to jointly develop the capture project using Carbon Circle's CaCiMod modular system.

name: Energy Farmers
tech_note: Develops in-house pyrolysis and gasification systems to convert organic waste (wheat straw, poultry litter, weed biomass, sewage sludge) into biochar and bioenergy, selling biochar to Australian farmers under the farmchar brand.
description: Energy Farmers Australia is a Western Australia-based small company that has developed its own pyrolysis kilns (including mobile/containerised units) to process organic wastes into biochar and bioenergy. They supply biochar products to Australian agriculture and industry via their farmchar brand and have worked on projects with poultry farms, weed-control (African Boxthorn) and waste water sludge.

name: Energy Ocean
tech_note: Operates a pyrolysis plant converting regional wood biomass into EBC-certified biochar, supplying heat to the village of Luthern as a by-product.
description: eoc energy ocean GmbH produces EBC-certified biochar in Luthern, canton Lucerne, Switzerland, binding CO2 while delivering heat to the village and promoting the circular economy. Its first pyrolysis plant went into operation in Luthern in September 2023. Products are marketed under the Swiss Biochar brand.

name: Engrow
tech_note: Operates zero-emission continuous carbonization/pyrolysis units in South India that convert fast-growing hardwood energy-plantation biomass into enriched biochar (used as soil amendment) plus co-products such as bio-furnace oil and briquettes.
description: Engrow Carbon Energy Private Limited is an India-based biochar producer incorporated in May 2019 and registered in Erode, Tamil Nadu. The company converts biomass residues into energy and soil amendments via pyrolysis and gasification, and its thermochemical plant generates carbon reduction credits by producing bio-furnace oil and biochar. It is named by the International Biochar Initiative among biochar producers actively scaling projects in India.

name: Enhanced rock weathering start
tech_note: Applied olivine (optimized for fast weathering) to agricultural land and used a patented direct-measurement MRV approach based on immobile trace elements in soil samples to quantify CO2 removal.
description: Eion was a U.S.-based enhanced rock weathering (ERW) company known for pioneering olivine-based deployments and an early track record of technical innovation, including some of the first issued ERW credits. In February 2026, ERW firm Terradot acquired Eion, including its commitment to deliver 8,000 tons of carbon removal credits to Microsoft under a deal signed in 2024. Eion's assets, IP, team, and contracts are now integrated into Terradot.

name: Enrzi
tech_note: Enrzi operates a biomass pyrolysis process to produce biochar and other bio-based products as a soil amendment and carbon sequestration solution.
description: Enrzi is an India-based company using biomass pyrolysis to convert organic feedstock into biochar, which they market as a soil amendment with carbon sequestration benefits. Their website is live and describes biochar as a carbon-rich, porous material from their pyrolysis process. Public signals beyond their website are limited — Coresignal shows 0 LinkedIn employees and no registry-listed credits, suggesting a small, early-stage operation.

name: EnviraPAC
tech_note: Operates a high-temperature pyrolysis facility in Monticello, Arkansas that converts soft yellow pine sawmill residuals into biochar (enviraChar for agriculture) and renewable carbon powders (enviraCarb for industrial applications such as rubber, plastics, paints, and drilling fluids).
description: EnviraPAC Monticello LLC is one of the largest biomass-based carbon production facilities in the US, with capacity near 20 million pounds/year, producing biochar and renewable engineered carbon powders as substitutes for petroleum-derived carbon black. The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified, affiliated with Generate Capital, and listed with the American Biochar Institute (formerly USBI). A portion of output is industrial CCU rather than permanent sequestration, but agricultural biochar applications qualify as durable CDR.

name: Envisgas
tech_note: Envigas operates industrial pyrolysis plants converting forestry residues (sawdust, shavings, wood pellets) at ~600°C into high-quality biocarbon (>90% C), pyrolysis oil, and syngas.
description: Envigas is a Swedish cleantech company that builds, owns and operates large-scale pyrolysis plants converting forest-industry residues into biocarbon, pyrolysis oil and renewable energy. Its existing Bureå facility produces ~5,000 t/yr of biocarbon and ~3,000 t/yr of pyrolysis oil, primarily supplying the metallurgical/steel industry as a fossil-coal replacement, with soil, asphalt and cement also cited as sink applications. In 2023 Outokumpu acquired a 20% stake (€9.9M), and in 2025 Envigas announced plans with Skellefteå Kraft to explore a >25,000 t/yr biocarbon facility in Hedensbyn.

name: Ephemeral
tech_note: Accelerates natural silicate rock weathering by grinding alkaline minerals and deploying them in shallow coastal ocean waters, increasing ocean alkalinity and converting CO2 into stable bicarbonates/carbonates.
description: Ephemeral Carbon is an unfunded company based in Santa Clara, United States, founded in 2023 by Josh Perfetto, operating as a provider of carbon removal solutions. The company specializes in the permanent removal of CO2 through Oceanic Enhanced Weathering, grinding alkaline rock into sand which is then deployed in ocean waters to neutralize acidity and restore marine ecosystems. It is a pre-revenue, early-stage OAE supplier focused on field trials and community engagement.

name: Equatic
tech_note: Equatic uses a patented seawater electrolysis process combined with direct air contacting to permanently sequester CO2 as dissolved bicarbonate and solid carbonate minerals, while co-producing carbon-negative hydrogen.
description: Founded in 2021, California-based Equatic has developed an electrolytic process for atmospheric carbon removal that accelerates the ocean's ability to absorb and permanently store massive amounts of carbon, while producing carbon negative hydrogen as a co-product. The company is a UCLA spin-out operating pilot plants in Los Angeles and Singapore, and is building the Equatic-1 demonstration plant in Singapore plus a planned commercial facility in Quebec with Deep Sky. In August 2025 Equatic raised $11.6 million in a Series A funding round led by Temasek Trust's C3H and Kibo Invest.

name: Equilibrium
tech_note: Operates biochar pyro-gasification facilities using invasive biomass and crop residues, plus agroforestry, regenerative agriculture, and mangrove restoration projects with proprietary dMRV.
description: Equilibrium (operating entity Climeverse Pvt. Ltd.) is an India-based full-stack carbon removal project developer running biochar, agroforestry, regenerative agriculture, and mangrove restoration projects across nine Indian states. It operates a Puro.earth-listed biochar facility (Mundargi/Murudagiri) that pyro-gasifies invasive Prosopis juliflora and corn cobs, and raised $3M seed funding in September 2025 from Kalaari Capital, Peak XV Partners, and Avaana Capital.

name: Equinor/Rolls Royce
tech_note: Liquid-solvent (amine-based, water-based absorbent) Direct Air Capture system originally developed by Rolls-Royce with CSIRO, whose IP and assets Equinor acquired in April 2024; Rolls-Royce continues as test operator at the Derby Test Bed 52 demonstrator.
description: Equinor is a Norwegian energy major that in April 2024 acquired Rolls-Royce's liquid-solvent DAC technology IP and novated the UK DESNZ-funded Project ENCORE contract, taking ownership of a demonstrator plant that has captured over 100 tonnes CO2/year at Rolls-Royce's Derby campus. The program is now an internal DAC development effort within Equinor, targeting a capture cost below USD 200/t, and sits alongside Equinor's other CDR/CCS activities (Northern Lights, RepAir, Captura).

name: Euthenia Energy Group
tech_note: Produces biochar via Beston BST-30 pyrolysis of olive-grove agricultural residues in Andalusia, Spain, issuing Puro-certified CORC credits.
description: Euthenia Energy Group operates a biochar production facility in Lucena, Andalusia (Spain), converting olive orchard agricultural waste into biochar via Beston BST-30 pyrolysis technology. The company is registered on Puro.earth, has issued CORCs under the Biochar methodology, and co-hosted the 2025 European Biochar CDR Conference in Málaga in October 2025.

name: Everest Carbon
tech_note: Everest Carbon develops a patent-pending in-field alkalinity sensor with IoT connectivity that directly measures carbonate alkalinity efflux to provide real-time MRV for Enhanced Rock Weathering projects.
description: Everest Carbon was founded in late 2022 as an ERW project developer, but at the end of 2023 its co-founders pivoted the company to commercialize its proprietary sensor. The company now sells hardware and software that enables ERW project developers to measure carbon removal in the field, aiming to reduce MRV costs by over 90%. They are a technology supplier building core removal-enabling infrastructure for the ERW pathway.

name: Evero Energy
tech_note: Evero retrofits its waste-wood biomass power plants (Ince BioPower and Mersey Bioenergy) with MHI amine-solvent carbon capture, storing biogenic CO₂ in depleted Irish Sea gas fields via the HyNet cluster.
description: Evero Energy Group Limited (previously known as Bioenergy Infrastructure Group) is a UK low-carbon waste-to-energy company partnering with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to deliver its InBECCS (Ince Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) project. The company is retrofitting CCS onto its existing Ince Biopower and Mersey Bioenergy plants, which already process over 300,000 tonnes of waste wood into renewable electricity, with the addition generating up to 400,000 tons of CDRs per annum. Its InBECCS project was listed on Puro.earth's Future Facility program in December 2025, making it the first and only UK BECCS project included in that program.

name: Evident
tech_note: Evident operates C-Capsule, a carbon removal registry and standard for durable CDR credits (Carbon Removal Units), building on its global environmental certificate registry expertise (I-RECs).
description: Evident is a global sustainability certification firm with over two decades of expertise in establishing trusted renewable energy markets. Its C-Capsule product is a standard and registry for durable Carbon Dioxide Removal that certifies only carbon that has been permanently removed from the atmosphere. The C-Capsule registry issues CDR credits through partnerships such as with Cowboy Clean Fuels and Absolute Climate, aimed at meeting quality, traceability, and verification expectations.

name: Exomad Green
tech_note: Industrial pyrolysis (~600°C, Beston BST-50 units) of hardwood sawmill residues into high-carbon biochar (86% organic C, H:C 0.24) donated to indigenous farmers, generating Puro.earth CORCs.
description: Exomad Green is the biochar/CDR division of Exomad, Bolivia's largest wood exporter. It converts hardwood forestry residues from ABT-certified sawmills into biochar via pyrolysis at Riberalta and Concepción facilities, with credits certified under Puro.earth. It is among the largest biochar CDR suppliers globally, notably signing a 1.24M-tonne 10-year offtake with Microsoft in May 2025.

name: Explocom
tech_note: Produces biochar and wood vinegar via patented pyrolysis of wood waste at an industrial facility in Harghita County, Romania, with EBC certification and Puro.earth CORC listing.
description: Explocom GK SRL is a production company of biochar-based products located in Lupeni Jud-Harghita, Romania, and its products are EBC certified. The firm is a manufacturer of organic chemicals and a producer of charcoal and bulk char, which added wood waste to its production in 2007, and through Innovation Norway financing developed biochar, wood vinegar, wood oil and cellulosic alcohol products. The company is listed as a biochar supplier on the Puro.earth registry.

name: Exterra
tech_note: Ex-situ accelerated mineral carbonation that converts asbestos mine tailings into reactive magnesium oxides (LOW process) then reacts them with CO2 to form stable carbonate minerals (ROC process), while co-producing nickel and silica byproducts.
description: Exterra Carbon Solutions is a Quebec-based cleantech company that transforms legacy asbestos mine tailings into low-carbon critical minerals (magnesium oxide, nickel concentrate, amorphous silica) while permanently mineralizing CO2. The company raised a CAD $20M Series A in May 2025 and is developing Hub I, scheduled to begin construction in 2027, which it claims will become the world's largest asbestos mitigation plant. Exterra partners with BASF, Énergir, WSP and Winsome Resources to deploy its LOW and ROC processes at industrial scale.

name: ExxonMobil
tech_note: ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions is running an in-house solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture pilot at its Baytown, Texas facility, alongside a broader CCS business built on the Denbury pipeline network.
description: ExxonMobil is a major integrated oil and gas company whose Low Carbon Solutions division operates a proprietary DAC pilot (started February 2024 in Baytown, TX) after ending its partnership with Global Thermostat. The division also runs large-scale point-source CCS operations leveraging Denbury's CO2 pipeline infrastructure, with CEO Darren Woods calling DAC the "holy grail" of emissions technologies while targeting a 50% cost reduction from the current $600-$1,000/ton range.

name: FETZER Rohstoffe + Recycling
tech_note: Operates three pyrolysis plants producing ~1,500 m³/year of biochar from wood chips and spelt husks under the "Moola" brand, with waste heat reused in the adjacent recycling facility.
description: FETZER Rohstoffe + Recycling GmbH is a German recycling company based in Eislingen that has been producing biochar from wood waste for over a decade under its Moola brand. EBC-certified since 2013, its three pyrolysis plants produce around 1,500 m³ of biochar per year, which is primarily sold as a soil amendment. Biochar credits are offered via marketplaces such as Klimate.

name: FS
tech_note: FS captures fermentation CO2 from its corn-ethanol biorefinery in Lucas do Rio Verde (Mato Grosso, Brazil) and injects it ~800m+ underground into the Diamantino formation for permanent geological storage.
description: FS Agrisolutions Indústria de Biocombustíveis Ltda is a joint venture between Summit Brazil Renewables (a subsidiary of Summit Agricultural Group) and Tapajós Participações and is Brazil's largest corn-based ethanol producer. The BECCS project will prevent the release of approximately 423,000 tons of CO2 into the atmosphere per year from operations in Lucas do Rio Verde, with construction expected to start once licensing approvals are granted and CO2 injection operations targeted to begin by July 2026. FS has signed forward credit sale agreements with Pinheiro Neto Advogados, SLB, and Rubicon Carbon & YvY Capital, with the credits classified as removal credits under the Gold Standard methodology.

name: FabricNano/Veolia
tech_note: Immobilizes carbonic anhydrase enzyme onto large-particle basalt/silicate rock to catalytically accelerate enhanced rock weathering on agricultural land.
description: FabricNano is a London-based biotechnology startup that develops enzyme-immobilization technology, most notably applying the carbonic anhydrase enzyme to basalt rock fines to accelerate enhanced rock weathering. In partnership with Veolia UK, the company ran a world-first field trial near Bicester (UK) spreading enzyme-coated basalt on farmland to accelerate CO2 sequestration from decades to a few years. The firm also applies its enzyme platform to non-CDR applications (bio-manufacturing with Ginkgo/Sumitomo, PFAS research), so CDR is one of multiple product lines.

name: Fasera Holdings
tech_note: Fasera pyrolyzes spent eucalyptus biomass (left over from steam distillation of eucalyptus oil from mallee plantations) to produce biochar and wood vinegar, generating CORCs under Puro.earth and ACCUs from associated plantings.
description: Fasera Holdings is an Australian company that operates oil mallee plantations in Western Australia, producing eucalyptus oil, biochar, and wood vinegar. Its biochar is listed as a Puro.earth supplier (Fasera Biochar Plant 1) and it also generates Australian Carbon Credit Units from its plantations.
