CDR is a core integrated product line alongside eucalyptus oil, qualifying it as a supplier.

name: Fidelis
tech_note: Parent company of AtmosClear, which is developing a biomass-fired power plant with post-combustion CO2 capture (BECCS) in Baton Rouge, with CO2 transported and stored via ExxonMobil's Class VI wells; also develops Norne CO2 storage hub in Denmark and Capio CCS services.
description: Fidelis (Fidelis New Energy, LLC) is a Houston-based energy infrastructure developer whose portfolio company AtmosClear is building an $800M BECCS facility at the Port of Greater Baton Rouge, Louisiana, designed to capture 680,000 tonnes of biogenic CO2 per year starting in 2029. In April 2025 AtmosClear signed a 15-year, 6.75M-tonne CDR offtake with Microsoft — the largest permanent carbon removal deal to date — and in September 2025 selected ExxonMobil for CO2 transport and storage. Fidelis also develops related CDR/CCS infrastructure including the Norne Carbon Storage Hub in Denmark and Capio Sequestration.

name: Fiora Mara
tech_note: Fiora Mara cultivates seaweed in biodegradable open-ocean farms and sinks the biomass to the deep seafloor for long-term carbon sequestration.
description: Fiora Mara is developing ocean-based carbon removal systems by deploying regenerative seaweed farms designed to sequester atmospheric CO₂. The approach leverages large-scale, biodegradable cultivation arrays to grow fast-growing macroalgae such as kelp, and once matured the biomass is transported and sequestered in the deep ocean. The company is an early-stage US startup founded in 2024 that aims to generate revenue by selling high-integrity carbon credits.

name: First Climate
tech_note: Carbon project developer, financier, and credit marketer specialising in biochar and nature-based removal credits — they do not operate removal hardware themselves but certify and offtake credits from partner pyrolysis and forestry projects.
description: First Climate is a 25-year-old German/Swiss carbon management services firm that develops, finances, sources, certifies, and markets verified emission reduction and carbon removal credits (especially biochar) from partner projects worldwide, alongside climate strategy consulting and green energy procurement. They do not operate removal technology themselves — e.g., the CARBONITY biochar plant in Canada uses Airex Energy pyrolysis technology, with First Climate acting as the offtake/certification/marketing partner. CDR project development is a core part of their business, placing them in the CDR ecosystem as a developer/broker rather than a technology supplier.

name: Flux
tech_note: Flux crushes silicate (basalt) rock and spreads it on smallholder farmland in Kenya (and, via partnership, Cameroon) to accelerate weathering, remove atmospheric CO2, and boost crop yields, selling verified ERW removal credits.
description: Flux is a Nairobi-based climate startup that has sold Africa's first carbon dioxide removal credits based on the practice of using crushed basalt to absorb CO2, pre-selling credits for 540 tons of CO2 removal via enhanced rock weathering. Flux is working to unlock the potential of ERW across Africa, aiming to sequester hundreds of millions of tonnes of CO2 while improving soils and yields for millions of farmers across the continent. The company has also signed on to work with African Food Security on a 205,000-hectare maize farming project in Cameroon.

name: Forge Minerals
tech_note: Forge Minerals operates a low-energy reactor that reacts waste CO2 with feedstocks to produce high-purity carbonate mineral products (starting with magnesium carbonate) as a permanent mineralization storage pathway.
description: Forge Minerals was founded in 2024 in Edinburgh to turn waste CO2 into high-quality mineral products that can directly replace carbon-intensive materials used across industry, focusing on displacement of carbon-intensive materials with substantially lower embedded emissions. At the heart of their technology is a low-energy reactor that permanently stores CO2 by converting it into valuable mineral products, displacing emissions in downstream industries such as pharmaceuticals, construction, and chemicals. The company recently opened its first laboratory at the Edinburgh Innovation Hub and is using pre-seed funding to support lab and pilot-scale trials toward initial commercial deployment.

name: Forward
tech_note: Svante manufactures solid-sorbent nanoengineered filters (using metal-organic frameworks/CALF-20) and rotary adsorption machines (RAM) for post-combustion point-source carbon capture and direct air capture, and is developing BECCS projects via its Carbon Alpha acquisition.
description: Svante Inc. (website tagline "Forward-Thinking Carbon Capture") is a Vancouver/Burnaby-based carbon capture technology company that builds solid-sorbent filters and rotary contactor machines for industrial point-source CCS, BECCS and DAC. In May 2025 it commissioned its Redwood gigafactory in Burnaby and acquired Carbon Alpha, adding the North Star BECCS project which signed a 626,000-tonne CDR offtake with Microsoft. It also supplies filters to Climeworks and is partnering with Nikkiso on Canada's first DAC facility.

name: Freres Lumber
tech_note: Freres operates a 100% biomass-fired cogeneration boiler at its Lyons, Oregon wood-products mill; biochar is recovered as a byproduct and sold as Puro.earth-certified CORCs.
description: Freres Lumber (Freres Engineered Wood) is a family-owned Oregon manufacturer of plywood, veneer, and Mass Ply engineered wood products whose biomass cogeneration facility produces biochar as a byproduct. The biochar project is registered on Puro.earth and has supplied CORCs to Microsoft via ACT Group. Biochar is a secondary revenue line to the core lumber business, but the firm is a bona fide supplier of durable carbon removal credits.

name: Freshean
tech_note: Develops a nano-engineered solid sorbent ("Nano-in-Nano" platform) for Direct Air Capture, with an HVAC-integrated DAC + chemical filter product aimed at semiconductor fabs and office buildings.
description: Freshean is a Phoenix, Arizona nanotechnology startup founded in 2017 by Dr. Xiwang Qi, developing a nano-engineered solid sorbent for Direct Air Capture alongside indoor air pollution solutions. The company claims a proprietary "Nano-in-Nano" platform for improved CO2 capture efficiency and cost, and participated in the Venture for ClimateTech Cohort 4 in mid-2024 and presented at SEMICON West 2024. Per Tracxn (March 2026), Freshean remains unfunded, with minimal LinkedIn footprint (1 employee), suggesting it is an early-stage R&D/licensing outfit rather than an operating removal supplier.

name: Frontier Infrastructure Holdings
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from ethanol refineries, transports via rail (Union Pacific), and permanently sequesters it in a Class VI well at the Sweetwater Carbon Storage Hub in Wyoming.
description: Frontier Infrastructure Holdings is a Tailwater Capital-backed developer of low-carbon infrastructure across the US Mountain West and Texas, specializing in BECCS by capturing biogenic CO2 from ethanol refineries and transporting it via rail to its Sweetwater Carbon Storage Hub in Wyoming for permanent geologic sequestration. The company has signed offtake deals (e.g. 120,000 tonnes with Wild Assets) and partnerships with Baker Hughes, Gevo/Verity, and Union Pacific.

name: Funga
tech_note: Funga inoculates tree seedlings and forest soils with native mycorrhizal fungal communities (identified via DNA sequencing and ML) to accelerate tree growth and carbon sequestration in working forests, primarily loblolly pine in the southeastern US.
description: Funga is a public benefit corporation focused on restoring the power of fungal biodiversity to working forests, thereby accelerating tree growth and carbon drawdown. They operate forest microbiome restoration projects in the southeastern US loblolly pine belt and sell nature-based carbon removal credits to corporate buyers. In November 2024 Funga secured its first major deal to deliver more than 500,000 tons of carbon removal to a major corporate buyer.

name: Förvaltnings AB Helje
tech_note: On-site pyrolysis of biomass to produce biochar that is mixed into potting/growing substrate used for tree and shrub cultivation at a commercial plant nursery.
description: Förvaltnings AB Helje is a Swedish property/holding company associated with Heljesgården in Essunga, which houses Essunga Plantskola's biochar production facility (built 2022). Biochar is produced primarily for use in the nursery's own peat-reduced growing substrate, with carbon-removal credits listed on the Global-C Registry. It is a small side-business of a family-owned plant nursery group (Esstella Group).

name: GE Vernova
tech_note: Solid sorbent direct air capture using temperature/pressure/concentration swing desorption, developed at GE Vernova's Advanced Research Centers.
description: GE Vernova is a publicly traded global energy company (NYSE: GEV) whose DAC program, run out of its Advanced Research Centers in Niskayuna, NY and Bengaluru, India, is developing proprietary solid-sorbent direct air capture technology. The company commissioned a 10-ton/year DAC test facility in New York and in September 2025 announced a partnership with Deep Sky to deploy a 1,500 tonne/year DAC unit at Deep Sky Alpha in Innisfail, Alberta, with operations scheduled to begin in late 2026.

name: Gaia
tech_note: Gaia is retrofitting amine-based carbon capture onto Vestforbrænding's waste-to-energy plant in Glostrup, Denmark, capturing the biogenic fraction of flue-gas CO2 for permanent geological storage (BECCS from Energy-from-Waste).
description: Gaia is a joint venture between Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP, via its Energy Transition Fund) and Danish municipal waste-to-energy operator Vestforbrænding, developing a full-scale CCS facility aiming to capture up to 500,000 tonnes of CO2 per year from 2029. The project was pre-qualified for Denmark's CCS Fund in May 2025 and signed a landmark 2.95 Mt offtake agreement with Microsoft in July 2025 for the biogenic (BECCS) portion of captured CO2.

name: Gaia Refinery
tech_note: Gaia Refinery is developing a hybrid Bio-DAC system combining liquid-solvent direct air capture with biomass carbon removal (BiCRS), using biogenic acetic acid and fuel cells to capture CO2 at low energy demand for industrial integration.
description: Halifax-based Gaia Refinery was founded in 2020 by Dr. Tammy Cai and Genny Shaw to scale up carbon removal systems. The company has developed a dual-capture process that combines biomass carbon removal (BiCRS) with direct air capture (DAC) to remove CO2 from the atmosphere and biogenic sources, designed for integration into industrial operations. They are a Canadian CDR technology developer (supplier), backed by accelerators including Brinc, Hatcher+, Kiloton Fund, and CICE's Women in Climate Tech program.

name: Geolocked
tech_note: Geolocked sequesters carbon by burying biomass and landfill waste underground for permanent storage.
description: Geolocked operates in carbon sequestration, focusing on the removal of carbon by utilizing biomass and landfill waste, which it stores underground. It is based in Houston, Texas. The company applied to Frontier's 2025 Summer prepurchase round, indicating active participation in the CDR supplier market.

name: Gevo
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from ethanol fermentation and permanently sequesters it in an onsite Class VI injection well in the Broom Creek formation in North Dakota, generating Puro.earth-certified BECCS removal credits (CORCs).
description: Gevo (NASDAQ: GEVO) is a US-based diversified bioenergy company that operates an ethanol plant in Richardton, North Dakota with an integrated BECCS system, capturing biogenic CO2 from fermentation and sequestering it in an onsite Class VI well. The site is permitted for 180K tCO2/year with capacity to scale to 1M tCO2/year, producing Puro.earth-certified CORCs. In September 2025 Gevo signed a ~$26M, 5-year CDR offtake deal with Biorecro, and made its first CORC delivery in November 2025.

name: Gevo (Red Trail Energy)
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from corn ethanol fermentation and injects it into a Class VI well more than a mile below the surface into the Broom Creek formation for permanent geologic storage.
description: Gevo North Dakota (formerly Red Trail Energy, now renamed "Net-Zero North") is an operating ethanol plant with adjacent CCS assets in Richardton, ND, acquired by Gevo in February 2025 for $210M. The CCS site, operated by Gevo subsidiary Richardton CCS, LLC (RCCS), has been sequestering biogenic CO2 since June 2022 and currently injects roughly 160,000–180,000 tonnes annually, generating BECCS credits registered on Puro.earth.

name: GigaDAC/Victory Over Carbon
tech_note: Spray-based liquid-solvent DAC contactor designed around aerospace airflow engineering to reduce build and operating costs at gigaton scale.
description: GigaDAC (legal name Victory Over Carbon Inc.) is a Houston-based DAC startup spun out of Rice Alliance and resident at Greentown Labs, developing a spray-and-aerodynamic-separator contactor to replace filter/cooling-tower designs. The company has received NSF SBIR funding and was building a commercial-scale pilot targeted for early 2025, with plans to sell removal credits and claim 45Q. Small team (~4 employees) in early R&D stage.

name: Gigablue
tech_note: Deploys engineered particles (nutrient shell + gravity-controlling core) in the ocean to stimulate phytoplankton growth and sink the resulting biomass to the deep sea for long-term carbon storage.
description: Gigablue is an ocean-based CDR startup (founded in Israel, headquartered in New York) that uses geo-specific engineered particles to grow phytoplankton and sink captured carbon to the deep ocean. It has completed multiple trials off New Zealand, signed a 200,000-ton offtake with SkiesFifty, and is pursuing a Puro.earth methodology, though its approach has drawn scientific scrutiny over parallels to iron fertilization.

name: Gigafex
tech_note: Gigafex operates proprietary pyrolysis reactors that convert palm oil mill empty fruit bunch (EFB) biomass into biochar for permanent carbon removal and soil application.
description: Gigafex helps palm oil mills turn EFB biomass into biochar and verifiable carbon removal credits using proprietary, patent-pending pyrolysis reactors purpose-built for EFB biomass that integrate into existing mill operations at industrial scale. The company markets the resulting biochar as both a stable carbon removal pathway and a soil amendment that reduces reliance on chemical fertilizers.

name: Giner
tech_note: Develops an electrochemical DAC system using KOH capture solution coupled with a hydrogen-assisted carbonate electrolyzer to regenerate purified CO2 at low voltage.
description: Giner, Inc. is a Newton, Massachusetts-based electrochemical R&D firm founded in 1973 with a broad portfolio spanning fuel cells, electrolyzers, batteries, biomedical devices, and aerospace technologies. Within that portfolio they are developing a lab-scale Direct Air Capture system that uses a concentrated KOH air contactor paired with a hydrogen-assisted carbonate electrolyzer to capture and regenerate purified CO2, a project funded through DOE's DAC Pre-Commercial Technology Prize. DAC is one of several research lines rather than the company's principal business, but Giner is building the removal technology itself rather than buying credits.

name: Glanris
tech_note: Glanris pyrolyzes rice husks into Biocarbon® biochar that functions as a dual-function water filtration medium (removing metals and organics) while sequestering carbon durably.
description: Glanris specializes in the production of biocarbon biochar, with offerings including biochar for water filtration and soil enhancement, as well as an additive in cement and concrete, all derived from processed agricultural waste such as rice husks. It was founded in 2018 and is based in Olive Branch, Mississippi. Its Biocarbon filtration biochar was declared net CO2 negative via a Life Cycle Assessment with Accend, a Puro.Earth partner, and was added to the Puro.Earth CORC exchange.

name: GoBiochar
tech_note: Bulk biochar supply, consulting, and distribution for agricultural and soil regeneration applications, sourcing customer-specific biochar across multiple feedstocks.
description: GoBiochar LLC is a Salt Lake City, Utah-based biochar supply and consulting company that sources and distributes bulk biochar to agriculture, climate tech, and heavy industry clients across North America. Founded and led by John Webster (also Development Director for Biochar On Site and former Communications Director at US Biochar Initiative), the firm produces customer-specific biochar across a range of feedstocks and supports projects from concept to delivery. Their focus is primarily agricultural/soil amendment with carbon sequestration co-benefits rather than explicit CDR credit issuance.

name: Goal 300
tech_note: Applies finely crushed basalt to agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering, capturing CO₂ as stable bicarbonates while improving soil pH and fertility.
description: Goal 300 is a US-based (Oregon/Pacific Northwest) Enhanced Rock Weathering supplier that partners with landowners to apply crushed basalt to agricultural soils to sequester CO₂ and generate carbon credits. The company is focused on removing legacy greenhouse gas emissions through Enhanced Rock Weathering in the Pacific Northwest USA and claims the largest active carbon removal project in Washington State. It is a very small operation (1 employee on Coresignal) with no public registry-listed credits yet.

name: Grain Ecosystem
tech_note: Digital platform providing project development software, financing tools, and equipment selection workflows for biochar/waste-to-value operators — not a physical biochar producer.
description: Grain Ecosystem was a Boston-based digital platform (founded 2022) providing software and workflows for biochar project developers, connecting operators, investors, and equipment manufacturers in the voluntary carbon market. It did not physically produce biochar itself — it offered financing tools, equipment selection software, and project development infrastructure. In April 2026, Mangrove Systems acquired select operating assets from Grain Ecosystem, folding its operator customer base onto Mangrove's MRV platform.

name: Graphyte
tech_note: Graphyte compresses waste biomass from timber/agriculture into dried, wrapped blocks ("Carbon Casting") and stores them in engineered underground vaults for durable (1,000+ year) CO2 sequestration.
description: Graphyte is a US-based carbon removal supplier backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Prelude Ventures and Carbon Direct Capital that operates Project Loblolly in Pine Bluff, Arkansas, and is developing Project Ponderosa in Arizona. It delivers biomass-burial CDR credits to buyers including American Airlines, JPMorganChase (60,000 tons over 10 years), and Frontier, targeting sub-$100/ton durable removal.

name: Grassroots Biochar
tech_note: Small-scale biochar producer on Öland, Sweden, using Kon-Tiki flame-curtain kilns to pyrolyze biomass into biochar sold as a soil amendment for agriculture and gardening.
description: Grassroots Biochar AB is a small Swedish company based on Öland that manufactures, refines and innovates biochar products, offering charged and activated biochar for soil management, fertilizing, water holding, filtration and decontamination. The company uses the Kon-Tiki method and is focused on the agricultural/gardening market in Sweden, without any listed carbon-sink registry certifications.

name: Grassroots Carbon
tech_note: Partners with U.S. ranchers to implement regenerative grazing practices that sequester atmospheric carbon in grassland soils, measured via deep soil sampling and sold as certified soil carbon credits.
description: Founded in 2021, Grassroots Carbon is a U.S. company dedicated to measuring, verifying, and rewarding ranchers for storing carbon on America's grasslands, now spanning 2 million acres across 22 states. They generate soil carbon removal credits through regenerative grazing practices and have delivered credits to buyers including Nestlé, Microsoft, Shopify, and Chevron.

name: Great Carbon Valley
tech_note: Project developer and systems integrator assembling DAC+S hubs (technology partners + geothermal power + basalt mineralization storage) in Kenya's Great Rift Valley.
description: Great Carbon Valley (GCV) is a Kenyan project development venture and systems integrator, founded in 2023 by Bilha Ndirangu and James Irungu Mwangi, working to build DAC+storage hubs in the Great Rift Valley by aggregating land, geothermal/renewable power, basalt mineralization storage, and DAC technology partners. GCV has signed agreements with Climeworks, Sirona Technologies, Yama, AspiraDAC, Beyond Captur, Cella, and Carbfix, targeting 1 million tonnes/year of CO2 removal by 2030 with first plants planned from 2026-2028. Although GCV does not build capture hardware itself, it is the project developer/operator assembling the removal facilities, which places it on the supplier side of the market.

name: Green Carbon
tech_note: Green Carbon develops nature-based carbon credit projects, including industrial-scale biochar carbon removal projects in India and Thailand (converting agricultural and forestry residues into biochar), alongside rice paddy methane reduction, forest conservation, mangrove afforestation, and livestock projects across Japan and Southeast Asia.
description: Green Carbon Inc. is a Tokyo-based developer of nature-based carbon credits founded in 2019, operating in Japan, Southeast Asia, Australia, and South America. Its CDR-relevant activity centers on biochar projects — notably a partnership with Excellent Enfab in India targeting Isometric-certified biochar carbon removal (~18,000 t CO2/yr per plant) and an MOU with the Rubber Authority of Thailand for biochar from rubber trees. The company also develops agriculture/forestry J-Credits and operates the NCCX blockchain credit exchange.

name: Green Carbon Products
tech_note: Small Ontario-based producer of biochar from sustainably sourced clean wood via pyrolysis, sold as soil amendment, compost additive, and animal bedding.
description: Green Carbon Products provides sustainable wood reduction and biochar supply services, with an approach that amends soil and ensures minimal disruption to the environment. Their biochar is crafted from wood in Ontario using sustainable methods, aimed at gardeners and environmentalists. The company appears to be a small retail/agricultural biochar supplier with no publicly evident carbon credit registry issuances.

name: Green Carbon Solutions
tech_note: GCS operates a pyrolysis facility in Indiantown, Florida that converts eucalyptus wood into high-carbon biochar (~95% C), with secondary bio-oil sequestration in geologic formations and bio-energy co-products.
description: Green Carbon Solutions is a renewable bio-carbon manufacturing company focused on large-scale production of sustainable engineered bio-carbon, bio-oil, and bio-energy, leveraging proprietary design-build-operate technology to decarbonize industrial supply chains and deliver CO₂ removal solutions. Led by Martin Ellis in Indiantown, Florida, the company uses pyrolysis to transform eucalyptus wood into high-quality biochar and activated carbon. A March 2025 tour highlighted its 110-foot retort processing eucalyptus wood into biochar for silicon chipmakers, with plans by 2029 to enrich soil, purify water, and generate electricity.

name: Green Golf Carbon
tech_note: Deploys a patented silicate-based soil amendment as a replacement for top-sands on golf courses, remineralizing soils while driving enhanced rock weathering for CO2 removal.
description: Green Golf Carbon is a Miami-based startup founded in 2024 that applies enhanced rock weathering soil amendments to golf courses and managed turf to sequester atmospheric CO2. It is led by co-founder/CEO Brian Morrison and has participated in the Greenshot Accelerator and presented at CERAWeek 2025.

name: Green Man Char
tech_note: Continuous slow pyrolysis of local woody waste biomass via Earth Systems CharMaker CPP500 technology producing biochar and wood vinegar.
description: Green Man Char is an Australian biochar producer operating at the Yarra Ranges Council biochar facility in Lysterfield, Victoria, using Earth Systems' CharMaker continuous pyrolysis technology to convert local woody waste into biochar and wood vinegar. The facility was commissioned in 2023 and won the 2025 LGPro VIC Award for Environmental Sustainability. Biochar products are sold primarily as soil conditioners for horticulture and agriculture.

name: Green Sequest
tech_note: Crushes and thermoactivates antigorite serpentinite to accelerate ex-situ enhanced rock weathering, spreading it on agricultural soils to remove CO2 while serving as a magnesium fertilizer.
description: Green Sequest is a Polish startup (founded 2022, based in Nasławice) developing an Enhanced Rock Weathering technology based on antigorite serpentinite, a magnesium-rich rock that permanently mineralizes CO2. They also commercialize a serpentinite-based fertilizer ("Green Mag Balance") approved by the Polish Ministry of Agriculture, and have participated in accelerators such as Carbon Removal ClimAccelerator and Google Startups for Sustainable Development.

name: Green State Biochar
tech_note: Small-scale pyrolysis of local waste wood into biochar, sold directly to farmers and used in on-farm filtration systems for manure/runoff management in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom.
description: Green State Biochar is a family-run Vermont biochar producer based in Greensboro Bend, making biochar from locally sourced waste wood for soil amendment, manure management, and runoff filtration. The company operates a homemade pyrolysis kiln producing a few hundred pounds per day and sells in buckets and supersacks to farmers, consumers, and researchers.

name: GreenCap Solutions
tech_note: Develops zeolite-based solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture technology, using physical adsorption followed by thermal desorption to capture and liquefy CO2 for storage or industrial use.
description: GreenCap Solutions AS is a Norwegian environmental technology provider of carbon dioxide removal solutions, applying Direct Air Capture technology to closed greenhouse systems and industrial applications. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Sandnes, Norway, the company is also the DAC technology provider to Removr, a joint venture 60% owned by Vanir Green Industries and 40% owned by GreenCap Solutions, which aims to build a 1-million-ton solid sorbent DAC plant.

name: GreenCarbonFactory
tech_note: Pyrolysis of clean woodchips into EBC-certified biochar plus co-produced green heat and electricity at small-scale on-site facilities.
description: GreenCarbonFactory is an Arnhem-based Dutch sustainable technology company founded by Jerom van Roosmalen and Harold Joanknecht that operates small-scale biochar and green-energy facilities at client sites. They convert certified clean (White Listed, PEFC/FSC) woodchips into biochar and heat/electricity via thermal pyrolysis, serving as a Managed Service Provider for site partners.

name: GreenChar Climate Solutions
tech_note: GreenChar develops biochar carbon removal projects in China by partnering with pyrolysis manufacturers that convert agricultural, food, forestry, and manure waste into biochar, and issues internationally certified biochar carbon removal credits with integrated MRV.
description: GreenChar Climate Solutions is a Singapore-headquartered biochar project developer operating across China that transforms organic waste into biochar and sells internationally verified biochar carbon removal credits under standards including Puro.Earth, Verra, Isometric, EBC, and CSI. The company was endorsed by Carbon Standards International as an Artisan C-Sink Manager in September 2025 and serves as the carbon accounting and certification partner for the Yangtze Delta Biochar-Based Zero-Carbon Countryside Collaborative Initiative.

name: GreenGlow
tech_note: GreenGlow operates pyrolysis facilities in Southeast Asia that convert agricultural and forestry biomass residues into biochar for soil application and durable carbon removal, issuing CORCs via Puro.earth.
description: GreenGlow is a Malaysia-based biochar producer converting Southeast Asian biomass waste into biochar, renewable energy, and carbon removal credits. In September 2025 it signed a 50,000+ ton CORC offtake agreement with Swiss CDR financier Altitude, verified through Puro.earth.

name: Greenlyte Carbon Technologies
tech_note: Low-temperature liquid-sorbent DAC that converts captured CO2 to salt then uses electrolysis to yield concentrated CO2 and hydrogen streams for CDR or synthesis into e-fuels.
description: Greenlyte Carbon Technologies is a German DAC company founded in 2022, headquartered in Essen, that has developed a liquid-sorbent Direct Air Capture process which co-produces green hydrogen alongside captured CO2. The company operates both CDR (via a partnership with Deep Sky in Quebec) and CCU pathways (DAC-to-eMethanol, DAC-to-SAF, DAC-to-SNG), with its first LiquidSolar SNG plant inaugurated in Duisburg in November 2025 and a 500-ton commercial module planned at Chempark Marl in 2026.

name: Groh Land Air & Water
tech_note: Applies biochar (along with microbes, biopolymers, and nanobubbles) to soils and water systems for agricultural improvement, water treatment, and ecosystem restoration.
description: Groh Land Air & Water is a Wisconsin-based environmental services company that uses biochar as one of several natural tools for sustainable agriculture, water treatment, and ecosystem restoration. They describe biochar as a porous charcoal-like substance created through pyrolysis that sequesters carbon and improves soil health. They are a member of the US Biochar Initiative but there is no public evidence of CDR credit issuance or registry activity.

name: Ground Up
tech_note: Ground Up operates industrial biochar production hubs in India, using pyrolysis to convert agricultural crop residues into biochar-based fertilizers that sequester carbon in soil while improving farm productivity.
description: Ground Up is a Mumbai-based startup founded in 2024 by Shanay Jhaveri, Rhea Dabriwala and Naveen Shivalingam, developing industrial biochar production hubs that convert agricultural residues into high-quality biochar using advanced pyrolysis technology, aiming to eliminate open-field burning and produce a carbon-rich soil amendment. Its latest funding round was a Seed round on May 21, 2025, and the company has joined the Carbon Business Council coalition of carbon management startups.

name: Groundwork BioAg
tech_note: Applies mycorrhizal fungi inoculants to croplands to accelerate permanent soil carbon sequestration via Mineral-Associated Organic Matter (MAOM) formation, generating Verra VM0042 soil-carbon removal credits.
description: Groundwork BioAg is an Israeli bioagriculture company producing mycorrhizal fungi inoculants (Rootella®) that, when applied to croplands, catalyze the formation of Mineral-Associated Organic Matter (MAOM) for durable soil carbon sequestration. Their Rootella Carbon® program generates Verra VM0042-verified CDR credits, with a September 2025 collaboration with Anew Climate to commercialize 500,000 tCO2e of mycorrhizal CDR credits over three years. They are an active CDR supplier, not a buyer.

name: Groupe Bordet
tech_note: French industrial producer of biochar, activated carbon, charcoal, and bio-oil via slow pyrolysis of wood from local sawmill residues, with Puro.earth-certified carbon removal credits.
description: Groupe Bordet is a French industrial group transforming wood into charcoal, based in Leuglay, Burgundy since 1860, producing a locally-sourced plant-based charcoal with over 90% carbon content. Its biochar production has been certified by Puro.earth with support from Carbonapp, and the group is investing over €30M in a new plant in Decize (Nièvre), operational in Q1 2027, to add 15,000 tonnes of biochar capacity (from 4,200 t today) and develop bio-oil, aiming for 60,000 tonnes of biochar by 2030.

name: HEMPALTA
tech_note: Generates carbon credits from industrial hemp cultivation plus biochar application on a global farm network, with its own MRV methodology and blockchain registry (Trusted Carbon) via subsidiary Hemp Carbon Standard.
description: Hempalta Corp. (TSXV: HEMP) is a Calgary-based company that pivoted in 2025 from hemp processing to a nature-based carbon removal program built around industrial hemp cultivation and biochar application via its wholly owned subsidiary Hemp Carbon Standard (HCS). It also operates a proprietary blockchain-based registry called Trusted Carbon, and sells verified credits via Cloverly and brokers. The company wound down its own hemp/biochar processing plant in September 2025 and now works through a global network of farms to generate credits under ISO 14064-2 and Puro.earth.

name: Hafslund Celsio
tech_note: Hafslund Celsio is building a full-scale post-combustion amine-based carbon capture plant at its Klemetsrud waste-to-energy facility in Oslo, with liquefaction and ship transport to Northern Lights for permanent sub-seabed storage; ~60% of captured CO2 is biogenic, yielding BECCS removals.
description: Hafslund Celsio is Norway's largest district heating supplier and operator of the country's largest waste-to-energy plant at Klemetsrud, Oslo. It is a partly-owned subsidiary within the Hafslund/Infranode/HitecVision consortium developing a flagship BECCS project under Norway's Longship program, with FID reached in January 2025 and operations targeted for Q3 2029. The project has secured major CDR offtakes including a 10-year, 1.1 Mt deal with Microsoft and a Frontier prepay.

name: Hago Energetics
tech_note: Converts organic waste (cow manure, agricultural residues, landfill gas, wastewater byproducts) into fuel-cell-grade green hydrogen via biomethane pyrolysis, producing biochar as a carbon-sequestering co-product used as soil amendment.
description: Hago Energetics is a California-based startup (founded 2017) developing a carbon-negative hydrogen process that strips hydrogen from biomethane and deposits the carbon as biochar. EcoEngineers' third-party LCA validated strongly negative carbon intensity (as low as -492 gCO2e/MJ with biochar sequestration). The company was selected as a Qualified Hydrogen Supplier by First Public Hydrogen Authority in January 2026 and has won DOE, CEC, NASA and NYSERDA awards.

name: Haliburton Forest Biochar
tech_note: Pyrolysis of sustainably harvested hardwood sawmill residues to produce biochar for soil amendment and as a fossil-carbon-black substitute in advanced manufacturing.
description: Haliburton Forest Biochar is a joint venture/subsidiary of Haliburton Forest & Wild Life Reserve Ltd. in central Ontario, Canada, producing high-quality biochar from sustainably harvested hardwood sawmill residues via proprietary pyrolysis. Products serve soil amendment and advanced manufacturing applications (e.g., as a fossil carbon-black replacement). The company received a $4.6M Ontario provincial investment announced in 2025 to scale engineered biochar production.

name: Happy Ground
tech_note: Happy Ground converts Thai agricultural residues (rice, sugarcane, coconut, rubber) into biochar and biochar-enhanced fertilizers, deploying them with smallholder farmers and tracking carbon removal via an IoT/satellite traceability platform.
description: Happy Ground is a Thailand-based biochar CDR supplier working with smallholder farmers to turn agricultural residues into carbon removal, avoiding open-field burning and PM2.5 pollution. It is developing a large-scale project across 100,000 hectares with 10,000 farmers, is in certification with Carbon Standards International, and targets Puro.earth-aligned verification. The company also operates an insetting/traceability platform for corporate Scope 3 reporting.

name: Harvestone
tech_note: Operates three corn ethanol biorefineries and captures biogenic fermentation CO2 for permanent sequestration via Class VI injection wells (BECCS).
description: Harvestone Low Carbon Partners (HLCP), a portfolio company of Energy Capital Partners formed in 2022, owns three Midwest ethanol biorefineries (Blue Flint and Dakota Spirit in North Dakota; Iroquois Bio-Energy in Indiana) producing ~220 million gallons/year. Blue Flint began sequestering biogenic CO2 in October 2023 via an on-site Class VI injection well — the third U.S. biorefinery to do so and the first post-IRA — and HLCP is developing similar CCS at Dakota Spirit (including a trucking-based transport plan) under its Vision Carbon Zero initiative.

name: Heirloom
tech_note: Heirloom accelerates the natural carbonation of calcined limestone to capture atmospheric CO2, then stores the CO2 permanently underground (Class VI wells) or mineralized in concrete.
description: Heirloom is a U.S. Direct Air Capture company that uses limestone (calcium oxide/carbonate) as a solid sorbent to pull CO2 from the atmosphere. It operates North America's first commercial DAC facility in Tracy, California, and is building two additional DAC facilities in Northwest Louisiana, including a contribution to the DOE-funded Project Cypress DAC Hub.

name: HerbaCarbo
tech_note: Pyrolytic carbonization of plant biomass (including herbal pomace from medicinal-plant extraction) into EBC-certified biochar sold as plant carbon and feed carbon.
description: HerbaCarbo GbR is a production company of biochar-based products located in Andernach, Germany, with products sold under the HerbaCarbo brand. They produce EBC-certified biochar from biomass including herbal pomace and woodchips via pyrolysis at 500–700°C, marketed for Terra Preta soil applications and as a feed additive. The company is a small, family-run GbR that has been operating since ~2015.

name: High Hopes Labs
tech_note: High Hopes Labs is developing high-altitude balloon-based cryogenic direct air capture, freezing CO2 out of stratospheric air at ~-80°C and returning it to ground for sequestration or use.
description: High Hopes Labs is an Israeli startup based in central Israel that develops carbon-catching balloons intended to capture frozen CO2 roughly 9 miles above Earth at stratospheric altitudes. The company received a U.S. patent for its balloon-based capture invention, designed by CTO Eran Oren. The company is an independent startup (not a division of a larger firm) and is a genuine technology developer/supplier, though public signals of activity have been quiet since 2022.

name: Hjelmsäters Egendom
tech_note: Swedish farm estate producing EBC-certified biochar from forestry residues using BIOMACON pyrolysis technology, selling CORCs via Puro.earth.
description: Hjelmsäters Egendom is a Swedish agricultural and forestry estate in Hällekis that operates a biochar production unit (branded biokol.se) using BIOMACON pyrolysis technology fed with forestry residues. The biochar is EBC-certified and used as soil amendment in the agricultural sector, and the project generates CORCs issued through Puro.earth.

name: Hokuetsu Corporation
tech_note: Paper mill operator hosting CO2 capture on a black-liquor-fired chemical recovery boiler (biogenic source) with storage planned in depleted Niigata oil/gas fields via pipeline.
description: Hokuetsu Corporation is one of Japan's leading paper manufacturers and is the biogenic emission-source host for a BECCS project at its Niigata Mill, where CO2 from a black-liquor-fired chemical recovery boiler is being captured. It is one of four partners (with JAPEX, Tohoku Electric, and Mitsubishi Gas Chemical) in JOGMEC's Advanced CCS Project in the Higashi-Niigata area, targeting operations by 2030, and launched a CO2 capture demonstration with MHI's CO2MPACT Mobile system in November 2024.

name: Holocene
tech_note: Liquid-based, low-temperature DAC using amino acids and guanidine-based organic compounds (licensed from ORNL) that precipitate captured CO2 as a solid for regeneration and permanent geological storage.
description: Holocene is a Knoxville, Tennessee-based direct air capture startup founded in 2022 by former Climeworks engineers, using a liquid-based, low-temperature thermochemical process with amino acids and guanidine compounds (licensed from Oak Ridge National Laboratory). In September 2024 it signed a landmark $100/ton, 100,000-ton carbon removal deal with Google, and in April 2025 it was acquired by Occidental Petroleum, which is integrating the technology with its Carbon Engineering/1PointFive DAC business.

name: Hovyu
tech_note: Develops the ZEUS liquid-solvent absorption/stripping process for DAC and point-source CO2 capture, designed to release CO2 at high pressure without requiring thermal regeneration.
description: Hovyu is a Netherlands-based carbon capture engineering firm developing the ZEUS (Zero-Emission Ultra-Stripping) liquid-solvent process for Direct Air Capture, flue gas capture, and biogas upgrading. Their ZEUS technology is a flexible and scalable process to remove CO2 from industrial emissions or from air, with CO2 release proceeding at room temperature requiring no heat, which is an advantage where steam availability is constrained. They have diversified international operations with projects in the Netherlands, Norway and Brazil.

name: Husk
tech_note: Converts rice husk waste into biochar via pyrolysis at rice mills and formulates it into fertilizers for smallholder farmers, issuing EBC C-Sink removal credits.
description: Husk operates a biochar plant co-located with a rice mill, producing biochar via pyrolysis from rice husks under European Biochar Certification (EBC C-Sink) standards. The company sells biochar-based fertilizers to smallholder farmers in Cambodia and Vietnam and issues EBC C-Sink carbon removal credits. In June 2025, atmosfair and HUSK signed a contract to build a new pyrolysis plant in Kampong Thom, Cambodia, commissioning in November 2025, producing ~3 tons of biochar per day.

name: Hydrogen Naturally
tech_note: Gasifies forestry waste fibre to produce hydrogen and a pure CO2 stream, which is compressed and geologically sequestered — a BECCS-with-hydrogen pathway, not biochar.
description: Hydrogen Naturally (H2N) is a Canadian startup developing "Bright Green Hydrogen" facilities that gasify forestry residuals to co-produce hydrogen and pure CO2 for permanent underground storage. It is backed by founding partners Peak Renewables and North West Capital, and is planning hubs in Alberta's Industrial Heartland and British Columbia. In April 2025 it received a $3M grant from Emissions Reduction Alberta to advance its negative-emission hydrogen project.

name: HyveGeo
tech_note: Pyrolyzes biogenic residues into biochar "charged" with microalgae-derived biostimulants and microbes to regenerate desert soils while storing carbon.
description: HyveGeo is a UK/UAE-based climate-tech startup (founded 2023) that produces engineered biochar from agricultural and forestry residues, charged with microalgae-derived biostimulants and beneficial microbes, to regenerate arid desert soils while locking away carbon. The company operates pilots in the UAE and sells CDR credits alongside soil-regeneration products.

name: Húmica
tech_note: Húmica produces tailor-made biochar-based biofertilizers via pyrolysis and applies them to smallholder agricultural soils in Mexico, combined with regenerative agroforestry practices.
description: Húmica is a Mexican biotech startup founded in 2019–2020 that works with smallholder farmers (with a focus on women producers in Puebla, Veracruz, Tabasco, and Oaxaca) to sequester carbon through biochar production and regenerative agroforestry. The company diagnoses soils, formulates site-specific biochar recipes, and helps farmers access carbon credit markets while commercializing their crops.

name: Ibero Massa Florestal
tech_note: Produces biochar via slow pyrolysis of forest and agricultural biomass at its Oliveira de Azeméis plant in Portugal, selling agricultural Ecochar and domestic Carvão Zero, with CDR credits sold via Carbonfuture under EBC/Global C-Sink certifications.
description: Ibero Massa Florestal (IMF) is a Portuguese company focused on the production of biochar and bio-based sustainable solutions, based in Oliveira de Azeméis, transforming forest biomass through slow pyrolysis to produce Carvão Zero (a charcoal for household use) and Ecochar (a certified biochar for agriculture, forest restoration, and long-term carbon removal), with an installed capacity of 5,000 tonnes per year and certifications including EBC, GLOBAL C-SINK, FSC, and PEFC. The company sells biochar carbon removal credits through partners such as Carbonfuture.

name: InPlanet
tech_note: Applies finely crushed basalt silicate rock powder to tropical Brazilian farmland to accelerate natural weathering that converts atmospheric CO2 into stable bicarbonates.
description: InPlanet is a Brazil/Germany-based CDR supplier pioneering tropical Enhanced Rock Weathering, spreading finely crushed basalt on farmland to permanently sequester CO2 as bicarbonates while improving soil fertility. The company delivered the world's first independently verified ERW credits (via Isometric) and in December 2025 signed a deal with Microsoft for 28,500+ tonnes to be delivered 2026-2028.

name: Indigo
tech_note: Enrolls US farmers in regenerative agriculture practices (cover crops, reduced tillage) and issues registry-verified agricultural soil carbon removal credits through the Climate Action Reserve's Soil Enrichment Protocol.
description: Indigo Ag is a US-based sustainable agriculture company whose Carbon by Indigo program (operated by subsidiary Indigo Carbon PBC) develops and issues agricultural soil carbon credits. Since 2018, Indigo Carbon has enrolled more than 8 million acres across 28 U.S. states and sequestered/abated approximately 2.1 million metric tons of CO₂e. Under a 12-year agreement, Microsoft will purchase 2.85 million soil carbon removal credits from Indigo.

name: Industrielle Werke Basel
tech_note: Operates a PYREG pyrolysis plant that converts green waste (wood chips, sawdust, Christmas trees) into EBC-certified biochar while generating district heat.
description: IWB (Industrielle Werke Basel) is the municipal utility of the Swiss canton of Basel-City, providing electricity, natural gas, district heat, drinking water, and telecommunications. Within the utility, IWB operates a PYREG pyrolysis plant that carbonises green waste into biochar (~550 t/year) sold to farmers and private customers, and has piloted biochar-infused "CO2-negative" asphalt. CDR is a flagship sustainability initiative but a small part of the utility's overall business.

name: Inherit
tech_note: Inherit captures biogenic CO2 from biogas production at wastewater/organic-waste facilities and sends it via Northern Lights to permanent geological storage below the North Sea seabed.
description: Inherit Carbon Solutions is a Norwegian BECCS project developer that captures biogenic CO2 from biogas plants processing wastewater and agricultural organic waste and permanently stores it under the North Sea. In March 2026 it entered operation with what it describes as the world's first carbon removal project from biogas, delivering Puro.earth-certified credits to buyers including Microsoft, DNV and Nordea.

name: Inkan Negro
tech_note: Peruvian company producing biochar soil amendments from agricultural and urban green waste biomass, with applications in soil remediation, agriculture, and mine reclamation.
description: Inkan Negro is a Peruvian-owned company that manufactures and sells its own ecologically sustainable biochar soil amendment, based on over 10 years of scientific research conducted in Peru. They produce biochar by converting urban green and agricultural wastes into an optimized soil amendment that improves soil structural properties and fertility. The company has engaged with Puro.earth through a Pre-CORC biochar project.

name: Inkoh
tech_note: Inkoh operates a Biomacon pyrolysis reactor in Maienfeld, Switzerland that converts untreated forest waste wood into biochar for soil amendment, animal feed additive, and climate concrete (KLARK), while also supplying heat and issuing CO2 certificates.
description: Inkoh AG is a Swiss biochar producer that has operated a pyrolysis plant in Maienfeld since May 2020, capable of producing approximately 450 tons of biochar per year from forest waste wood. The company sells biochar directly and as substrate mixtures (including tree-pit substrates for sponge-city applications) and issues carbon removal certificates via First Climate. Swiss Post is a notable partner investing in Inkoh biochar as part of its 2040 carbon-neutral strategy.

name: InnoSepra
tech_note: InnoSepra develops a solid-sorbent-based Direct Air Capture process using physical sorbents in structured form to reduce regeneration energy below 4 GJ/tonne, alongside related post-combustion CO2 capture and biogas upgrading technologies.
description: InnoSepra, founded in 2007 by Dr. Ravi Jain and based in Middlesex, NJ, is testing its second-generation post-combustion carbon capture technology at Technology Centre Mongstad (TCM), with partial funding from the US Department of Energy. The company has received multiple DOE SBIR awards to develop a sorbent-based Direct Air Capture process, advancing a DAC process using sorbent materials with high CO2 capacities and low regeneration energy requirements. It remains an R&D-stage DAC technology developer and therefore qualifies as a supplier.

name: Inspiratus Technology
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of agricultural residues (primarily sugarcane bagasse) for soil amendment and carbon removal credits at an industrial plant in Sullana, Piura, Peru.
description: Inspiratus Technologies is a Peru-based subsidiary of Belgian Inspiratus BV (part of the Durabilis Group) that operates Peru's first industrial biochar plant, inaugurated in June 2025 in Jibito, Sullana with $3M investment and capacity to process 40,000 t/yr of agricultural residues into 10,000 t/yr of biochar. Revenue model combines carbon credits with regenerative agriculture soil amendments; also develops activated carbon applications for water decontamination and metal recovery.

name: InterEarth
tech_note: InterEarth grows coppicing native Eucalyptus/Acacia on degraded low-rainfall Australian farmland, harvests the above-ground biomass, and stores it in engineered above-ground "Dry Stack" chambers designed to maintain biomass-inert conditions for 100+ years.
description: InterEarth removes CO2 with the woody biomass burial method to store carbon captured within the biomass. Their business is harvesting, transporting and stacking dried biomass within their Dry Stack above-ground storage chamber, using woody biomass from plantation-grown native Australian Eucalyptus and Acacia trees. InterEarth lodged an Australian Provisional Patent in May 2023 and filed an International PCT in May 2024 for its Dry Stack Biomass Carbon sequestration technology.

name: Interholco
tech_note: Produces biochar from FSC-certified tropical hardwood sawmill residues at its sawmill in the Republic of Congo, applying the biochar to soils in its managed forest concession.
description: Interholco AG is a Swiss timber company (founded 1962) that manages 1.16 million hectares of FSC-certified tropical forest in the Republic of Congo via its IFO subsidiary. It operates a biochar carbon removal project converting sawmill residues into stable carbon, with C-sink certification through the EBC / Global C-Sink Registry. While timber is its core business, the biochar project is an integrated CDR supplier operation.

name: International Tie Disposal
tech_note: ITD uses slow pyrolysis in vacuum-sealed kilns (equipment from Biochar Now) to convert creosote-treated legacy railroad ties into biochar for carbon sequestration and industrial/agricultural uses.
description: International Tie Disposal (ITD), owned by North Carolina-based Polivka International, is building a biochar production facility in Richmond County, NC that pyrolyzes old creosote-treated railroad ties to produce stable biochar. Biochar Now supplied the kiln equipment and has agreed to purchase the output. The project has been tied up in permitting battles and litigation but has cleared most hurdles as of 2024.

name: Ionada
tech_note: Ionada develops containerized modular carbon capture systems based on patented hollow fiber membrane contactor (HFMC) technology using amine solvents, marketed as iDAC for direct air capture and iDeCarbon for post-combustion flue-gas capture.
description: Ionada is an Ontario, Canada-based climate technology company that in August 2025 received grant funding from the NGIF Accelerator to advance its modular carbon capture system, supporting construction and demonstration of an industrial-scale unit. In August 2025 the company announced completion and demonstration of the world's first production-scale Hollow Fiber Membrane Contactor (HFMC) carbon capture system. Its iDAC product applies the same membrane contactor technology to direct air capture, while its core commercial focus is point-source capture for natural gas, marine, hydrogen, steel, cement, and thermal power applications.

name: Isometric
tech_note: Isometric is a carbon removal registry and science/MRV platform that develops protocols, verifies CDR projects, and issues credits across pathways including enhanced weathering, biochar, DAC, and reforestation.
description: Isometric is a carbon removal registry, which in 2025 signed its 100th supplier (Flux), with suppliers spanning every major CDR pathway. In March 2025 it launched Certify, a platform that reduces the CDR verification process from years down to roughly one month. Isometric has received endorsements from ICROA, CORSIA, and ICVCM, allowing it to issue credits under the Core Carbon Principles label.

name: Italian Carbon Removal Network
tech_note: Industry association/network coordinating Italian CDR stakeholders (startups, policymakers, researchers) — not a removal supplier itself.
description: The Italian Carbon Removal Network (Rete Italiana Rimozione Carbonio, RIRC) is Italy's first dedicated national carbon removal industry network, launched on 14 April 2026 in Padova during Padova Climate Action Week in collaboration with the Negative Emissions Platform. It serves as a coordinating industry body for CDR stakeholders in Italy, analogous to France's AFEN, Germany's DVNE, and the Nordic NCRA, promoting deployment, governance, and public understanding of carbon removal.

name: Jeevan Climate Solutions
tech_note: Solid-sorbent DAC using a copper-coordinated weak-base ion-exchange resin (DeCarbonHIX) that can be regenerated with low-grade heat or seawater; captured CO2 can be sequestered as bicarbonate/baking soda.
description: Jeevan Climate Solutions is a Pennsylvania-based (Allentown/Bethlehem) DAC startup spun out of Lehigh University, founded in 2022 by Prof. Arup SenGupta. It develops DeCarbonHIX, a copper-armored ion-exchange solid sorbent that captures CO2 from air or flue gas, regenerates with low-temperature heat or seawater, and can convert CO2 to baking soda for ocean storage. The company has received DOE SBIR Phase I funding and investment from Blue Action Accelerator, Founders Factory, and Ben Franklin Technology Partners.

name: Jeffries Group
tech_note: Jeffries operates a commercial biochar plant in South Australia using Pyrocal Continuous Carbonisation Technology to pyrolyze green waste, producing biochar for soil amendment and using syngas via an ORC turbine to generate renewable energy.
description: Jeffries Group is a 180+ year-old South Australian composting and soil products family business that commissioned one of the Southern Hemisphere's largest biochar plants in 2021. The plant pyrolyzes kerbside green waste into biochar (sold as soil amendment and in pelletized CulChar fertiliser) while powering itself via ORC turbines driven by syngas. The company is a Puro.earth-listed CORC supplier, though the CDR-credit project remains in early development status.

name: Jiaxing Tongao Technology/Climate Future
tech_note: Chinese manufacturer of continuous pyrolysis equipment and operator of a Puro.earth-listed biochar carbon removal plant, converting agricultural residues into biochar for soil application and carbon sequestration.
description: Jiaxing Tongao Environmental Technology Co. Ltd. is a Chinese biochar pyrolysis technology provider that designs and supplies continuous pyrolysis systems and operates its own biochar facility listed on Puro.earth. In December 2025 it signed an MoU with Stack Carbon (Uganda) and TerraCapX (Norway) to deliver 30 tonnes/day of biochar capacity for the $12M Nile Char Carbon Removal Project in Uganda — its first international deployment.

name: Jord
tech_note: Cultivates perennial C4 grass on marginal/degraded land and pyrolyzes residues into biochar for soil sequestration, alongside producing solid biofuel pellets.
description: Jord is a Swedish company (founded 2017, HQ Stockholm) with cultivation operations in Senegal and the Dominican Republic that produces biochar and solid biofuel pellets from C4 grass grown on degraded land. The company also sells carbon credits combining avoidance and biochar-based removal. It has active 2024-2025 partnerships with Votion Biorefineries (SAF), TEXEL (electricity), and Borga (construction).

name: KORALL
tech_note: Liquid direct air capture that binds CO2 in solid form within the solvent, targeting both permanent underground storage and CO2 utilization as feedstock for e-fuels/SAF.
description: KORALL (Korall Carbon Capture AB) is a Swedish DAC startup headquartered in Gothenburg, founded in 2023, developing a novel liquid solvent DAC technology that binds captured CO2 in solid form to reduce process steps and energy use. The company targets both permanent geological storage (mineralization in bedrock) and CO2 utilization for renewable fuels, and designs plants to flex power consumption with renewable grid surplus.

name: KWS Ökokraft
tech_note: Operates a SynCraft wood-gas CHP plant in Ternitz, Austria (since 2020) that produces electricity and district heat while generating EBC-certified biochar as a byproduct via pyrolysis of forestry chips.
description: KWS Ökokraft GmbH is an Austrian company founded in 2017 that runs a 400 kW electric / 600 kW thermal wood gasification plant in Ternitz. The facility co-produces biochar (roughly 3.7 m³/day, ~1.8 t CO2/day sequestered) alongside renewable power and heat fed into the local district-heating network. It is a small owner-operated facility (3 shareholders, ~2 employees) using SynCraft technology rather than a commercial CDR-credit issuer.

name: Kairos Carbon
tech_note: Uses hydrothermal/supercritical water oxidation on wet organic wastes (manure, sewage sludge) to convert biogenic carbon to CO2 for geological sequestration, while recovering clean water and mineral fertilizer co-products.
description: Kairos Carbon is a UK-based CDR startup (incorporated April 2024) developing a supercritical water oxidation process that treats high-moisture biogenic waste streams, captures the resulting CO2 for permanent underground storage, and recovers phosphorus and other nutrients. The company is building a pilot facility and has received backing from Zero Carbon Capital, Grantham Foundation, Innovate UK, and a £1M Defra Farming Innovation grant. Milkywire's Climate Transformation Fund selected them as a 2025 CDR purchase.

name: Kanadevia Inova
tech_note: Kanadevia Inova (formerly Hitachi Zosen Inova, subsidiary of Japan's Kanadevia Corporation) is an EPC contractor that builds waste-to-energy plants with amine-scrubbing carbon capture (BECCS) and anaerobic digestion facilities that produce biochar from digestate via gasification.
description: Switzerland-based green-tech subsidiary of Kanadevia Corporation specializing in Waste-to-Energy and Renewable Gas. Currently building the UK's first full-scale WtE carbon capture facility at Protos (370,000 tCO2/yr for HyNet storage under Liverpool Bay) for Encyclis, and broke ground in 2026 on a Minnesota anaerobic digestion plant producing ~8,000 t/yr of biochar alongside RNG.

name: Kanop
tech_note: AI-powered SaaS platform using satellite imagery (optical, radar, LiDAR) and machine learning to provide MRV, baselining, and monitoring for nature-based carbon projects (afforestation/reforestation, REDD+, mangroves, agroforestry).
description: Kanop is a Paris-based MRV software company founded in 2021 that provides satellite-based monitoring, baselining, and verification services for nature-based carbon projects and corporate supply chain reporting. It supports major carbon standards including Verra, Gold Standard, Isometric, and Equitable Earth, and was recently selected by Isometric as a nature-based service partner. Kanop does not remove CO2 itself but provides the measurement infrastructure used by project developers, investors, and buyers.

name: Karbonetiq
tech_note: Karbonetiq accelerates surficial mineralization by crushing alkaline industrial residues (slags, ash) and exposing them to air/moisture via passive aeration so atmospheric CO₂ bonds into stable carbonates on-site.
description: Karbonetiq is a Santa Barbara, California-based CDR startup (founded 2022) that mineralizes CO₂ by processing alkaline industrial residues through a low-cost passive aeration system with sensor-based MRV. It was selected in Frontier's Summer 2025 prepurchase round (2,142 tons) alongside Limenet and pHathom, on behalf of Stripe, Shopify, and Google. The company is a Puro.earth registry participant and an active mineralization supplier.

name: Karbonwerke
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from biogas plants and biorefineries and sequesters it underground for permanent storage, selling carbon removal credits and long-term CO2 offtake.
description: Karbonwerke is a Swiss company that captures and stores CO2 from biogenic sources — biogas plants and biorefineries that release CO2 as a byproduct — to provide negative emissions. They offer carbon removal credits and long-term CO2 offtake to partner facilities, and also run a small advisory arm on CDR technologies.

name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries
tech_note: Solid-sorbent DAC using amine-coated porous beads that desorb CO2 at ~60°C using waste heat, with captured CO2 stored in CO2-SUICOM concrete via a partnership with Kajima.
description: Kawasaki Heavy Industries is a Japanese industrial conglomerate whose Kawasaki CO2 Capture (KCC) division develops proprietary solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture technology, originally derived from CO2 control systems for submarines and space stations. In November 2025 it commissioned one of Japan's largest DAC pilots at its Kobe Works (100–200 tCO2/yr) and has announced ambitions to scale to a 500,000–1,000,000 tCO2/yr commercial unit by 2030. It is also collaborating with Kajima Corporation to store captured CO2 in CO2-SUICOM concrete.

name: Kepler ReCapture
tech_note: Designs autonomous offshore spar platforms that combine OTEC/wave-powered desalination with CO2 extraction from air and seawater, converting captured carbon into carbonate minerals and durable materials.
description: Kepler ReCapture is a U.S.-based (Austin, TX) division of aerospace firm Kepler Shipyards, developing conceptual ocean-based floating platforms that integrate carbon-negative desalination with CO2 removal from the ocean-atmosphere system. The company was founded in 2021 as an XPRIZE Carbon Removal entrant and remains in early/pre-deployment stage, with artist renderings rather than operational systems. Multiple revenue streams are claimed including freshwater, renewable energy, carbonate minerals, and gases.

name: Kita
tech_note: Kita is a Lloyd's of London Coverholder offering specialty insurance products (Non-Delivery, Non-Payment, Political Risk, Carbon Purchase Protection Cover) for carbon and CDR market participants.
description: Kita is a Lloyd's of London Coverholder and carbon insurance specialist, a UK-based startup formed in December 2021 to insure CO2 removal credits that are often forward-purchased and carry delivery risks. Its policies provide coverage tailored to carbon and natural capital asset classes, including Delivery, Counterparty, Political and Buffer Depletion. They are part of the CDR ecosystem as a financial-infrastructure provider rather than a physical CO2 remover.

name: Klim
tech_note: Klim is a project developer and MRV provider that works with farmers to implement regenerative agriculture practices (cover cropping, reduced tillage, diverse rotations) that sequester carbon in agricultural soils, generating carbon credits and Scope 3 insetting outcomes for corporate partners.
description: Klim is a Berlin-based agritech company that scales regenerative agriculture by partnering with 3,500+ farmers across Germany, Poland, the USA, UK, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic. They act as project developer, manager, and MRV provider, offering Scope 3 insetting projects and soil-carbon credits to corporate buyers including Nestlé and ADM.

name: Klimafarmer
tech_note: Produces and markets EBC-certified biochar (klimafarmer® Pflanzenkohle »Carbon-Sink«) from untreated regional wood, plus terra preta soils, soil amendments and biochar-based fertilizers for agriculture, viticulture and horticulture.
description: Klimafarmer GmbH is a German biochar company founded in 2019 and based in Nierstein, Rhineland-Palatinate, with production activity across Rhineland-Palatinate, Hesse and North Rhine-Westphalia. It sells EBC-certified biochar products and runs "Klimawinzer" projects with wineries (e.g. Schloss Vollrads) that carbonize vine cuttings into biochar for soil application and long-term CO2 storage.

name: Klimate
tech_note: Klimate operates a CO2 asset management platform and brokerage that helps corporate buyers build and manage diversified carbon removal portfolios across biochar, BECCS, DAC, ERW, reforestation, and bio-oil projects.
description: Klimate.co is a Copenhagen-based company founded in 2020 that specializes in carbon asset management, with a platform that enables businesses to secure high-quality carbon removal solutions. Klimate buys the removal of CO2 from the atmosphere on behalf of its clients through different removal projects and combines them into portfolios, with options for custom portfolios. They are a broker/marketplace rather than a technology developer, making them part of the CDR ecosystem.

name: Kodama Systems
tech_note: Buries waste woody biomass from forest-thinning operations in engineered dryland "wood vaults" to prevent decomposition, paired with teleoperated/autonomous skidder technology for efficient feedstock collection.
description: Kodama Systems is a Sonora, California-based forest management and robotics company that thins fire-prone western US forests and sequesters the waste woody biomass in engineered underground "wood vaults." It combines teleoperated/autonomous skidder technology (Kodama Autopilot, RS1) with biomass burial CDR in partnership with the Yale Carbon Containment Lab. Backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Congruent Ventures, and a Frontier/Stripe pre-purchase for ~415 tonnes of CO2.

name: KohleHelden
tech_note: Manufactures EBC- and GMP+ certified biochar (plant charcoal and feed charcoal) from German wood via pyrolysis, sold for soil amendment and animal feed.
description: KohleHelden GmbH & Co. KG is a manufacturing company of biochar located in Zierenberg, Germany. They produce EBC- and GMP+ certified plant charcoal and feed charcoal (Pflanzenkohle and Futterkohle), sourced regionally from North Hesse near Kassel. Products are actively sold via their website and Amazon, providing a permanent biochar carbon sink for agricultural applications.

name: LOCOAL
tech_note: Builds relocatable/containerized induction-pyrolysis gasifiers (Rainmaker) that convert wood and biomass waste into biochar, syngas for electricity, and bio-oils, with cloud-based MRV (IMPCT.AI) for carbon credits.
description: LOCOAL is a US waste-to-energy and biochar company that builds the Rainmaker induction pyrolysis platform to convert biomass waste (wood, agricultural, forestry residues) into biochar, bio-oil/wood vinegar, and syngas for clean electricity. The biochar co-product sequesters carbon, and the company's IMPCT.AI software tracks carbon reductions for carbon credits. Recent 2025 blog posts and LinkedIn activity indicate the company remains operational.

name: Leilac/Calix
tech_note: Leilac builds indirectly heated electric calciners that separate pure process CO2 from limestone; the technology is licensed to Heirloom for DAC plants and applied to cement/lime process-emission capture.
description: Leilac is an Australian subsidiary of ASX-listed Calix Limited that develops indirectly heated electric calcination technology for decarbonising cement and lime production. Its CDR relevance stems from a perpetual global licence with Heirloom, whose Direct Air Capture facilities (including a 17,000 tpa Shreveport plant and a 300,000 tpa Project Cypress hub contribution) deploy Leilac's electric calciner as core hardware. Leilac also received Frontier's zero-carbon lime grant and continues projects like ZETA, Leilac-2, and two US DOE-funded pre-FEED studies.

name: Levitree
tech_note: Injects wood-chip slurry into shallow (5-100 m) subsurface apertures where anoxic conditions prevent decomposition, achieving long-duration carbon storage while raising ground elevation for flood mitigation.
description: Levitree is a San Rafael/Berkeley, California-based startup founded in 2021 that sequesters carbon by injecting wood-chip slurries 5-100 meters underground using AI-enabled robotic equipment, a technique called Subterranean Wood Injection (SWI). The process also raises the ground surface, providing a flood-protection co-benefit for infrastructure. The company was a finalist in NYU Tandon's 2025 Urban Future Prize Competition and is backed by Berkeley SkyDeck.

name: LightNET Carbon Capture
tech_note: Accelerated ex-situ mineralization of CO2 into stable carbonates via nanotech-engineered coatings (CO2atings) and ceramics (CO2rallites) using Ca/Mg oxides and industrial waste feedstocks like steel slags.
description: LightNET Carbon Capture (LNCC) is a Barcelona-based spin-off of ICN2 and CSIC that develops accelerated ex-situ CO2 mineralization technologies, turning CO2 into carbonates within coatings (CO2atings®) and advanced ceramics (CO2rallites®) using earth-abundant oxides/hydroxides and industrial waste. The company has run pilots with SACYR on construction sites, published a peer-reviewed paper in APL Energy (2025), was a finalist at the SteelTech Awards 2025, and had CSIC formalize shareholder participation in November 2025.

name: LignoCarbon
tech_note: Swiss company producing biochar through pyrolysis/charring of wood, processing and trading coal-based products under the LignoCarbon brand.
description: LignoCarbon Schweiz AG is a Swiss biochar producer based in Illnau-Effretikon, Zurich, operating a pyrolysis facility that converts wood into biochar products. The company was founded in 2020 and remains active in the Swiss commercial register, with its stated purpose being the charring/pyrolysis of wood and the processing, refining, storage, transport and trading of various coal products.

name: Lillianah Technologies
tech_note: Cultivates and disperses native diatoms (phytoplankton) in coastal hypoxic dead zones to capture CO2 via the biological pump, with permanence claimed via marine sedimentation.
description: Lillianah Technologies is a Houston-based ocean CDR startup founded in 2021 that removes CO2 by dispersing diatoms into nutrient-rich marine dead zones (initially on the Gulf Coast), using MRV based on dissolved oxygen sensors and sediment traps. It is an IndieBio/SOSV portfolio company that has raised roughly $525K–$1.2M in seed and grant funding and signed an early offtake agreement with Clearyst°. Operational signals since 2023 are limited, with a small team (~4–7 employees) and no disclosed new funding rounds.

name: Limenet
tech_note: Limenet operates an industrial plant in Augusta, Sicily that combines CO2 (from a biogas source) with hydrated lime and seawater to produce calcium bicarbonates released into the ocean, increasing alkalinity and storing carbon durably.
description: Limenet is an Italian climate tech company using a patented pH-equilibrated Ocean Alkalinization technology that stores CO₂ in seawater as equilibrated calcium bicarbonates, increasing ocean alkalinity. Its Augusta (Sicily) plant has been operational since September 2023, currently processes 800 tonnes of CO₂ per year, with plans to scale to 100,000 tonnes annually by 2028. In 2025, Carbonmark issued Limenet's first 14.7 OAE credits via Carbonmark Direct, a milestone for ocean-based carbon removal.

name: Liquid Trees
tech_note: Liquid Trees develops Ocean Iron Fertilization (OIF), adding trace iron to HNLC surface waters (notably the Southern Ocean) to stimulate phytoplankton blooms that export carbon to the deep ocean; earlier work focused on diatom-based freshwater bioremediation in rivers and lakes.
description: Liquid Trees is a seed-stage ocean CDR company (founded 2022, based in San Francisco with operations in Noida, India) pursuing Ocean Iron Fertilization as its primary pathway. It evolved from freshwater diatom bioremediation work across rivers in Bangladesh, Pakistan, Mexico, and India into open-ocean OIF research and advocacy, backed by Unruly Capital.

name: Lithos
tech_note: Applies ultra-fine basalt rock dust to US cropland and uses proprietary soil-chemistry MRV and ML modeling to quantify bicarbonate-form CO2 removal.
description: Lithos Carbon is a US-based CDR supplier scaling Enhanced Rock Weathering by applying crushed basalt rock dust to farmland, permanently removing CO2 while improving soil health. The company has signed major offtakes including a $57.1M/154,240-ton deal with Frontier and a multi-year agreement with Microsoft. In December 2025 it issued 5,160 registry-certified tons, billed as the largest ERW issuance to date.

name: Living Carbon
tech_note: Living Carbon develops photosynthesis-enhanced poplar trees and runs reforestation projects on degraded/former mine lands in the US to generate carbon removal credits.
description: Founded in 2019, California-based Living Carbon transforms marginal land into high-value environmental assets, with a focus on restoring abandoned mines, degraded farmland, and unproductive soils with site-tailored reforestation. The company combines biotech (photosynthesis-enhanced hybrid poplars) with large-scale reforestation of degraded lands, especially former Appalachian coal-mine sites. It is a CDR supplier generating verified reforestation carbon removal credits.

name: Longstraw Carbon
tech_note: Slow pyrolysis of agricultural residues (rice husk, crop straw) into biochar for soil application, with bio-oil and syngas co-products.
description: Longstraw Carbon is a Delhi, India-based biochar producer founded in 2024 that converts agricultural residues (rice husk, crop straw) into biochar, bio-oil, and syngas via its proprietary STS™ / RiceLoop™ pyrolysis technology. The company operates production sites in Kalahandi and Sambalpur (Odisha) and targets carbon removal markets for Indian smallholder agriculture.

name: Low Carbon Materials
tech_note: Manufactures carbon-negative lightweight aggregates (ACLA® for asphalt, OSTO® for concrete) that lock biogenic carbon and some carbonation-derived CO2 permanently into construction materials as a drop-in replacement for traditional aggregates.
description: Low Carbon Materials (LCM) is a Durham University spin-out based in Seaham, UK, that designs and manufactures carbon-negative aggregates — OSTO® for concrete and ACLA® for asphalt — which sequester biogenic carbon (with some additional carbonation uptake) permanently within construction materials. The company closed a £3M growth round led by Ada Ventures, won the BE100 SCALE competition at Blue Earth Summit 2025, and has deployed ACLA in trials on the M11 and numerous council road projects with National Highways, Skanska, and Tarmac. An EPD (EPD-IES-0016646) reports an A1-A3 GWP of –798 kg CO2e/t for ACLA.

name: LowCarbon
tech_note: Develops "Zero C" direct air capture units and a proprietary KLC catalyst that converts captured CO2 into sodium/calcium carbonates, alongside CCUS-linked clean hydrogen production.
description: LowCarbon is a South Korean climate-tech company founded in 2016 and based in Gangjin, Jeollanam-do, developing DAC and CCUS technologies. Its Zero C DAC product captures atmospheric CO2 and its KLC catalyst converts it into carbonate minerals; the company has also signed a DACCS supply contract with Space Florida and an MOA with the Florida state government for a clean hydrogen hub. It is a member of the DAC Coalition and remains operationally active as of 2025.

name: Lucrat
tech_note: Produces EBC-certified biochar from hardwood (beech) pyrolysis, used in biogas fermenters and construction, with the residual char incorporated into agricultural soils as a permanent carbon sink.
description: Lucrat GmbH is a German biochar producer based in Steinfurt, focused on applications in biogas plants and the construction industry. Their products are EBC-certified, and they also trade the resulting carbon credits, with biochar applied to agricultural land in Lower Saxony as a permanent sink.

name: MARINIX Ocean Tech AS
tech_note: Developing an ocean CDR method that induces formation of marine snow aggregates in the Southern Ocean to sink organic carbon to the deep sea.
description: MARINIX Ocean Tech AS is a Norwegian early-stage Ocean CDR startup founded by Hanne M. Edvardsen Jelavic, with scientific work led by Prof. Staša Puškarić on marine snow and ocean carbon kinetics. The company is pre-revenue and in R&D/funding phase, seeking philanthropic and research funding to scale a marine-snow-based ocean carbon removal concept.

name: MASH Makes
tech_note: MASH Makes operates containerised pyrolysis reactors that convert agricultural residues (primarily cashew nut shells) into biochar and bio-oil/biofuel, generating EBC-certified carbon removal credits.
description: MASH Makes A/S is a Danish company established in 2015 as a spin-off from the Technical University of Denmark, whose pyrolysis and gasification technology converts agricultural waste into carbon-negative energy commodities and biochar that removes CO2 from the atmosphere and produces carbon removal credits. The company employs 11 people in Denmark and 49 at its subsidiary in India operating the production facility in Udupi, Karnataka, and aims to scale from two to 30 sites by 2027. Credits are distributed via Carbonfuture under EBC certification.

name: MK Collect
tech_note: Liquid-solvent direct air capture using water-dispersible nanocatalysts that enable low-temperature (~88°C) solvent regeneration, allowing renewable/solar-hot-water-powered operation.
