description: MK Collect is an Australian DAC startup spun out of the University of Melbourne, commercializing Professor Kathryn Mumford's nanocatalyst-enhanced liquid solvent process. The company partnered with the University of Melbourne and engineering firm Innaco on a pilot plant, and secured $1.6M in grant funding in 2024 to scale the technology, which pairs capture with mineralization to produce carbonate products.

name: MYNO
tech_note: MYNO develops Carbon Removal Facilities that pyrolyze forest residuals and waste biomass into biochar for agriculture, infrastructure, and stormwater applications, while generating renewable energy and selling durable CDR credits.
description: MYNO Carbon is a Washington-based biochar producer founded in 2020 that planned a large-scale Carbon Removal Facility in Port Angeles, WA using forest residual feedstock. The company was awarded $20.4M from the USDA Fertilizer Production Expansion Program in late 2024, but that funding was cancelled by the Trump administration in April 2025, leaving the facility's status uncertain.

name: Macrocarbon
tech_note: MacroCarbon cultivates pelagic Sargassum seaweed in offshore aquafarms and converts the biomass via thermochemical processes (pyrolysis) into biochar, carbon black, and bio-hydrocarbons (including sustainable aviation fuel) for permanent carbon sequestration.
description: MacroCarbon SL is a Spain-based (Gran Canaria) spin-off of Germany's Alfred Wegener Institute and Carbonwave (US), focused on domesticating and cultivating Sargassum seaweed for carbon dioxide removal and industrial feedstock. The company produces sustainable aviation fuel and other biofuels from floating seaweeds like pelagic Sargassum, while storing part of the captured carbon in biochar and carbon black for long-term sequestration. In October 2025 MacroCarbon received permits from the Canary Islands government for a 40,000 m² seaweed farm near the Plataforma Oceánica de Canarias, bridging pilot and commercial deployment, with a first commercial facility requiring €80 million targeted in the next few years.

name: Made of Air
tech_note: Made of Air pyrolyzes forestry/agricultural waste into biochar and functionalizes it as a filler in thermoplastic composites used for building facades, automotive parts, and consumer goods, locking carbon into durable manufactured materials.
description: Berlin-based materials company founded in 2016 that turns wood-waste biochar into carbon-negative thermoplastic granules and composites for long-lived industrial applications (e.g., Audi dealership facades, H&M sunglasses). Each ton of material reportedly sequesters multiple tons of CO2 in products, positioning the firm as a biochar-based CDR supplier via durable material pools.

name: Mangrove Systems
tech_note: Digital MRV (dMRV) software platform (Mangrove Nexus) providing end-to-end measurement, carbon accounting, and registry reporting for CDR and CCS project operators.
description: Mangrove Systems is a Toronto-based digital MRV software company whose Mangrove Nexus platform tracks CO2 across CDR and CCS project value chains, supporting pathways including biochar, BECCS, DAC, and ERW. They do not remove CO2 themselves — they provide the data, accounting, and registry-reporting infrastructure used by CDR suppliers such as Pacific Biochar, Charm Industrial, Carbon Alpha, Super6 Carbon, and Summit Carbon Solutions. As an MRV/enabling-tech vendor whose entire business is the CDR/CCS market, they are part of the CDR ecosystem rather than a removal supplier.

name: Marquis Energy
tech_note: Marquis captures biogenic CO2 from its corn-ethanol fermentation process and injects it into an on-site Mt. Simon saline formation well for permanent geological storage (BECCS).
description: Marquis Energy operates the world's largest dry-mill ethanol plant in Hennepin, Illinois, and is developing a large-scale BECCS project (via subsidiary Marquis Carbon Capture LLC) to permanently sequester ~1.2 million tons/year of biogenic CO2 in the Mt. Simon formation beneath its industrial complex. While ethanol production is the core business, the company is building dedicated CDR removal infrastructure with permanent geological storage, qualifying it as a supplier.

name: Mast Reforestation
tech_note: Buries fire-killed trees in engineered low-oxygen underground chambers (Terrestrial Storage of Biomass) combined with post-wildfire reforestation, generating Puro.earth-certified durable CDR credits.
description: Mast Reforestation is a Seattle-based post-wildfire reforestation company that removes CO2 by burying unmerchantable fire-killed trees in engineered anoxic chambers, using credit revenue to fund native conifer replanting. Its MT1 project in Montana buried over 10 million pounds of biomass and issued 4,277 Puro.earth TSB credits in early 2026, with all MT1 credits sold to buyers including RBC, BMO, Bain & Company, CNaught, and Muir AI. The company operates two major Western US tree nurseries (Silvaseed and Cal Forest) and is scaling additional biomass burial projects.

name: Mati
tech_note: Spreads finely crushed basalt on smallholder croplands in India and Africa to accelerate silicate weathering and sequester CO2 as bicarbonate, supported by an in-house MRV platform (matiC) developed with IIT Kanpur and Yale.
description: Mati Carbon is a carbon removal supplier that deploys pulverized basalt onto smallholder farms in India, Tanzania, and Zambia to accelerate enhanced rock weathering. The company won the $50M XPRIZE Carbon Removal grand prize in 2025 and secured blended finance from J.P. Morgan backed by the Schmidt Family Foundation to expand across the Global South.

name: Metalplant
tech_note: Spreads crushed olivine/magnesium-silicate rock on fields planted with nickel-hyperaccumulating plants in Albania, producing both carbon-negative nickel ("NegativeNickel") and ERW-based CDR credits.
description: Metalplant is a US-headquartered CDR supplier operating field sites in Albania on serpentine-rich soils of the Mirdita Ophiolite. Its "Hyperweathering" approach couples enhanced rock weathering of olivine with nickel phytomining to co-produce carbon removal credits and critical minerals for the EV/green-steel supply chain. The company is working toward Puro.earth ERW methodology compliance and announced a commercial trial for 2025.

name: Metzler
tech_note: Rotary-kiln pyrolysis of sustainably harvested hardwood chips/sawdust at ~1,350°F, water-quenched to produce high-carbon (70–90%) biochar products.
description: Metzler Biochar, a division of Metzler Forest Products LLC in Reedsville, Pennsylvania, produces wood-based biochar from local sawmill co-products using an industrial-scale rotary kiln pyrolysis system. The company sells biochar and biochar-amended soil blends for agriculture, stormwater management, and livestock applications, and recovers excess process heat to displace propane in firewood drying kilns.

name: Meva Energy
tech_note: Modular biomass gasification plants producing industrial biosyngas with biochar as a carbon-sequestering by-product.
description: Meva Energy is a Swedish cleantech firm (founded 2008, based in Gothenburg) that builds modular biomass gasification plants producing renewable biosyngas for industrial customers, with biochar as a carbon-negative by-product used for soil carbon storage. In October 2025 the company secured €40M venture debt from the EIB to scale plants for Sofidel, IKEA Poland, and Elcowire.

name: Midori Partner
tech_note: Midori Climate Partner develops biochar carbon removal projects using agricultural biomass residues in Southeast Asia, alongside agroforestry and mangrove restoration.
description: Midori Climate Partner Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based carbon credit developer specializing in ecosystem restoration, structuring biochar and agroforestry projects across Southeast Asia including Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, and Malaysia. In early 2025 the company closed a pre-seed round led by Tokio Marine Holdings to expand biochar carbon removal projects across Asia, with its first project launching in Cambodia. Note: DB listed as Germany-based, but company is actually headquartered in Singapore.

name: Milkywire
tech_note: Milkywire is a Stockholm-based procurement platform and advisory that channels corporate funding into durable CDR suppliers via its Climate Transformation Fund and tailored Seed/Scale CDR portfolios.
description: Stockholm-based Milkywire is an impact platform that pre-purchases durable carbon removal credits and has purchased from many suppliers through its Climate Transformation Fund, backed by companies like Klarna, Spotify and ING Bank. Their 2025 round brought total CDR suppliers supported through the CTF to 40, second only to Shopify and Stripe per CDR.fyi data. They do not remove CO2 themselves — they run open calls, vet projects, and broker procurement for corporate buyers, placing them squarely in the CDR ecosystem.

name: MioTech
tech_note: MioTech's carbon asset team operates the Nian'da biochar facility in Nanjing, which pyrolyzes agricultural waste into biochar applied to farmland for durable carbon sequestration and CORC issuance.
description: MioTech is an AI-based ESG data and sustainability analytics company headquartered in Shanghai/Hong Kong that has expanded into CDR project development. Its carbon asset team developed China's first biochar carbon credit project, registered on Puro.earth with support from Nanjing Nian'da Environmental Technology and Nanjing Forestry University, and became the first biochar supplier in China to issue CORCs, with the Nanjing-based Nian'da project generating 330 CORCs in its first accreditation period. MioTech has announced plans to develop 50,000 tons of carbon credits by 2027 spanning biochar, geological storage, carbonated materials, and enhanced rock weathering.

name: Miraïa
tech_note: Miraïa operates modernized continuous vertical-furnace pyrolysis of woody biomass to produce biochar, bio-oils and syngas/electricity, targeting agriculture and industrial (e.g. metallurgical coke replacement) uses.
description: Miraïa is a French (Toulouse-based) climate-tech startup, founded in 2023, commercializing continuous wood pyrolysis to produce biochar, bio-oils, and renewable energy. It is building a pilot demonstrator in Colomiers (Haute-Garonne) and plans its first commercial-scale plant in Garlin (Pyrénées-Atlantiques) with a target of 20,000 t/yr biochar, with longer-term ambitions for 6–7 plants.

name: Mission Zero
tech_note: Develops a modular electrochemical direct air capture system that uses a water-based solvent regenerated with renewable electricity to recover atmospheric CO2 for utilization or permanent storage.
description: Mission Zero Technologies is a UK-based company that develops electrochemical direct air capture (DAC) technology inspired by biological reactions that manage CO₂ in the body, designed to recover atmospheric CO₂ at any scale. The company has deployed three systems to date, including a UK plant with O.C.O Technology that pairs DAC with building-materials production and a third system now capturing CO₂ for permanent underground storage at Deep Sky in Canada.

name: Moola Pflanzenkohle
tech_note: Pyrolysis of plant biomass to produce EBC-certified biochar for soil amendment, animal feed, and stable bedding applications.
description: Moola is a German/Austrian biochar producer that uses pyrolysis to convert plant biomass into EBC-certified biochar, sold as a soil amendment, animal feed additive, and stable bedding. The company describes itself as an early industrial biochar pioneer in Germany, and is an active member of the Fachverband Pflanzenkohle industry association. Products remain available through retailers in 2024–2025.

name: Mote
tech_note: Mote gasifies woody biomass waste (forestry and agricultural residues) to produce clean hydrogen while capturing and geologically sequestering the byproduct CO2, a BiCRS/BECCS approach.
description: Mote is a Los Angeles-based BiCRS startup, spun out of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, that converts wood waste into carbon-negative hydrogen with permanent CO2 sequestration. Its flagship Bakersfield, California facility has completed a FEL-2 study and received a DOE Loan Programs Office Part II invitation, with a second project planned with SMUD in Sacramento. In March 2025 Mote closed $7M in Series A funding to advance its first commercial-scale plant.

name: NAWARO ENERGIE Betrieb
tech_note: Operates wood-gasification CHP plants in Austria; biochar is produced as a by-product of wood gasification at the Perg site and sold for landscaping, agriculture, construction and metallurgy.
description: NAWARO ENERGIE Betrieb GmbH is an Austrian bioenergy producer headquartered in Zwettl, operating biomass and wood-gas power plants across the Waldviertel region. At its Perg location (in operation since 2023), wood gasification yields biochar as a co-product, which the company sells for agricultural, construction and metallurgical uses. The firm is listed as a member of the European Biochar Industry Consortium.

name: NEG8 Carbon
tech_note: Develops modular Electrostatic Direct Air Capture technology using thin-layer solid sorbents with industrial waste heat for regeneration.
description: NEG8 Carbon is a Waterford, Ireland-based Direct Air Capture company that develops proprietary Electrostatic DAC technology using thin-layer sorbent systems. The company built Ireland's first DAC prototype (1.2 tpa) and is advancing to a 50 tpa full-scale module in 2026 via a partnership with Prochem Engineering.

name: NULIFE GreenTech
tech_note: NULIFE uses hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) to convert waste biomass (food processing residues, ag residues, biosolids) into carbon-dense bio-oil that is injected into underground salt caverns / depleted reservoirs for permanent geological sequestration.
description: NULIFE GreenTech is a Canadian (Saskatoon) BiCRS supplier operating a commercial HTL facility that converts waste biomass into biocrude for permanent geological storage, with credits issued via the Isometric registry. It was selected by Frontier buyers for a multi-year 122,000-ton offtake covering 2026–2030 and has been delivering verified CDR credits since September 2025.

name: NY Carbon
tech_note: Produces high-carbon biochar via pyrolysis (Tigercat Carbonator 6050) from locally sourced woody waste biomass, primarily eastern white pine off-cuts from an adjacent lumber mill.
description: NY Carbon is a Saugerties, NY-based commercial-scale biochar producer serving the Hudson Valley and New England. They use 100% woody waste feedstock from within a 15-mile radius and supply biochar for agricultural soil applications, including partnerships with the 4 Corners Carbon Coalition, American Farmland Trust, and Cornell Cooperative Extension.

name: Nattergal
tech_note: Nattergal is a UK-based rewilding/nature-recovery company that purchases degraded farmland and restores it to biodiverse habitat mosaics, selling carbon credits, Biodiversity Net Gain units, and other ecosystem-service credits.
description: Nattergal is a UK private nature recovery company founded in 2021 that acquires and rewilds degraded agricultural land at scale, currently operating three sites (Boothby Wildland in Lincolnshire, High Fen Wildland in Norfolk, and Harold's Park in Essex). It generates revenue from carbon credits, Biodiversity Net Gain units, water credits, UK Landscape Recovery Scheme funding, and ecotourism, and partnered with Knepp Estate and Arup on the Knepp Wildland Carbon Project to quantify rewilding carbon sequestration.

name: Negative Emissions Platform
tech_note: Brussels-based industry coalition and trade association that advocates for EU policy recognition of permanent carbon dioxide removal technologies (DAC, BECCS, ERW, biochar, mineralisation, marine CDR).
description: The Negative Emissions Platform (NEP) is a Brussels-based membership association representing CDR technology developers, researchers and sponsors before EU institutions. It does not remove CO2 itself; instead it lobbies for the Carbon Removal Certification Framework, responds to EU consultations, and convenes the CDR community (e.g. hosting the CDR30 Pavilion at COP30). It is a core ecosystem/advocacy body dedicated solely to the CDR industry.

name: Nellie
tech_note: Grows microalgae in photobioreactors to capture CO2 from ambient air or point sources, then pyrolyzes the biomass into biochar (PhycoChar) used as a soil amendment/biofertiliser in UK agriculture.
description: Nellie Technologies is a UK-based CDR supplier operating a pilot facility in Mwyndy, South Wales, that cultivates microalgae for CO2 capture and converts the biomass into durable biochar. The company sells Puro.earth CORCs and signed a 17,500-ton, 5-year offtake with Zurich Insurance in January 2025, and won the 2025 IOP Business Start-Up Award.

name: NeoCarbon
tech_note: Solid-sorbent direct air capture modules retrofitted into industrial cooling towers, using existing airflow and waste heat; captured CO2 mineralized into concrete via partnership with Carbonaide.
description: NeoCarbon is a Berlin-based DAC startup that retrofits solid-sorbent carbon-capture modules onto industrial cooling towers, leveraging existing airflow and waste heat to reduce DAC costs. The company has built autonomous pilot modules, produced its first batch of low-carbon concrete with partner Carbonaide in early 2025, and plans to deploy its third DAC unit at a live data center in 2026.

name: Net Zero Lab
tech_note: Academic research group at the Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition studying climate tech, corporate decarbonization, and carbon markets, and co-organizing the ACRA accelerator for Sub-Saharan African CDR startups.
description: Net Zero Lab is an independent Max Planck research group (launched 2024, led by Benedict Probst) based in Munich, focused on economics of climate technology, corporate net-zero strategies, and carbon markets. It is a co-organizer of the Africa Carbon Removal Accelerator (ACRA) alongside sus.lab ETH Zurich, Strathmore University, Nuvoni, and remove. It is not a CDR supplier but an academic/ecosystem actor supporting CDR startup development.

name: NetZero
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of tropical agricultural residues (coffee husks, cocoa shells, sugarcane bagasse) at modular industrial plants and applies it to soils for high-permanence carbon removal.
description: NetZero is a French startup founded in 2021 and headquartered in Paris, specializing in large-scale biochar production from unused tropical crop residues for permanent atmospheric carbon removal and soil enhancement. It operates three first-generation plants — one in Cameroon processing cocoa husks and two in Brazil dedicated to coffee parchment, together processing 22,000 tonnes of organic waste into biochar per year (≈6,000 tCO2 sequestered annually). NetZero was first runner-up in the 2025 XPRIZE Carbon Removal competition, earning a $15 million prize.

name: Neustark
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from biogas plants and permanently stores it via accelerated mineralization (carbonation) in demolished concrete and other mineral wastes such as slag and incinerator bottom ash.
description: Founded in 2019, neustark is a spin-off from ETH Zurich based in Bern, and is expanding across Europe with 38 active capture and storage projects in Switzerland, Germany, Austria, the UK, France, Italy and Liechtenstein. The company captures CO2 at point source, then binds it in mineral waste streams via an accelerated mineralization process — biogenic CO2 is captured from partnering biogas plants, liquified and transported to construction waste recycling sites where it is injected into concrete granulates or other mineral waste such as slag, permanently binding the CO2.

name: Neutralizing Environmental Trash Inc.
tech_note: Pyrolysis of wood/biomass waste into biochar for carbon sequestration and soil amendment, deployed via JV with BluMountain Carbon using Vulcan pyrolysis equipment.
description: Neutralizing Environmental Trash Inc. (N.E.T. Inc), headquartered in Medford, Oregon, converts waste biomass into biochar for carbon removal and soil amendment. In November 2024 the company entered a 50/50 joint venture ("NET of the Villages LLC") with BluMountain Carbon (a BluSky Carbon joint venture) to build a biochar production facility in the Orlando area using local wood waste, targeting ~50,000 tonnes of annual carbon removal.

name: Neutura
tech_note: Neutura pyrolyzes palm oil empty fruit bunches (EFB) and other agricultural waste into biochar for carbon sequestration and soil amendment in Indonesia.
description: Neutura is a Singapore-headquartered carbon removal company operating biochar production facilities in Indonesia using palm-oil empty fruit bunches as feedstock. It has delivered a pilot project in collaboration with Universitas Sumatera Utara and signed partnerships with Indonesian farms to apply biochar to degraded agricultural land.

name: Next Wave Carbon Removals
tech_note: Produces biochar from waste wood using ARTi pyrolysis technology in partnership with Maxsum Environmental, with plans to sell carbon credits.
description: Next Wave Carbon Removal is a US-based (Des Moines, Iowa) biochar producer combining ARTi Biochar's pyrolysis technology with Maxsum Environmental's investment backing. The company aims to be a vertically integrated biochar-to-carbon-credit operation, starting in the US and expanding into Latin America.

name: NextGen CDR
tech_note: CDR buyers' club / advance market commitment purchasing certified permanent removal credits on behalf of a collective of corporate buyers.
description: NextGen CDR is a buyers' club / advance-market-commitment facility jointly established by South Pole and Mitsubishi Corporation to aggregate corporate demand for durable, certified carbon removals at a target price of $200/tonne. Founding and subsequent buyers include BCG, LGT, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, Swiss Re, UBS and Mizuho. It has contracted offtakes across DAC, BiCRS, biochar, mineralization and enhanced weathering (e.g. Neustark, Exomad Green, Alt Carbon) but does not itself remove CO2 — it is a demand-side aggregator in the CDR ecosystem.

name: Nina Energy
tech_note: Builds modular, on-site pyrolysis reactors that convert agro-industrial and forestry residues into biochar plus renewable thermal energy and bio-oil.
description: Nina Energy Limited is an Ecuadorian start-up founded in 2021 that specializes in developing and deploying thermochemical conversion systems for residual biomass, aimed at rural Latin American agro-industries. In November 2025, a pyrolysis plant was launched near Cotopaxi, Ecuador together with atmosfair, converting wood waste from ecological forestry into biochar. The company both operates biochar plants and designs/sells its proprietary pyrolysis reactor technology.

name: Nordbex
tech_note: Nordbex develops, builds, finances and operates combined heat and power plants fueled by forestry waste biomass integrated with post-combustion carbon capture (BECCS/Bio-CCUS) for permanent geological storage.
description: Nordbex AB is a Swedish company developing bioenergy with carbon capture, use and storage (BECCUS) facilities, working with Aker Carbon Capture on integration of Just Catch 100 units. Their first plant, Nordbex 1, is scheduled to begin operations in the SE4 electricity region by 2029 and will convert forestry waste into electricity and district heat while capturing and storing CO2. The company sells carbon removal credits from the biogenic CO2 captured and permanently stored.

name: Nordgau Carbon
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of locally-sourced PEFC-certified wood chips for use in agriculture and livestock, with carbon removal certified under Puro.earth and EBC.
description: Nordgau Carbon GmbH & Co. KG is a German biochar producer based in Wernberg-Köblitz, Bavaria, producing biochar from PEFC-certified local wood chips via pyrolysis since 2020. The company sells biochar products for agriculture, livestock, and soil uses, and issues CORCs through Puro.earth with EBC certification.

name: Nordic Carbon
tech_note: Nordic Carbon builds and operates pyrolysis facilities in Denmark that convert waste biomass into biochar for long-term soil carbon storage, with integrated MRV for carbon credit generation.
description: Nordic Carbon is a Danish biochar supplier that designs, builds and commissions pyrolysis facilities converting underutilized biomass residues into stable biochar applied to local farmland. The team brings 20+ years of biomass industry experience and generates carbon credits from the sequestered CO₂. Note: distinct from the similarly-named Nordic Carbon Removal Association (nordiccarbon.org).

name: Nordiczero
tech_note: Develops biochar and bioash from biogenic residues for use as additives in concrete and building materials, locking carbon into durable construction products.
description: Nordiczero is a Sweden-based company developing solutions that utilize biochar and bioash produced from biogenic residues as components in concrete and building materials. By embedding stable pyrolysis carbon in cementitious products, the company targets durable carbon storage in the built environment.

name: Nordvästra Skånes Renhållnings
tech_note: Municipal waste utility operating Sweden's largest biochar plant, pyrolyzing urban garden waste (~7,000 t/yr) into ~1,500 t/yr of biochar using Vow/Scanship BioGreen pyrolysis technology, with surplus heat fed to district heating.
description: Nordvästra Skånes Renhållnings AB (NSR) is a Swedish municipal recycling company owned by six northwest Skåne municipalities (Bjuv, Båstad, Helsingborg, Höganäs, Åstorp, Ängelholm). At its Filborna site in Helsingborg it operates a biochar production facility inaugurated in June 2022 — the largest of its kind in Sweden — converting residual urban green waste into biochar while supplying district heating, and hosts a Biochar Competence Centre opened alongside the 2023 International Biochar Summit.

name: Norma
tech_note: Norma is developing a supercapacitive electrochemical Direct Air Capture system that integrates energy storage with CO2 capture to dramatically reduce energy consumption.
description: Norma is a Paris-based climate tech startup building low-cost, modular machines for direct air capture, co-founded by CTO Silvia Pugliese and CEO Mónica Larrazábal (ex-McKinsey, MIT MBA). The company is developing a breakthrough DAC technology that integrates supercapacitor-based energy storage with carbon capture in a single electrochemical system, storing and reusing the energy required to capture CO₂. It secured its first customer for carbon removal through the Milkywire Climate Transformation Fund and is building its first pilot system.

name: NormaTech
tech_note: NormaTech is listed as a Germany-based direct air capture (DAC) technology developer, though no technical details about its capture process are publicly available.
description: NormaTech is a German direct air capture company (website normatech-dac.com) included in the cdrjobs.earth registry. Web searches return no press, partnerships, funding announcements, or LinkedIn footprint for the company, and it is absent from major German DAC industry directories that list peers like DACMA, Ucaneo, and PlasmaAir. The lack of any public signals raises questions about operational status.

name: North Star
tech_note: BECCS project capturing biogenic CO2 from a forestry waste-biomass cogeneration plant and permanently storing it in a deep saline aquifer in Saskatchewan.
description: North Star Carbon Solutions LP is a joint venture between Svante Technologies (via its Carbon Alpha subsidiary) and the Meadow Lake Tribal Council (MLTC) developing Canada's first majority Indigenous-owned BECCS project in Saskatchewan. The facility will capture biogenic CO2 from the MLTC Bioenergy Centre (fueled by sawmill waste biomass) and permanently store it in a deep saline aquifer, with Phase 1 designed for up to 140,000 tonnes CO2/year. In April 2026 it signed a 626,000-tonne, 15-year offtake with Microsoft; commercial operation is planned for 2029.

name: North Star Carbon Solutions
tech_note: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) project capturing biogenic CO₂ from a forestry-biomass cogeneration facility and injecting it into a deep saline aquifer for permanent geological storage.
description: North Star Carbon Solutions LP is a Saskatchewan-based BECCS project developer, a joint venture between the Meadow Lake Tribal Council (MLTC) and Svante Technologies (via its subsidiary Carbon Alpha). The project will capture biogenic CO₂ at the MLTC Bioenergy Centre (fed by sawmill waste biomass) and permanently store it in a saline aquifer southwest of Meadow Lake, targeting ~90,000 tonnes/year with commercial operation planned for 2029.

name: NorthStar Clean Energy
tech_note: Developing a BECCS/BiCRS project by converting the TES Filer City coal plant in Michigan to biomass fuel retrofitted with Babcock & Wilcox's SolveBright post-combustion CO2 capture, targeting ~500,000 tons CO2/yr permanently stored underground.
description: NorthStar Clean Energy is a wholly owned subsidiary of CMS Energy (NYSE: CMS) developing one of the first US large-scale BECCS/BiCRS projects at the Filer City Station in Michigan, with planned commercial operation in 2029. The project would capture and permanently store up to 550,000 tons of CO2 annually and sell carbon removal credits to corporate buyers, alongside the parent firm's broader solar, wind, storage, and natural gas portfolio.

name: Northern Lights
tech_note: Operates ship-and-pipeline CO2 transport plus permanent geological storage in saline aquifers 2,600m below the North Sea seabed, providing the storage leg of CCS/BECCS value chains.
description: Northern Lights is a joint venture of Equinor, Shell, and TotalEnergies offering commercial CO2 transport and storage as a service from its terminal in Øygarden, Norway. It began injecting CO2 in August 2025 and has BECCS removal contracts with Stockholm Exergi (900kt/yr biogenic CO2 from 2028) and Ørsted's bio-power plant, alongside industrial CCS customers. Phase 2 FID announced in March 2025 will expand capacity from 1.5 to 5+ Mt CO2/year.

name: Nova Pangaea Technologies
tech_note: Licenses the REFNOVA® thermal process (steam-assisted rapid pyrolysis) that converts lignocellulosic biomass residues into 2G sugars for sustainable aviation fuel and biochar as a carbon-sequestering co-product.
description: Nova Pangaea Technologies is a UK cleantech company headquartered at Wilton International, Redcar, that has commissioned an end-to-end demonstration plant for its patented REFNOVA® process, converting woody and agricultural residues into 2G ethanol (for SAF) and biochar. While SAF is its primary commercial focus (through Project Speedbird with British Airways and LanzaJet), the biochar co-product delivers net-negative CO₂ emissions, placing NPT within the biochar-supplier segment of the CDR market.

name: Novocarbo
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis-based Carbon Removal Parks that convert biogenic residues into biochar plus renewable heat for district heating networks.
description: Novocarbo is a Hamburg-based climate tech company that operates Carbon Removal Parks across Germany, using pyrolysis to convert biogenic residues into biochar while producing renewable heat. Recent activity includes new sites in Bochum and Dessau, the German Sustainability Award 2025, and a 2025 pilot with Hansa Asphalt that produced the first certified CDR credits from biochar-infused asphalt.

name: NuAria
tech_note: NuAria develops solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture systems using cylindrical wound sorbent-filled membranes designed to be low-cost and scalable, and offers carbon credit subscriptions.
description: NuAria is a US-based direct air capture startup developing a novel sorbent packaged as cylindrical wound membranes, aiming at affordable and scalable CO2 removal. The company sells carbon credits via subscriptions and upfront purchases to industries and governments pursuing net-zero targets. Public signals are limited — the website is live and it was featured on a 2025 DAC watchlist, but there is no recent funding or deployment news.

name: NuWa Solutions
tech_note: Develops Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) pilots with MRV, safety stop-rules, and community-first permitting to deliver verifiable marine CO2 removals.
description: NuWa Solutions is a Delaware-based marine carbon dioxide removal company specializing in ocean alkalinity enhancement and blue carbon approaches, working with governments, institutions, and enterprises. The company develops OAE for verifiable marine CO2 removal with rigorous MRV and safety guardrails, and is currently pre-credit with a buyer interest list.

name: Nuxsen
tech_note: Electrochemical DAC using a solid, electrochemically-activated sorbent bonded to structured monolithic supports, swinging CO2 capture/release via voltage rather than heat.
description: Nuxsen is an early-stage US DAC startup founded in 2022 in New York, developing electrochemical direct air capture technology that uses variable-controlled voltage instead of thermal regeneration to release CO2 from a solid sorbent. It was a DOE DAC Pre-Commercial Technology Prize semifinalist ($100k cash + $50k technical assistance in 2023) and has been testing its patented sorbent and CarbonJet/SlipStream reactor designs at NETL's DAC Center in Pittsburgh. Per Tracxn (mid-2025) the company remains unfunded.

name: Néolithe
tech_note: Néolithe shreds non-recyclable waste and binds it with a mineral binder under high pressure to produce construction aggregates ("Anthropocite") that lock in biogenic carbon from the waste.
description: Néolithe is a French industrial startup (based in Anjou, ~100-200 employees) that operates "Fossilizers" — machines that transform non-recyclable, non-hazardous waste into mineral aggregates via its Accelerated Fossilization process, sequestering biogenic carbon contained in the waste. The aggregates substitute natural aggregates in concrete and are claimed to store ~337-420 kg CO2e per tonne. The company raised €60M in 2023 and is scaling plants across France.

name: O.C.O Technology
tech_note: Uses patented Accelerated Carbonation Technology (ACT) to react CO2 with Air Pollution Control residues and other industrial wastes, permanently sequestering CO2 as stable carbonate minerals in a carbon-negative manufactured limestone aggregate for construction.
description: O.C.O Technology is a UK-based mineralization CDR supplier operating multiple aggregate manufacturing facilities (Brandon, Avonmouth, Leeds, Wretham) that transform hazardous waste residues and CO2 into carbon-negative construction aggregate. They sell verified carbon removal credits via the Puro.earth registry and are partnering with Mission Zero Technologies to co-locate DAC at their Wretham site.

name: OBIO
tech_note: Operates an industrial-scale pyrolysis plant at Rudshøgda, Norway, converting PEFC-certified forestry wood chips into EBC-certified biochar for soil amendment, animal feed, and concrete applications.
description: OBIO is a Norwegian biochar company based in the Opland/central region that built the first industrial-scale pyrolysis plant in Norway at Rudshøgda in Ringsaker municipality. Obio AS was founded in December 2022 when the pyrolysis business was transferred from Oplandske Bioenergi, and is owned 60% by district heating company Eidsiva Bioenergi and 40% by forest owners cooperative Glommen Mjøsen Skog. The company sells Puro.earth CORCs and produces biochar for agricultural, livestock feed, and concrete applications.

name: OLNEO
tech_note: Produces biochar from agricultural residues via pyrolysis and applies it to degraded soils, with integrated sensor/satellite-based MRV for carbon credit certification.
description: OLNEO is a climate deeptech startup developing modular carbon removal systems, based in Paris, France with 1-10 employees. The company is building carbon removal infrastructure in Africa using biochar, converting local agricultural residues into high-quality biochar, rooted in Algeria and designed to scale across Africa and the MENA region.

name: Occidental Petroleum
tech_note: Develops and operates liquid-solvent (KOH/calciner) Direct Air Capture plants with saline-formation geologic sequestration via Class VI injection wells in the Permian Basin.
description: Occidental Petroleum (NYSE: OXY) is a major U.S. oil and gas company that operates a significant Direct Air Capture business through its wholly-owned subsidiaries 1PointFive and Carbon Engineering (acquired 2023). Its flagship STRATOS facility in Ector County, Texas — designed to capture up to 500,000 tonnes of CO2 per year — is in final startup, with Phase 1 expected online in Q2 2026 and CDR credit offtakes signed with Microsoft, Amazon, BlackRock, JPMorgan, Palo Alto Networks, and Bain & Company.

name: Ocean
tech_note: Nonprofit convener/accelerator for ocean-based CDR — publishes road maps, runs Launchpad advisory program, maintains mCDR Ecosystem and Field Trial databases, develops EIAF frameworks.
description: Ocean Visions is a US-based nonprofit that catalyzes research, road maps, field trials, and an accelerator (Launchpad) for marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). It convenes scientists, startups, funders, and policymakers and publishes ecosystem databases, MRV frameworks, and technology road maps across pathways like ocean alkalinity enhancement, electrochemical CDR, macroalgae/microalgae, and blue carbon. It is not a physical CDR supplier but a core ecosystem actor.

name: Ocean Frontier Institute
tech_note: OFI is a Canadian academic research institute (Dalhousie/Memorial/UPEI) conducting interdisciplinary ocean research, including marine CDR science, MRV for ocean carbon, and the CONVERGE CDR and Transforming Climate Action programs.
description: The Ocean Frontier Institute (OFI) is a non-profit research organization led by Dalhousie University with Memorial University and UPEI, funded by the Canada First Research Excellence Fund. It conducts ocean climate research including marine CDR science (ocean alkalinity enhancement, iron fertilization, seaweed, direct ocean capture) through programs like CONVERGE CDR and the North Atlantic Carbon Observatory, but does not itself deliver carbon removal credits.

name: Ocean Nourishment Corporation
tech_note: Ocean Nourishment Corporation develops macronutrient ocean fertilization technology (PhytoPlus biostimulant, now green-ammonia-based) deployed from ships or offshore platforms to stimulate phytoplankton growth and export carbon to the deep ocean.
description: Ocean Nourishment Corporation (ONC) is an Australian marine CDR company founded in 2004 that uses ocean fertilization by adding balanced macronutrients to nutrient-poor waters to stimulate phytoplankton growth and sequester CO2. Together with its sister WhaleX Foundation, ONC is a Top 100 XPRIZE Carbon Removal team and is running small-scale biopod and photobioreactor experiments while seeking partners in green hydrogen, green ammonia, shipping, and offshore platforms.

name: Ocean pHix
tech_note: Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement — adding alkaline materials to seawater to convert dissolved CO2 into stable bicarbonate/carbonate ions for long-term ocean storage.
description: Ocean pHix is a UK-based company listed on the Isometric supplier registry under the Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) pathway. Public information on the company is very limited; it appears to be an early-stage marine CDR supplier working on increasing ocean alkalinity to durably sequester atmospheric CO2. No recent press, hiring activity, or delivery announcements were surfaced in research.

name: Octavia Carbon
tech_note: Octavia Carbon designs and deploys solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture machines powered by Kenyan geothermal energy, with captured CO2 injected into Rift Valley basalt (via partner Cella) for permanent mineralization.
description: Founded in 2022 by Martin Freimüller and Duncan Kariuki, Octavia has grown to about 60 people designing, building, and deploying DAC machines in Kenya, with a pilot along the Rift Valley near Gilgil. In 2025, Octavia commissioned Project Hummingbird, described as the first commercial DAC plant on the African continent. Hummingbird targets ~1,500 tCO2/yr gross (~1,000 tCO2/yr net) with a subsequent larger development aimed at ~10,000 tCO2/yr.

name: One Earth Energy
tech_note: Corn ethanol producer capturing fermentation CO2 and injecting it into the Mt. Simon Sandstone formation in Illinois via a planned short intrastate pipeline.
description: One Earth Energy operates a 150-million-gallon corn ethanol plant in Gibson City, Illinois, and (via sister entity One Earth Sequestration, owned by parent REX American Resources) is developing a BECCS project to capture ~460,000 tonnes CO2/year from fermentation and inject it into deep saline formations. As of FY2024, REX had substantially completed capture and compression construction, with >$115M invested, though the pipeline permit has faced Illinois Commerce Commission pushback. The project is progressing but delivery has slipped past mid-2025.

name: OnePoint5
tech_note: Converts surplus agricultural crop residue in South Asia into biochar via pyrolysis for soil and infrastructure applications, generating durable carbon removal credits.
description: OnePoint5 is an India-based biochar CDR supplier that transforms agricultural residue (crop stubble) into high-quality biochar for soil and infrastructure applications. They operate a batch-tracing platform called StubbleX and are listed as a supplier on the Isometric registry.

name: Onnu
tech_note: Onnu develops pyrolysis plants and manufactures biochar from waste biomass (including poultry litter, oil palm residues), selling EBC-certified biochar and generating Puro.Earth CORCs.
description: Onnu is a UK-headquartered project developer and technology provider that develops its own pyrolysis plants and consults on plants for clients across Europe and SE Asia. It operates Onnu Biochar, the biochar trading arm selling EBC-certified biochar for retail customers in Europe, and Onnu Bioflow, the renewable commodities trading arm for larger-scale customers. Onnu is registered with the Puro.Earth carbon registry and biochar from its Wye Valley hubs qualifies for CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs).

name: Oraquel
tech_note: Oraquel builds modular Hi-DAC reactors that use patented filters with a sorbent mix of eight natural absorbent/adsorbent substances, powered by solar PV and hydro, to capture CO2 from ambient air.
description: Oraquel S.A. is a Warsaw-based DAC technology developer (the website references a Swiss "Oraquel Group") building modular, solar-powered direct air capture reactors rated at up to 500 tCO2/yr each. In September 2025 the company partnered with the city of Kielce to deploy Poland's first DAC pilot facility, providing the hardware and technical expertise under CEO Wojciech Mudyna.

name: Oregon Biochar Solutions
tech_note: Produces ultra-pure biochar at industrial scale via high-temperature pyrolysis of Pacific Northwest forest wood residues, generating Puro.earth CORCs for biochar carbon removal.
description: Oregon Biochar Solutions (OBS), based in White City, Oregon, manufactures Rogue Biochar from Douglas fir and pine logging residues at its industrial-scale facility. The company is a registered Puro.earth biochar supplier with thousands of CORCs issued and retired, and partnered with Oka and GECA Environnement on world-first invalidation-insured biochar credits.

name: Origen
tech_note: Limestone-based DAC combining a zero-emission lime kiln with a low-intensity air contactor; CO2 from calcination is stored underground while the resulting lime passively absorbs atmospheric CO2.
description: Origen (Origen Power Limited) is a UK/US-based DAC company using limestone chemistry combined with a proprietary green lime kiln and low-intensity air contactor to capture CO2 and store it underground. The company raised $13M Series A in January 2025 led by Barclays Climate Ventures with Shell Ventures participation, and has partnerships with EERC (North Dakota, 1,000 tpa) and Shell/Mitsubishi (Pelican Gulf Coast DAC Hub, up to 50,000 tpa).

name: Origin Biochar
tech_note: Pyrolysis of sustainably sourced biomass using a Biomacon reactor to produce biochar for feed and horticultural markets, with co-produced renewable heat.
description: Origin Biochar is a Northern Ireland-based manufacturer producing biochar via pyrolysis using a Biomacon unit. Their product range includes feedchar for livestock (cattle, sheep, pigs, poultry, equine) and horticultural biochar, marketed for animal health and soil amendment. Carbon sequestration is presented as a co-benefit of the pyrolysis process alongside renewable heat production.

name: Orsted
tech_note: Post-combustion amine-based CO2 capture on biomass (wood chip and straw) CHP plants, with liquefaction, shipping to Northern Lights, and permanent storage in a saline aquifer 2.6 km below the North Sea seabed.
description: Ørsted is a Danish renewable energy utility developing the Kalundborg CO2 Hub, a BECCS project capturing biogenic CO2 from its wood-chip-fired Asnæs and straw-fired Avedøre power stations for permanent subsea storage via Northern Lights in the Norwegian North Sea. The company has signed major carbon-removal offtake agreements totaling 3.67 Mt with Microsoft and 330,000 tonnes with Equinor, with operations commencing in 2025-2026. While Ørsted's main business is renewable power, its BECCS activities constitute a material CDR supplier division.

name: Oxford Charcoal Company
tech_note: Produces biochar as a byproduct of sustainable hardwood charcoal kilns in the UK, sold in retail bags for gardening and soil enhancement.
description: Oxford Charcoal Company is a UK-based producer of sustainable lumpwood barbecue charcoal that also manufactures biochar as a byproduct of its low-emission charcoal kilns. The biochar is sold primarily to gardeners and horticultural users rather than into carbon credit registries, so CDR is a secondary revenue line alongside the core BBQ charcoal business.

name: Oxy
tech_note: Oxy deploys Carbon Engineering's liquid-solvent DAC technology at commercial scale via subsidiary 1PointFive, with captured CO2 sequestered in Class VI wells or used for enhanced oil recovery.
description: Occidental (Oxy) is a major US oil & gas producer that, through its subsidiary 1PointFive (and with Carbon Engineering technology and OxyChem operations), is building large-scale Direct Air Capture facilities including STRATOS in Ector County, Texas. STRATOS, described as the world's largest DAC facility, received EPA Class VI sequestration permits in April 2025 for Ector County, Texas and in January 2026, 1PointFive announced Bain & Company had purchased 9,000 metric tons of DAC-based CDR credits over three years.

name: Ozen
tech_note: Ozen operates a wood pyrolysis plant in Wałcz, Poland producing charcoal/biochar briquettes and renewable electricity, with an EBC C-Sink certificate showing ~3.22 t CO2eq sink potential per ton of biochar.
description: Ozen Sp. z o.o. is a Polish charcoal and biochar manufacturer based in Wałcz that uses a patented wood-pyrolysis technology to produce charcoal, briquettes, and green electricity from pyrolysis heat. The company obtained a European Biochar Certificate (EBC) C-Sink certification for a batch produced in 2021-2022, qualifying it as a biochar CDR supplier, though its primary commercial focus remains industrial/BBQ charcoal rather than CDR credit sales.

name: PENNSACO TECHNOLOGIES
tech_note: Pennsaco uses a patented thermal conversion / dual-stream system to process biomass, plastic, and municipal solid waste into green hydrogen plus high-purity biochar as a carbon-sequestration co-product.
description: Pennsaco Technologies is a US (Radnor, PA) green hydrogen and carbon capture company founded in 2018-2019 that produces 'Ultra Green Hydrogen' and high-purity biochar from waste feedstocks via patented thermal conversion. The biochar co-product is marketed as a permanent carbon-removal pathway alongside regenerative agriculture benefits. The company has no disclosed funding, very few employees, and no significant public news since 2021-2022.

name: PUHI
tech_note: PUHI operates pyrolysis reactors that convert wood- and agriculture-based side streams (including recycled demolition wood) into biochar, district heat, and biochar carbon removal credits.
description: PUHI is a Finland-based biochar and carbon removal company offering pyrolysis-based climate tech, biochar products, and biomass piloting services, with its first biochar production plant in Industrial Park MORE, Hämeenlinna. Its environmental permit allows PUHI to process up to 20,000 tons of wood- and agriculture-based side streams annually into biochar, district heating, and carbon removal credits. PUHI is listed as a CORC supplier on Puro.earth and is a member of the European Biochar Industry Consortium.

name: Pacific Biochar
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis/gasification at partner biomass power plants using California forest residues, distributing it as a soil amendment for durable carbon storage.
description: Pacific Biochar is a California-based benefit corporation that produces biochar by modifying existing biomass power plants (e.g., Humboldt Sawmill, Hat Creek Bioenergy) to co-produce biochar from forest residue feedstock. The biochar is distributed for agricultural use, primarily blended with compost, delivering durable carbon removal credits registered on Puro.earth. They were CDR.FYI's #1 durable CDR supplier by deliveries in 2023.

name: Pacific Biochar/Wren
tech_note: Retrofits existing biomass power plants and sawmills to co-produce biochar from forest and sawmill residues, which is then applied to agricultural soils for durable carbon storage.
description: Pacific Biochar is a California-based benefit corporation that partners with biomass power plants and sawmills to produce biochar from forestry residues. The biochar is distributed to agricultural operations, primarily vineyards and compost yards, and the company sells verified carbon removal credits under standards including Isometric's Biochar Protocol.

name: Paebbl
tech_note: Reacts captured CO₂ with crushed olivine in a reactor to form magnesium carbonate powder used as a supplementary cementitious material in concrete.
description: Paebbl is a Dutch-Nordic mineralization company that converts captured CO₂ into a stable mineral powder used as a supplementary cementitious material (SCM) for the construction industry. In March 2025 the company launched its continuous demo plant in Rotterdam, claimed as a world-first for continuous CO₂ mineralization at demo scale, and plans a commercial plant by 2027.

name: Pannonia Bio
tech_note: Captures high-purity biogenic CO2 from large-scale corn/barley ethanol fermentation and biomethane upgrading, with planned pipeline transport and geological injection into onshore saline aquifers/depleted gas fields in Hungary.
description: Pannonia Bio is Europe's largest single-site grain biorefinery, located in Dunaföldvár, Hungary, producing bioethanol, biomethane, animal feed, proteins and corn oil. The company is developing a BECCS project ("Danube Removals") to capture ~500,000 tonnes/year of biogenic CO2 from its fermentation and biomethane-upgrading processes and inject it into nearby depleted gas fields/saline aquifers with partner OGD Green Storage. The capture-and-storage infrastructure is pre-FID, pending a 3D seismic study and test well, but the fermentation CO2 source is operational today.

name: Parallel Carbon
tech_note: Electrochemical DAC using a mineral sorbent coupled to water electrolysis, producing CO2 removal credits plus green hydrogen as a co-product.
description: Parallel Carbon is a UK-based (Manchester) direct air capture startup founded in 2021 that combines mineral-sorbent DAC with water electrolysis to co-produce CDR credits and green hydrogen. In February 2026 it signed a pre-purchase deal with Zurich Insurance Group for 1,200 tonnes of CDR, and it is joining the 2025 Shell StartUp Engine UK cohort while preparing a commercial pilot (100 t H2 and 1,000–2,000 t CO2/yr).

name: Partanna
tech_note: Produces a Portland-cement alternative from brine and steel slag that cures by absorbing atmospheric CO2 via mineralization, embedding permanent carbon into concrete building products.
description: Partanna Global is an advanced materials company co-founded by Rick Fox that has developed a sustainable alternative to Portland cement, eliminating the clinkering process while permanently removing CO₂ from the atmosphere. Their concrete substitute uses upcycled brine and steel slag that, when mixed, generate compounds that capture carbon dioxide. The company has a Verra-registered project and is expanding via partnerships with ADIO and Exeed Industries in the UAE.

name: Patch
tech_note: Patch operates a software platform and marketplace that helps corporate buyers source, diligence, purchase, and manage carbon credits (including CDR) from a global network of project suppliers.
description: Patch is a climate solutions provider that offers companies software, data and expertise to streamline purchasing and management of carbon credits. The platform aggregates a centralized database of more than 25,000 projects, including 100% of the projects from ICROA-endorsed registries. Patch is part of the CDR ecosystem as a marketplace/platform, not a supplier that physically removes CO2.

name: Pathway Energy
tech_note: Integrates biomass gasification, Fischer-Tropsch syngas conversion, and geological CO2 sequestration to co-produce carbon-negative SAF and engineered carbon removals.
description: Pathway Energy is a Houston-based developer of carbon-negative sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) projects and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Nexus Holdings. Its first project in Port Arthur, Texas, aims to pair biomass gasification + Fischer-Tropsch SAF production with a BECCS system expected to remove ~1.9 million tonnes of CO2 annually, with construction targeted for 2026 and operations in 2029. Biomass will be supplied under a heads-of-terms agreement with Drax Group.

name: Pelican Renewables
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from an ethanol plant and transports it by barge for permanent geologic sequestration in Class VI wells beneath the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta.
description: Pelican Renewables LLC is developing the Pelican Carbon Sequestration Hub on Rindge Tract in California's Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, anchored by their Stockton ethanol facility which provides biogenic CO2 for permanent geologic storage via Class VI injection wells. The project also accepts third-party CO2 delivered by rail and barge (via affiliate ZuCO2 Transport), and was selected for a $45.2M DOE CarbonSAFE Phase III award in 2024-2025.

name: Perennial
tech_note: Perennial provides MMRV (measurement, monitoring, reporting, verification) software and digital soil mapping (ATLAS-SOC, VT0014) for soil carbon projects and agricultural Scope 3 programs; they quantify soil organic carbon rather than physically removing CO2.
description: Perennial (formerly Cloud Agronomics) is a Boulder, CO-based MRV platform for soil-based carbon removal, using AI, remote sensing, and digital soil mapping to quantify soil organic carbon at scale. They led the development of Verra's VT0014 tool and serve project developers, food/ag companies, and sustainability teams — they are part of the CDR ecosystem as a verifier/MRV provider, not a CO2 remover themselves.

name: Phlair
tech_note: Phlair develops an electrochemical hydrolyzer-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) system using a liquid pH-swing sorbent regenerated with renewable electricity.
description: Founded in 2022 and based in Munich, Germany, Phlair develops hydrolyzer-based Direct Air Capture technology that uses a pH-swing mechanism for CO2 capture and release, enabling permanent storage or use in CO2-negative chemicals. The company serves buyers including Google, McKinsey, JPMorganChase, Shopify, Stripe, H&M, and Deep Sky, closed a €12M+ seed round in 2024 with a €2.5M EU grant, and announced a $30M offtake agreement in 2025.

name: Phoenix Energy
tech_note: Phoenix Energy builds, owns, and operates community-scale biomass gasification plants in California that generate renewable electricity from forest/agricultural waste while producing biochar and carbon removal credits.
description: Phoenix Energy is a California-based developer and operator of community-scale BECCS plants that convert forestry and agricultural waste into renewable energy and biochar (sold under the Earthworks Biochar brand). Its North Fork Community Power plant is operational and it is constructing the 3 MW Blue Mountain Electric Company (BMEC) plant, with a third project planned at Napa Recycling & Waste Services. The company sells carbon removal credits alongside wildfire-mitigation services to agencies like Cal Fire and the US Forest Service.

name: Phykos
tech_note: Phykos grows fast-growing seaweed on solar-powered autonomous ocean platforms, then harvests and sinks the biomass below 1,500 m for long-term carbon sequestration.
description: Phykos, PBC is an Oakland, California ocean CDR startup (YC S21) founded in 2020 that develops mobile, solar-powered robotic vessels to cultivate seaweed in the open ocean and sink the biomass in the deep sea for carbon sequestration. The company sells carbon credits based on biomass sunk and remains a small early-stage team with limited public activity in the last ~12 months.

name: Pina Earth
tech_note: Develops forest conversion (monoculture-to-mixed-forest) carbon projects in Central Europe using remote-sensing and digital-twin simulation for MRV, then issues and sells the resulting certified carbon credits.
description: Pina Earth is a Munich-based climate-tech company that develops forest conversion and adaptation projects in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, turning monoculture stands into climate-resilient mixed forests and issuing carbon credits certified under ISO 14064-2 and the eva Forest Climate Standard. In July 2025 it merged with Tree.ly to form Europe's largest forest carbon platform, and it has ongoing active partnerships (e.g. with myclimate on the Herzfelde project in Brandenburg).

name: Planet Savers
tech_note: Planet Savers is developing a Direct Air Capture system using a novel zeolite-based solid sorbent and a modular capture/concentration unit optimized for that adsorbent.
description: Planet Savers is Japan's first Direct Air Capture startup, spun out of the University of Tokyo and founded in 2023, backed by NEDO and Japan's Ministry of Environment. It is building a DACCU (DAC + Carbon Utilization) system based on an innovative zeolite adsorbent, having raised a ¥250M seed round in 2024 from Spiral Capital and JAFCO and targeting a 1 ton/day prototype.

name: Planetary
tech_note: Planetary adds purified alkaline minerals (e.g., magnesium/calcium oxide) to coastal outfalls at existing infrastructure like power-plant cooling-water discharges, driving ocean uptake of atmospheric CO2 as stable bicarbonate.
description: Planetary Technologies is a Canadian ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) supplier headquartered in Nova Scotia, with active projects in Halifax (Tufts Cove) and Virginia. In 2025 they delivered the world's first independently verified OAE credits (625.6 tonnes) to Stripe, Shopify, and British Airways under Isometric's OAE protocol, and signed a $31M offtake with Frontier.

name: Planeteers
tech_note: Planeteers operates reactors that dissolve limestone with CO2 from point sources (e.g. wastewater/biomass flue gas) to produce bicarbonate-rich mineralized water and ikaite, which are released into the ocean for permanent storage via ocean alkalinity enhancement.
description: Planeteers GmbH is a Hamburg-based climate-tech company focused on carbon dioxide removal via ocean storage, founded in December 2022 by Florian Birner, Frank Rattey, Jens Hartmann, and Florian Brinkmann. The firm's patented HCM technology accelerates the natural weathering of limestone by reacting it with captured CO2 to produce bicarbonate and ikaite, which are then released into the marine environment to enhance ocean alkalinity. The company has field-tested a pilot unit with a 60-ton annual CO2 capture capacity and plans to scale rapidly, aiming for a global capacity of one megaton by 2030.

name: Plantd Materials
tech_note: Grows Arundo donax perennial grass and processes it via automated low-emission manufacturing into durable structural panels that lock biogenic carbon into buildings as a substitute for OSB/plywood.
description: Plantd is an Oxford, North Carolina-based company founded in 2021 that cultivates fast-growing perennial Arundo donax grass and manufactures it into carbon-negative structural building panels intended as drop-in replacements for OSB/plywood. The company sequesters atmospheric CO2 in the walls and roofs of new homes, raised a $22M Series B in September 2025 (bringing total funding to ~$47.5M), and has a multi-year contract with D.R. Horton for 10 million panels.

name: Positive Biocarbon
tech_note: Manufactures and distributes graded biochar produced via pyrolysis of FSC-certified virgin waste-stream woody biomass for soil amendment and carbon sequestration applications.
description: Positive BioCarbon is a biochar manufacturing and distribution business operating as a division of Rectella International Ltd, headquartered in Burnley, Lancashire, UK. They supply FSC-accredited biochar derived from virgin waste-stream biomass (including invasive species clearance) to commercial horticulture, arboriculture, agriculture, and environmental remediation markets. The company has partnered with Lancashire County Council on soil remediation and atmospheric carbon capture trials.

name: Poás Bioenergy
tech_note: Builds hybrid biomass gasification reactors that convert wet tropical agricultural residues (coffee pulp, pineapple crowns, etc.) into syngas for on-site heat/power and ~20% biochar for soil application and carbon sequestration.
description: Poás Bioenergy is a University of Michigan-spinout startup (founded 2021/2022, HQ Ann Arbor with Costa Rica operations) commercializing a proprietary gasifier for agribusinesses in Latin America. The system monetizes waste handling, clean process heat, and biochar carbon credits shared with smallholder farmers. It has secured offtake agreements (e.g., Nicoverde pineapple) and investment from Mercy Corps Ventures, Brinc, Ecosphere Ventures, and others.

name: Pratt Energy
tech_note: Corn/milo ethanol producer in Pratt, Kansas planning to capture fermentation CO2 and inject it into an onsite Class VI sequestration well.
description: Pratt Energy, LLC operates a fuel ethanol plant in Pratt, Kansas processing regionally grown corn and milo. In late 2023 the company filed an EPA Class VI application to construct Kansas's first CO2 sequestration well alongside PureField Ingredients, though project specifics remain undisclosed and the permitting process is expected to take about two years. No public milestone updates have appeared on the project since the February 2024 news cycle.

name: Premier Forest
tech_note: Pyrolysis of wood-waste feedstock into carbon-dense biochar bricks (>85% carbon) certified under the Puro.earth biochar methodology.
description: Premier Forest Products is a UK timber importer and distributor based in South Wales that also operates a pyrolysis facility converting wood waste into biochar bricks. The biochar project is registered under the Puro.earth biochar methodology and issues CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs). Biochar is one revenue stream within a larger timber/panel-products business.

name: Preol
tech_note: Operates a PX1500 pyrolysis unit that converts rapeseed chaff (post-harvest agricultural residues) into biochar at its Lovosice facility, with expected annual production of ~715 tons of biochar from 2,350 tons of feedstock.
description: PREOL is the largest Czech rapeseed processor (subsidiary of the AGROFERT Group) producing biofuels, rapeseed oil, glycerin, and animal feed, with biochar added as a product line. Their pyrolysis unit for rapeseed chaff was commissioned in November 2024 following a CZK 38 million investment, producing biochar marketed as a soil amendment and long-term carbon storage medium.

name: Preterra
tech_note: Produces biochar from sustainably sourced BC wood waste (sawmill residues, forest-thinning slash) using SPSC pyrolysis retort/kiln technology, for soil amendment and carbon-optimized concrete applications.
description: Preterra BioCarbon Solutions, based on Salt Spring Island, BC, identifies proven European biochar technologies and brings them to North America, offering tools to sequester carbon in soils and building materials while improving wildfire resiliency. The company uses BC wood waste (slash from clearcut logging and sawmill residues) as feedstock, focusing on slash from forest-thinning for wildfire resiliency. They also sell bagged biochar to consumers via Amazon.ca.

name: ProE Bioenergie
tech_note: Produces and distributes biochar (under the Carbio® brand) made via pyrolysis of biomass at ~450°C for soil improvement, animal husbandry, and construction use.
description: ProE Bioenergie GmbH is a German company founded in 2006, based in Auenwald, that produces and sells biochar products (marketed as Carbio®) and offers consulting services around biochar, pyrolysis, and renewable energy. They supply EBC-certified and non-certified biochar for agricultural, animal, and industrial applications. Scale appears modest and focus is commercial biochar distribution rather than engineered CDR with carbon-credit issuance.

name: Prometheus Materials
tech_note: Uses microalgae combined with natural binders to biomineralize calcium carbonate, producing a carbon-negative cement replacement (ProZERO™) that sequesters CO2 in concrete.
description: Prometheus Materials is a Longmont, Colorado-based startup producing ProZERO™, a carbon-negative supplemental cement blend made by combining microalgae with natural binders, mimicking how corals and seashells form. The company sells ready-mix, precast and block products and licenses its formulation to concrete manufacturers, and was awarded a role in a 2024 $10M DOE grant on CDR measurement in cement and concrete.

name: Pronoe
tech_note: Pronoe builds modular electrochemical water-treatment units that connect to coastal industrial outflows (e.g. desalination plants) to dissolve crushed limestone into seawater, increasing ocean alkalinity and enhancing CO2 uptake.
description: Pronoe is a French developer of modular water-treatment units designed to connect to desalination plants and other coastal facilities, with systems that dissolve crushed limestone into seawater using an electrically driven process, producing alkaline discharge that boosts ocean CO2 absorption. The company claims its approach avoids lime calcination and on-site CO2 storage, reducing emissions and infrastructure requirements.

name: Provocative
tech_note: Builds data centers where conventional cooling is replaced by direct air capture units, using waste heat from AI compute to drive sorbent regeneration and deliver carbon-negative compute.
description: Provocative is a Boston-based Greentown Labs member founded in 2024 (CEO Nick Meyer, President Rob Fisher, Head of Engineering Andrew Bouma) that makes AI carbon-negative by combining data centers and direct air capture, replacing conventional cooling systems with carbon capture. The company is a DAC supplier integrating removal hardware directly into air-cooled high-performance compute facilities.

name: Pull to Refresh
tech_note: Operates a biomass-fueled pyrolysis process that converts shredded waste/garbage into carbon and hydrogen char for long-term soil carbon storage, with waste heat used to reduce cement-factory emissions; previously developed solar-powered autonomous vessels to sink invasive sargassum seaweed in the deep ocean as an XPRIZE Carbon Removal entrant.
description: Pull To Refresh Inc. is a California-based (San Francisco/Lucerne) carbon removal startup founded in 2021. Its current focus is a biomass-fueled process that transforms shredded garbage into carbon/hydrogen char for durable soil storage while supplying energy to cement production, having pivoted from an earlier XPRIZE-era concept of sinking invasive seaweed with autonomous solar vessels. The company self-identifies as a carbon removal supplier across biomass, biochar, and ocean pathways.

name: Pure Carbon Blue
tech_note: Direct Water Capture (DWC) — extracts dissolved CO2 from water (canals/ocean) via a two-stage process, producing purified CO2 for feedstock or permanent sequestration.
description: Pure Carbon Blue is a Dutch startup developing Direct Water Capture (DWC) technology that extracts CO2 from water bodies (canals, ocean), exploiting the fact that CO2 concentration in water is ~100x higher than in air. Captured CO2 is either used as bio-carbon feedstock for fuels, food, and materials (CCU) or routed to permanent storage (CDR). As of early 2025, the first pilot in Dutch canals was at TRL 5, with ambitions to scale to 1 Gt/year by 2030.

name: PureField Carbon
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from wheat-starch ethanol fermentation at its Russell, Kansas facility and permanently stores it via a Class VI injection well (bioethanol CCS / BECCS).
description: PureField Ingredients (operating carbon-capture through its Purefield Carbon Capture LLC subsidiary) received EPA approval in April 2026 to begin permanent geologic sequestration of CO2 from its Russell, Kansas ethanol and wheat-protein operations, and will launch CCS operations following commissioning. The permit allows injection of up to 1.8 million metric tons of CO2 into deep rock formations in Russell County over a 12-year period. The company is an integrated wheat-to-ethanol producer, making the fermentation-CO2 sequestration a BECCS CDR pathway.

name: PureField Ingredients
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from wheat-starch ethanol fermentation at its Russell, Kansas plant and permanently stores it underground via a newly permitted EPA Class VI injection well.
description: PureField Ingredients operates a U.S.-based integrated food ingredient and advanced biofuels platform in Russell, Kansas, producing wheat protein ingredients and low-carbon biofuels from U.S.-grown crops. In April 2026, the EPA approved the company's request to begin permanent geologic sequestration of CO2 from the Russell operations, and following final commissioning PureField will begin CCS operations. The Class VI well permit allows PureField Carbon Capture LLC to permanently store up to 1.8 million metric tons of CO2 over 12 years at a depth of about 3,500 feet.

name: Puro
tech_note: Puro.earth is a carbon removal standard and registry that certifies CDR suppliers via third-party verification and issues CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs) tracked in the Puro Registry.
description: Puro.earth is a Finland-based carbon removal standard and registry (majority-owned by Nasdaq since 2021) that certifies engineered CDR projects such as biochar, BECCS, DAC, and enhanced weathering. They issue and track CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs) representing verified, durable removals of 100+ years, and operate a supplier marketplace connecting buyers with certified CDR project developers. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves — they are the leading CDR-focused registry and standards body.

name: Puro.earth
tech_note: Puro.earth operates the Puro Standard and Puro Registry, certifying third-party-verified CORCs (CO2 Removal Certificates) for durable carbon removal suppliers across biochar, BECCS, DAC, ERW, and mineralization pathways.
description: Puro.earth is a carbon-crediting platform for durable carbon dioxide removal; via the Puro Standard's methodologies, suppliers that remove CO2 from the atmosphere to durable storages for at least 100 years are certified and issued CORCs into the transparent Puro Registry. It is a Nasdaq-backed standard/registry — part of the CDR ecosystem, not a physical supplier itself.

name: Pyrocal
tech_note: Pyrocal designs, manufactures and operates Continuous Carbonisation Technology (CCT) systems that pyrolyze biosolids and biomass into stable biochar, with heat recovery and emissions control.
description: Pyrocal is a Queensland, Australia-based supplier of proprietary continuous carbonisation (pyrolysis) systems that convert biosolids and organic biomass into biochar. They operate Australia's first biosolids carbonisation facility at Loganholme WWTP (Logan Water) and are building a system for the Capital Regional District in British Columbia, Canada, also supporting clients with carbon credit generation via their Terix Biochar brand.

name: Pyrogen
tech_note: Pyrogen produces biochar from waste/invasive biomass and infuses it into patented low-carbon concrete mix designs for construction products.
description: Pyrogen is a Kenya-based biochar-concrete carbon removals company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Gilgil. It holds a Kenyan utility model patent for biochar-infused concrete mixes and is developing a commercial pilot plant in Baringo County targeting ~3,000 tonnes CO2/yr of sequestration. It is a listed Puro.earth supplier and has piloted biochar-concrete affordable housing with CGAP (World Bank) and Habitat for Humanity.

name: Pyrogreen Energy
tech_note: Manufactures rotary kiln and screw-conveyor biomass pyrolysis/carbonization equipment to convert agricultural and forestry residues into stable biochar for carbon sequestration.
description: Pyrogreen Energy (Wuxi Powermax Renewable Energy Technology Co., Ltd.) is a China-based manufacturer of biomass pyrolysis, torrefaction and carbonization equipment that produces biochar for carbon sequestration and renewable energy applications. They offer rotary kiln and screw conveyor carbonization systems at scales from 50kg/hr to 5MT/hr and support customers in generating biochar carbon removal (BCR) credits, including through a pre-approval by Isometric.

name: Pyronam
tech_note: Operates low-tech pyrolysis plants in Namibia converting encroaching bush biomass (primarily acacia) into biochar for soil application and CDR carbon credits.
description: PyroNam is the Namibian subsidiary of German biochar CDR company PyroCCS GmbH, producing biochar from invasive bush biomass using locally-manufactured pyrolysis technology. It operates an industrial plant in Otjozondjupa/Otjiwarongo and partners with atmosfair to scale biochar CDR projects, with stated plans to deploy 50 plants across Namibia by 2030.

name: Qualterra
tech_note: Qualterra designs and operates Biomass Processing Units (BPUs) that use pyrolysis and gasification to convert agricultural and forestry residues into biochar soil amendment while generating renewable thermal energy.
description: Qualterra is an agricultural technology company whose Cheney, Washington biochar production facility was listed on the Climate Action Reserve (CAR) registry in April 2025 — only the third biochar project globally to achieve registration under CAR's U.S. Biochar Protocol. Headquartered in Washington State, Qualterra operates three commercial facilities that serve customers all over the world. They sell biochar to farmers and manufacture/sell biomass processing units to customers such as Vaagen Timbers, and partner with 3Degrees to deliver verified carbon removal credits.

name: RWE
tech_note: Post-combustion amine CO2 capture retrofitted to biomass-fired (wood pellet) power plants, with CO2 to be transported by pipeline/ship for permanent storage in North Sea offshore depleted gas fields.
description: RWE is a major German energy utility (~46.8 GW generation capacity) whose BECCUS initiative at its Dutch Amer and Eemshaven biomass-co-fired power plants is planned to deliver 11–14 Mt/yr of negative emissions from 2030, subject to technical and economic feasibility. The project is still in permitting/development with no final investment decision announced, and RWE's broader 2025–2030 capex plan has been reduced by €10B. CDR is a small part of RWE's overall business, but they would be the physical operator of the BECCS plants.

name: Rainbow Bee Eater
tech_note: Designs and builds modular ECHO2 pyrolysis systems that convert agricultural/wood residues into biochar, syngas, and wood vinegar, generating Puro.earth CORCs.
description: Rainbow Bee Eater's ECHO2 is a modular automated carbon-negative system for transforming low-value biomass residues into energy, biochar, wood vinegar, horticultural CO2 and carbon drawdown certificates. They were the first company outside Europe to produce and sell Puro.earth certified CORCs, generating roughly 1 CORC per tonne of feedstock. RBE installed a Mark 4 ECHO2 system at Holla-Fresh in June 2024 and is installing six Mark 4 modules at Katunga Fresh in Victoria.

name: Rainforest Builder
tech_note: Fully integrated tropical forest restoration developer planting native species across degraded land in West Africa (Sierra Leone, Ghana, Guinea) to generate Verra VM0047/CCB carbon removal credits.
description: Rainforest Builder is a UK-headquartered tropical reforestation company founded in 2022, operating in Sierra Leone, Ghana and Guinea with four active projects targeting 370,000+ hectares of restoration. In February 2026 it signed a 15-year, 1.8M-credit offtake with Microsoft from Project Buffalo (Sierra Leone), and in March 2026 closed a Series A led by BNP Paribas AM Alts with parallel project financing for Project Colobus in Ghana. The company owns the full restoration stack — nurseries, planting operations, MRV (Chameleon data platform), and carbon project development.

name: Re-Vi
tech_note: Re-Vi operates a large-scale pyrolysis biochar facility on Kangaroo Island, converting fire-damaged forestry biomass into agricultural-grade biochar and issuing Puro.earth CORC carbon removal credits.
description: Re-Vi is an Australian CDR developer building one of the world's largest biochar projects, on Kangaroo Island, South Australia. The project converts 4.5 million tonnes of bushfire-damaged timber plantations into biochar and durable CDR credits, with full production targeted for 2026 at ~200,000 tCO2/yr. It is listed as a supplier on Puro.earth.

name: ReCarber
tech_note: Platform and project development firm that commercializes and finances Nordic BECCS/bio-CCS projects by matching emitters (biomass heat/power operators) with CDR off-takers rather than owning capture assets itself.
description: ReCarber is a Stockholm-based startup founded in 2024 that operates a digital platform to commercialize and finance BECCS projects across the Nordics, partnering with biomass-fired heat and power operators such as Skellefteå Kraft. It raised SEK 60M (~$5.3M) seed in February 2025 from Luminar Ventures, Spintop Ventures, and Course Corrected, and acts as a matchmaker/commercial developer between CDR buyers and biogenic CO2 emitters rather than owning capture infrastructure.

name: ReGenEarth
