description: Telge Återvinning AB is a Swedish municipal waste management and recycling company that began producing biochar as a treatment for green waste in 2021 using first-of-its-kind-in-Europe CharMaker batch pyrolysis technology supplied by Australian firm Earth Systems. The Södertälje-based facility processes oversized green waste logs into biochar, and the project was successfully installed and commissioned in 2020 and registered for C-sink credits in 2021 by Telge. It operates as a subsidiary of the municipally owned Telge AB group.

name: Tellus
tech_note: Tellus converts biomass residues into biochar via pyrolysis, producing a stable carbon soil amendment sold as certified carbon removal.
description: Tellus Biocarbon is a Brazilian climate-tech company that works with local producers to transform biomass waste into biochar, marketed as a soil-improving, carbon-removing product. They are listed as a CDR30 member and their biochar is reportedly certified under international CDR standards.

name: Tera
tech_note: Tera operates a pyrolysis facility in Kisumu, Kenya that converts sugarcane bagasse into biochar, which is applied to farmland for soil improvement and long-term carbon sequestration.
description: Tera (Tera Carbon) is a Kenyan climate-tech startup producing biochar from sugarcane bagasse waste collected from mills in the Kisumu/Lake Victoria sugarcane belt. In 2025 it became the first African project developer independently validated on the Riverse carbon registry, and uses a custom digital MRV system (built with partner CYNK) to track carbon removal from biomass collection through pyrolysis and field application.

name: Terra Char
tech_note: Terra Char produces biochar via biomass pyrolysis and distributes it as a soil amendment for agricultural carbon sequestration through a multi-state U.S. distribution network.
description: Terra Char (trademark of BioEnergy Innovations Global, Inc., based in Columbia, Missouri) has marketed biochar products since 2009/2013 across the U.S. Midwest for soil amendment and carbon sink projects. The company sells biochar in retail buckets, totes, and bulk loads, and its founder Phil Blom recently joined Sustainable Green Team's Restore.Earth platform as a strategic ambassador for biochar verification.

name: Terra fertilis
tech_note: Slow-pyrolysis of French forest duramen (hardwood core) to produce high-porosity, high-carbon biochar sold as soil amendment for agriculture and horticulture.
description: Terra Fertilis is a French biochar producer based in Argentan (Normandy), operating a pyrolysis plant that converts sustainably-sourced French forest biomass into biochar soil amendments for professional agriculture and consumer gardening. It was the first biochar to receive ANSES market authorization in France and is EBC-certified. In 2024 its activities were consolidated under SYLVA FERTILIS INTERNATIONAL within Groupe SLB.

name: TerraBaru
tech_note: Pyrolysis of agricultural waste biomass to produce stable biochar for soil amendment and durable carbon storage.
description: TerraBaru is an Indonesian biochar producer that converts agricultural waste into engineered biochar ("TerraKarbon") via pyrolysis, generating carbon removal credits alongside soil, infrastructure, and energy applications. The company operates in Indonesia with a Singapore office and is actively representing itself at carbon industry events in 2025.

name: TerraFixing
tech_note: Ottawa-based DAC company using structured zeolite packing in a temperature vacuum swing adsorption (TVSA) cycle, designed specifically to operate in cold, dry climates.
description: TerraFixing is an Ottawa-based direct air capture company developing cold-climate DAC technology using structured zeolite packing to capture CO2, aiming to fit a 1,000-tonnes-per-year unit into a shipping container with costs below $100 per tonne at scale. In 2024 it signed a $10 million CAD commercial agreement with Tugliq Énergie for two cold-climate DAC units in Northern Canada.

name: TerraNova Energy
tech_note: TerraNova Energy is a German technology provider and licensor of the TerraNova®ultra hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) process, which converts moist biomass and sewage sludge into hydrochar — a lignite-like, carbon-rich solid suitable for permanent CO2 storage.
description: TerraNova Energy is a technology provider for upgrading organic waste streams via Thermal Hydrolysis Process (THP) and Hydrothermal Carbonization (HTC). Its TerraNova®ultra process enables the use of moist biomass, particularly waste streams such as sewage sludge or organic waste, to generate "Hydrochar," in which over 90% of the biomass carbon is stored; it has a stability comparable to lignite and is positioned for permanent CO2 removal. A plant based on TerraNova HTC technology including a pyrolysis unit was built in Mexico City to process 23,000 tons of organic waste per year.

name: TerraWatt
tech_note: TerraWatt couples pyrolysis with biological methanation to convert non-fermentable biomass (green/wood waste) into biochar for soil sequestration plus renewable biomethane.
description: TerraWatt is a French startup (Meslay-du-Maine, founded 2014) developing a patented process that combines pyrolysis and biological methanation to produce biochar and biomethane from woody and non-fermentable biomass. The biochar is used as a soil amendment for long-term carbon sequestration, while the syngas is biologically converted into biomethane for grid injection or transport fuel. The company participates in EU Horizon projects FENIX and SEMPRE-BIO.

name: Terradot
tech_note: Terradot spreads crushed basalt (and, post-Eion, olivine) on agricultural land to accelerate silicate weathering, permanently sequestering atmospheric CO2 as bicarbonates while using biogeochemical MRV to quantify removal.
description: Terradot is a U.S.-headquartered Enhanced Rock Weathering carbon removal supplier founded in 2022 at Stanford, with large-scale basalt deployments across 5,000+ hectares of Brazilian farmland. The company has raised $58.2M, holds major offtake contracts with Google (200,000 tonnes), Frontier, and Microsoft, and in February 2026 acquired Eion's assets to form one of the largest contracted ERW portfolios globally (~400,000 tonnes).

name: Terraformation
tech_note: Terraformation develops native, biodiverse reforestation projects (including mangrove and tropical forest restoration) and operates the Terraware open-source forest-management platform to generate high-integrity carbon removal credits.
description: Terraformation is a forestry startup founded in 2019 by former Reddit CEO Yishan Wong that scales native, biodiverse reforestation projects across Africa, Latin America, and Southeast Asia. In 2025 it restored 2,155 hectares, planted 5.4 million native trees, and had two supported projects enter validation under Verra's carbon standards. The company also develops Terraware, an open-source forest-management platform, and runs a Seed to Carbon Forest Accelerator for partner forestry teams.

name: Terrafront
tech_note: Terrafront develops carbon removal projects across multiple pathways—biochar from agricultural residues (Terrachar), agroforestry/reforestation (Terraroots), and enhanced rock weathering (TerraRevive)—primarily working with smallholder farmers in South Asia and Africa.
description: Terrafront develops climate change adaptation and mitigation infrastructure in South Asia and Africa, operating three project lines: Terrachar for biochar, Terraroots for agroforestry/reforestation under Verra VM47 and Gold Standard ARR, and TerraRevive for enhanced rock weathering. They collaborate with Carboneers to process agricultural residues into biochar and heat, and partner with Together for Restoration to work with smallholder farmers in Assam, India.

name: Terranova
tech_note: Terranova builds autonomous tracked robots ("Prometheus"/"Ark") that drill wells 40-60 ft underground and inject a wood-waste slurry to lift subsiding, flood-prone land while sequestering biogenic carbon in anoxic subsurface storage.
description: Terranova is a San Rafael/Berkeley, California startup founded in 2021 that uses AI-guided terraforming robots to inject waste-wood slurry deep underground, simultaneously lifting flood-prone terrain and permanently burying biomass for carbon removal credits. The company emerged from stealth in November 2025 with a $7M seed round led by Outlander and Congruent Ventures (valuation $25.1M), with plans to deploy its first projects in San Rafael. Its primary commercial pitch is climate adaptation (flood defense), with CDR credits as a revenue co-product.

name: Terrasols
tech_note: Crushes volcanic basalt to optimal particle size and spreads it on Indian agricultural fields to accelerate silicate weathering reactions that convert atmospheric CO₂ into stable bicarbonates/carbonates.
description: Terrasols (terrasols.earth) is an India-based enhanced rock weathering supplier that crushes volcanic basalt and applies it on farmers' fields to permanently remove atmospheric CO₂ while improving soil health. They are profiled in the remove. Carbon Removal Accelerator as "Harnessing the power of ERW to permanently remove CO₂ while regenerating soils and enhancing microbial activity for long-term fertility." They also describe themselves as a sustainability consulting firm, but the operational activity is ERW deployment on smallholder farms.

name: Terraton
tech_note: Full-stack biochar franchise platform: hardware, operating SaaS, and MRV/credit sales for pyrolysis facilities converting agricultural waste into stable soil carbon.
description: Terraton is a U.S.-based biochar carbon removal platform that partners with agribusinesses in emerging markets to build and operate biochar production facilities, providing hardware, SaaS, financing, and MRV. The company raised an $11.5 million seed round in August 2025 led by Lowercarbon Capital and Gigascale Capital, with participation from ANA Future Frontier Fund, East Japan Railway's Takanawa Gateway fund, and angels including Jeff Dean and Bret Taylor. It has developed two facilities in Africa, one in Ghana and the other in Kenya.

name: The Carbon Removers
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from whisky distilleries and biogas plants in the UK and stores it via mineralization in building aggregates or permanent geological storage under the North Sea.
description: The Carbon Removers, formerly known as Carbon Capture Scotland, is a Scottish company specializing in engineered biogenic carbon dioxide removal, co-founded by brothers Richard and Ed Nimmons, having grown from dry ice production into a carbon removal provider. The company scales biogenic carbon capture and storage (BECCS) in Scotland, capturing CO₂ from distilleries and biogas facilities for mineralization into building aggregates and long-term storage. They also have an agreement to permanently sequester 50,000 tons of CO2 beneath the North Sea for the Greensand Future project.

name: The Future Forest Company
tech_note: Native tree planting and peatland restoration on UK estates, generating Woodland and Peatland Carbon Code units.
description: The Future Forest Company is a UK-based reforestation and peatland restoration developer operating sites in Scotland and Northern England, issuing Woodland Carbon Units and Peatland Carbon Units under the UK Woodland Carbon Code and Peatland Code. They have planted over one million trees and published a 2025 Impact Report. Their enhanced-weathering arm spun out as UNDO in 2022, leaving the parent focused on nature-based removals.

name: The New Black Biochar
tech_note: Operates a continuous-flow pyrolysis kiln in Tasmania that converts sawmill waste and other organic feedstocks into biochar for soil and remediation use.
description: The New Black Biochar is a small Tasmanian biochar producer co-founded in 2021 by Christina Giudici and Bodie Cavanagh, making biochar from sawmill and other organic waste at a kiln co-located with Dovetail Timbers. The company sells biochar for home gardens, regenerative agriculture, and environmental remediation, and is working toward scaling up to full commercial production.

name: Three Mountains Cocoa
tech_note: Host agribusiness for a biochar facility that pyrolyzes cocoa pod husk waste into stable carbon, developed in partnership with Terraton.
description: Three Mountains Cocoa (TMC) is a Ghanaian cocoa cooperative founded by Leslie Agyare that works with over 2,000 farmers across 15 communities producing organic single-origin cocoa beans. The Three Mountains Cocoa biochar project in Ghana, developed with Terraton and with preliminary approval from Puro.earth, is expected to contribute to over 20,000 tons of annual CO₂ removal, and Terraset has committed a six-figure carbon credit pre-purchase from the project. TMC serves as the host site and feedstock supplier (cocoa pod husk) for the biochar facility, which is listed on Puro.earth under its name.

name: Tierra Foods
tech_note: Uses oxalogenic trees (ramón/Brosimum alicastrum, English Oak) in agroforestry systems to drive the oxalate-carbonate pathway, precipitating atmospheric CO2 as stable calcium carbonate in soil, with AI-driven MRV.
description: Tierra Foods is a UK climate tech startup developing a carbon-removal system centred on plants that perform biomineralisation — specifically oxalogenic species that convert atmospheric CO2 into calcium carbonate stored in soil. The company develops agroforestry projects using biomineralisation-capable plants like the Uje/ramón tree (Brosimum alicastrum) via the Oxalate-Carbonate Pathway, producing both permanent carbon removal and sustainable food ingredients. It has raised a $520K round announced in early 2025 and is backed by £496,000 of Innovate UK funding for an AI-based MRV methodology with the University of Huddersfield.

name: Tierra Prieta
tech_note: Pyrolyzes waste pecan shells at an industrial facility in Parras, Coahuila, Mexico to produce biochar used as a soil amendment, generating durable carbon removal credits certified under Puro.earth.
description: Tierra Prieta is a Mexican biochar producer with a facility in Parras, Coahuila that uses pecan shells as feedstock, and is certifying its carbon removal for the voluntary carbon market. Carbon removal was to be certified by Puro.earth in Q2 2024, with current biochar production capacity of 500 tons per year, inaugurated in May 2023. The startup recently obtained certification of its first 1,200 carbon removal credits.

name: Timber Finance
tech_note: Swiss wealth manager and methodology developer creating Timber Carbon Capture & Storage (TCCS) certificates under an ICROA standard, mobilizing capital for mass-timber construction as long-term CO2 storage.
description: Timber Finance (Timber Finance Management AG), founded 2021 in Zurich, is a specialized investment advisor and methodology developer focused on mass timber as a carbon storage pathway. They are developing the world's first ICROA-aligned methodology for timber carbon removal certificates and offer financial products channeling capital into the forest-to-frame timber value chain. They do not physically operate removal facilities themselves — they build the financial/MRV infrastructure for timber-based CDR.

name: TimberTurn
tech_note: TimberTurn collects non-merchantable waste wood from wildfire fuel-thinning treatments and sequesters it via engineered anoxic burial with MRV monitoring to produce durable carbon removal credits.
description: TimberTurn is a Canadian CDR supplier that converts uneconomical waste wood from fuel-thinning operations into durable carbon storage through engineered biomass burial. The company pairs wildfire risk reduction with permanent carbon sequestration, offering landowners revenue-sharing partnerships and using geotechnical engineering plus MRV technology to verify storage. This is a biomass burial (BiCRS / Terrestrial Storage of Biomass) pathway — not BECCS as previously tagged.

name: Tivano Carbon
tech_note: Harvests invasive encroacher bush from Namibian savannas and stores it in engineered, sensor-monitored underground vaults designed for centuries of stability, generating biomass-burial carbon removal credits.
description: Tivano Carbon restores Namibia's savanna rangelands by converting invasive encroacher bush into permanently stored carbon using engineered underground burial in sensor-monitored vaults with MRV to produce verified carbon removal credits. The company collaborates with local farmers and experts from TU Berlin on its carbon vaults and landscape regeneration initiatives. This is a biomass burial supplier, not BECCS.

name: TorrCoal
tech_note: Torrefaction (mild pyrolysis at 200-300°C) of wood/agro residues and scrap wood into bio-carbon powder used mainly as a fossil-coal substitute in steel, cement and chemicals.
description: TorrCoal is a Belgian torrefaction technology specialist (founded 2005, based in Dilsen-Stokkem) that was acquired by Dutch climate-tech firm Perpetual Next in September 2021 and now operates as its subsidiary. The company uses torrefaction (mild pyrolysis) to convert wood and agro-residues — including scrap wood and plastic-containing waste — into bio-carbon powder supplied to steel (ArcelorMittal), chemical and cement industries as a fossil coal replacement. Parent Perpetual Next frames the activity as carbon removal via stable bio-carbon, though a significant share of output is used as a reductant/fuel which raises CCU-vs-CDR questions.

name: Toshiba ESS
tech_note: Post-combustion amine-based CO2 capture retrofitted to a 50 MW palm-kernel-shell biomass power plant, with CO2 liquefaction and planned ship transport for storage.
description: Toshiba Energy Systems & Solutions (Toshiba ESS) is the energy division of Toshiba Corporation that developed and operates a large-scale BECCS demonstration facility at the 50 MW Mikawa biomass power plant (operated by its subsidiary SIGMA POWER Ariake) in Omuta, Japan, capturing more than 500 tonnes of CO2 per day from palm kernel shell-fueled flue gas. The project, funded by Japan's Ministry of the Environment, began operations in 2020 and expanded under a FY2021–FY2025 demonstration including CO2 liquefaction and transport. Toshiba ESS's core business remains power generation equipment; CDR is an R&D/demonstration activity within the division.

name: Towing
tech_note: Produces "Soratan," a high-performance biochar inoculated with microorganisms and mixed with organic fertilizer, applied to farmland for soil improvement and carbon sequestration under Japan's J-Credit Scheme.
description: TOWING is a Japanese Nagoya University spinout founded in 2020 that has developed a crop cultivation system to enable more sustainable farming practices. In June 2023, a project of Soratan was registered under Japan's J-Credit Scheme for "Biochar Application to Farmland" and has issued carbon credits three times. The company partners with firms like Suntory and Biocare to scale biochar-based carbon removal globally.

name: Travertine
tech_note: Uses an electrochemical process to capture CO2 from air and permanently sequester it as solid carbonate minerals, while co-producing sulfuric acid and green hydrogen from upcycled industrial sulfate waste.
description: Travertine Technologies is a Boulder, CO-based CDR company spun out of UC Berkeley in 2022 by Prof. Laura Lammers. Its electrochemical platform mineralizes atmospheric CO2 into carbonates while upcycling sulfate waste from mining/fertilizer industries into sulfuric acid, targeting decarbonization of cement, critical-element extraction, and fertilizer production.

name: Treeconomy
tech_note: Treeconomy provides remote-sensing (satellite + drone LiDAR) and AI-based MRV for nature-based carbon projects, and operates a marketplace connecting project developers with corporate buyers of afforestation/reforestation carbon removal credits.
description: Treeconomy is a London-based CDR enabling-tech company focused on MRV and project enablement for nature-based carbon removal. It uses high-resolution satellite imagery, drone LiDAR and AI to quantify and monitor forest carbon stocks, supports project developers from concept to credit issuance, and runs a marketplace for afforestation/reforestation removal credits.

name: Tropicarbon
tech_note: Spreads fine silicate rock dust on Colombian farmland to accelerate weathering and permanently sequester CO2, with proprietary aqueous-phase MRV aligned to Isometric and Puro.earth protocols.
description: Tropicarbon leads Enhanced Rock Weathering in Colombia, targeting 1 million tons of CO2 removal by 2030, with a mission to achieve trustworthy carbon removal with innovative technology while optimizing benefits for local farmers. In partnership with Universidad del Norte, Tropicarbon launched the Barranquilla Project, testing how its rock powder interacts with dozens of Colombian soils under tropical conditions. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Colombia, the company has raised $100K with investment from GLOCAL (Argentina).

name: Truecoco
tech_note: Controlled pyrolysis of coconut husk agricultural waste in Ghana to produce Puro.earth-certified biochar applied as soil amendment.
description: Truecoco is a Ghana-based biochar carbon removal developer that originated as an organic coconut processor in 2017 and launched West Africa's first industrial-scale biochar facility in 2025, using coconut husk waste as feedstock. The company is Puro.earth certified and signed a multi-year offtake agreement with Climeworks extending to 2032. It aims to remove 250,000 tonnes of CO2 by 2030 while benefiting smallholder farmers.

name: Truecoco Ghana
tech_note: Operates a 2 MT/hour continuous pyrolysis (two-layer rotary drum kiln) plant in Ghana's Western Region that converts waste coconut husk from smallholder farmers into biochar used as soil amendment.
description: Truecoco Ghana is a Ghana-based biochar CDR supplier that sources waste coconut husks from smallholder farmer networks and pyrolyzes them into biochar for soil amendment and durable carbon storage. The project is certified under Puro.earth, received $3.3M in investment from GIP Ghana/BII in 2024, and produced its first tons of biochar in April 2025, targeting 250,000 tCO2 removed by 2030.

name: UNDO
tech_note: UNDO spreads crushed silicate rock (basalt in UK, wollastonite in Canada) on agricultural land to accelerate natural weathering, permanently mineralizing atmospheric CO2 as bicarbonate.
description: UNDO is a UK-based carbon removal developer specializing in Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW), operating in the UK and Canada with a hub in Kingston, Ontario and an expanding footprint via a Brazil partnership. The company was named one of four global winners of the $100M XPRIZE Carbon Removal competition in April 2025, and has delivery agreements with Microsoft, Barclays, British Airways, McLaren, and Stripe. UNDO handles both physical feedstock deployment and MRV, making it a full-stack ERW supplier.

name: Ucaneo
tech_note: Ucaneo develops a biomimetic electrochemical Direct Air Capture system using a specialized solvent that mimics the human lung to capture CO2 at room temperature, powered by renewable electricity.
description: Ucaneo is a Berlin-based DAC startup founded in 2022 that operates an industrial pilot capturing 30-50 tons CO2/year and is building what it claims will be Germany's largest DAC demonstration plant, targeted for commissioning in H1 2026. The company raised €6.75M in seed funding in September 2024, with Aramco Ventures joining the round in March 2025.

name: Uisa
tech_note: Sugarcane/corn biorefinery planning post-fermentation CO2 capture and geological injection into the Parecis Sedimentary Basin at its Nova Olímpia plant.
description: Uisa is one of Brazil's largest integrated biorefineries, producing sugar, ethanol, renewable energy, and yeast from sugarcane at its Nova Olímpia plant in Mato Grosso. The company announced BECCS plans to capture CO2 from its corn-to-ethanol operations and inject it into the Parecis Sedimentary Basin ~15 km from the plant, with drilling scheduled for 2024 and construction for 2025. The project is still in pre-operational development and depends on Brazil's CCS regulatory framework.

name: Underground Forest
tech_note: Drives Norway spruce wooden piles into anoxic Dutch peat and clay soils below the water table as building foundations, storing biogenic carbon for 1,000+ years while replacing emissions-heavy concrete piles.
description: Founded by Kees de Gruiter in 2023, Underground Forest revives ancient wood-piling techniques for long-term carbon storage, using sustainably sourced logs to store CO₂ for up to 1,000 years while offering solutions for peatland restoration and climate-neutral housing, with support from CarbonFix preparing to sequester its first kiloton of CO₂ by 2025. Their method is certified according to the IPCC CDR Taxonomy and the EU CRCF programme with a permanence of more than a thousand years. In 2025, greenhouse builder KUBO launched a partnership with Underground Forest to use wooden pile foundations that enable long-term CO2 storage.

name: Unemit
tech_note: Unemit develops modular, factory-assembled Direct Air Capture contactors using a chemical sorbent regenerated with low-temperature heat, enabling renewable-powered CO2 capture for permanent underground storage.
description: Unemit's DAC technology is designed to be scalable to gigatons, relying on existing supply chains, with CO2 captured in modular, factory-assembled contactors and extracted from the sorbent using low-temperature heat that can be powered by concentrated solar or other renewables, then permanently stored underground. The company is a Berkeley, California-based startup backed by Breakthrough Energy Fellows.

name: United Earth Energy
tech_note: Builds a containerized, mobile pyrolysis reactor (UNI-Box) that thermally decomposes organic waste in an oxygen-free environment to produce biochar, bio-oil, and syngas.
description: United Earth Energy is a US-based waste-to-energy technology company selling the UNI-Box mobile pyrolysis system, which converts agricultural, municipal, and industrial organic waste into biochar, bio-oil, and syngas. The biochar output provides carbon sequestration and soil enrichment, while the system also processes non-CDR feedstocks such as tires and plastics. The company markets the UNI-Box to municipalities, farms, and industrial clients and references carbon credit eligibility as a customer value proposition.

name: Unyte
tech_note: Unyte operates pyrolysis furnaces in Theddingworth, UK to convert hemp production waste and local green/wood waste into biochar, generating carbon removal credits via the Riverse registry.
description: Unyte Group is a UK-based sustainability group whose Unyte Hemp/Unyte Solutions division produces biochar from hemp and wood waste using Multi-Eco pyrolysing furnaces at a facility in Leicestershire. The project is registered under the Riverse biochar methodology and the company is an active participant in UK hemp-carbon research consortia including CHCx3.

name: UrjanovaC
tech_note: Aqueous-based carbon capture using a patented earth-abundant catalyst that captures CO2 from flue gas or ambient air in water (including wastewater/seawater) and permanently fixes it as stable mineral carbonates.
description: UrjanovaC is a Mumbai-based startup spun out of IIT Bombay's DST-supported National Centre of Excellence in Carbon Capture and Utilization, co-founded by Prof. Vikram Vishal and Prof. Arnab Dutta. The company is developing a catalyst-based aqueous CO2 capture technology (TRL 5) that works on both industrial flue gas and ambient air, with captured CO2 converted into stable mineral carbonates. The team is building a 3 tonnes-per-day pilot at IIT Bombay.

name: V-Grid Energy Systems
tech_note: VGrid operates modular, trailer-based high-temperature biomass gasification units ("Bioservers") that convert agricultural waste (e.g. pistachio shells) into renewable electricity and biochar, which stabilizes carbon for 1,000+ years.
description: V-Grid Energy Systems is a California-based clean energy and biochar producer headquartered in Camarillo, operating Bioserver gasification units in the Central Valley since 2019. The company sells CORC carbon removal credits through Puro.earth and markets biochar and bio-liquid products under the Persist and Karrikaid brands.

name: Valero
tech_note: Valero's ethanol segment supplies biogenic fermentation CO2 from eight Midwest ethanol plants to Summit Carbon Solutions' pipeline for geologic sequestration, a BECCS configuration; Valero also hosts a refinery-based SMR CCS project at Port Arthur (fossil, not CDR).
description: Valero Energy is a major U.S. oil refiner and the world's second-largest corn ethanol producer. Summit Carbon Solutions announced a partnership with Valero to connect eight of its ethanol plants in Iowa, Nebraska, Minnesota, and South Dakota to Summit's pipeline, which is expected to capture 3.1 million metric tons of CO2 each year. CDR is a minor part of Valero's overall business but the ethanol-plant CO2 capture qualifies as BECCS when paired with geologic storage.

name: Varaha
tech_note: Develops biochar via industrial gasification reactors plus regenerative agriculture, agroforestry and enhanced rock weathering projects with smallholder farmers in South Asia and Africa, using an in-house digital MRV system to generate verified carbon removal credits.
description: Varaha is an India-based carbon removal project developer operating across India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Ivory Coast, working with ~170,000+ smallholder farmers. Their primary pathway is industrial and artisanal biochar (registered on Puro.earth), supplemented by regenerative agriculture, agroforestry, and enhanced rock weathering. Major offtake deals with Google (100,000t, Jan 2025) and Microsoft (100,000t+, Jan 2026), and they raised $20M of a $45M Series B led by WestBridge Capital in Feb 2026.

name: Varhad
tech_note: Produces biochar via Kon-Tiki kilns and industrial pyrolysis reactors using cotton and pigeon pea stalks from farmer cooperatives in Maharashtra, India, and is expanding into biomethanol-linked CDR.
description: VCAP, a Varhad Group subsidiary, is India's largest artisanal biochar producer and registered C-sink manager, offering expert advisory on eco-friendly biocoal and biochar production. The company partnered with Japan's Green Carbon Inc. and Switzerland's Carbonfuture on a large-scale CDR project that will make approximately 120,300 tonnes of carbon removal credits available via Carbonfuture. As of early 2026, Varhad is scaling up carbon-removal capacity using both biochar and biomethanol pathways in an integrated biomass-to-biofuel and CDR model.

name: Varme
tech_note: Municipal solid waste incineration for electricity generation with post-combustion amine carbon capture and permanent geologic CO2 storage, generating BECCS credits from the biogenic fraction of the waste.
description: Varme Energy is a Canadian subsidiary of Norway-based Varme Energy AS developing Canada's first commercial-scale waste-to-energy facility with integrated carbon capture and storage in Alberta's Industrial Heartland. The AIH1 project targets commercial operations in 2029 and plans to deliver approximately 130,000 tonnes/year of BECCS carbon removal credits, with Carbon Direct marketing the credits. The project has received AUC approval, Alberta government funding, and partnership commitments from Canada Growth Fund and Gibson Energy.

name: Vault 44.01
tech_note: Vault 44.01 develops, permits, and operates geological CO2 storage projects (Class VI wells) for industrial emitters, with a heavy focus on capturing biogenic CO2 from ethanol fermentation plants and permanently sequestering it in saline formations such as the Mt. Simon sandstone.
description: Vault 44.01 is a North American carbon capture and sequestration (CCS) project developer headquartered in Calgary and Denver, backed by Grey Rock Investment Partners. They partner with ethanol producers (e.g., Cardinal Ethanol via the One Carbon Partnership JV, Alto Ingredients) and other industrial emitters to capture, transport, and permanently store CO2 underground, delivering BECCS-style removals when the source CO2 is biogenic.

name: Vaulted Deep
tech_note: Deep-well slurry injection of carbon-rich organic waste (biosolids, manure, paper sludge) into sedimentary rock and salt cavern formations for 1000+ year geologic storage, certified under Isometric's Biomass Geological Storage Protocol.
description: Vaulted Deep is a US-based carbon removal supplier that injects carbon-rich organic waste (biosolids, manure, paper sludge, agricultural residues) deep underground into sedimentary rock formations and salt caverns for permanent geologic sequestration. The company is certified by Isometric and has signed major offtake deals including a 4.9 Mt agreement with Microsoft (July 2025) and 50kt with Google (Sept 2025).

name: Verde Resources
tech_note: Produces biochar from biogenic waste and embeds it in asphalt (BioAsphalt™) for road construction to achieve durable, verifiable carbon sequestration.
description: Verde Resources (OTCQB: VRDR) is a US-listed sustainable infrastructure company that produces BioAsphalt™, incorporating engineered biochar into road construction materials to create durable carbon sinks. The company generated the first Puro.earth-verified carbon removal credits from an asphalt application (8 tons) via its NCAT pilot, and in March 2026 signed a supply deal with Biochar Solutions LLC for up to 38,500 tons of biochar annually, alongside a $2M strategic investment from Ergon.

name: Verdox
tech_note: MIT spin-off developing electro-swing adsorption (electrochemical) carbon capture using quinone-based electrodes that bind and release CO2 via small voltage changes, targeting both dilute industrial off-gas and direct air capture.
description: Verdox is a Boston-based electric carbon capture company founded in 2019 out of MIT, commercializing an all-electric electro-swing adsorption process that captures CO2 using electricity instead of heat or pressure. In November 2025 it completed a successful two-month industrial trial capturing CO2 from 1%-concentration aluminum smelter off-gas at Hydro's Sunndal plant in Norway, and commissioned a pilot-scale unit in October 2025 ahead of 2026 customer pilots. The company is backed by $80M from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Prelude Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, and strategic investor Hydro.

name: Verora
tech_note: Verora pyrolyzes clean tree/shrub cuttings in a PYREG plant at 500–650°C to produce EBC-certified biochar sold as soil amendment, feed additive and stable-litter product.
description: Verora is a Swiss cooperative of farmers in Zug that processes green waste and tree/shrub cuttings into climate-friendly products including humus compost, biochar (Pflanzenkohle), Terra Preta and quality wood chips. The biochar is produced in Neuheim using a PYREG pyrolysis unit, supplemented by partner producers using BIOMACON or CT-Schuster pyrolysis equipment. The CO2 sink services are transferred with the product and already included in the price unless the buyer requests otherwise.

name: Verra
tech_note: Verra is a non-profit carbon standards body and registry that administers the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Program, certifying and issuing carbon credits (VCUs) for projects including nature-based removals, and operating the Verra Registry.
description: Verra is a US-based non-profit that operates the world's largest voluntary carbon crediting program (VCS) and public registry, setting methodologies and certifying projects that issue Verified Carbon Units. It is core ecosystem infrastructure — a standards-setter, verifier, and registry rather than a physical CDR supplier — and is widely used across forestry, REDD+, and emerging engineered-removal pathways.

name: Vesta
tech_note: Vesta places ground olivine sand in nearshore coastal waters to accelerate marine enhanced rock weathering (a form of ocean alkalinity enhancement), causing the ocean to absorb and permanently store atmospheric CO2 as dissolved bicarbonate.
description: Vesta (formerly Project Vesta) is a US-based marine CDR supplier pioneering "Coastal Carbon Capture" — the deployment of olivine sand in coastal waters to drive ocean alkalinity enhancement and remove atmospheric CO2. With the placement of 8,200 metric tons of olivine sand off the coast of Duck, NC, Vesta deployed a first-of-its-kind marine carbon removal pilot, estimated to remove approximately 5,000 metric tons of CO2. The company completed a Series A financing round led by the Grantham Trust's Neglected Climate Opportunities program.

name: Viochar
tech_note: Viochar produces biochar in Denmark using pyrolysis batch reactors, sequestering carbon and improving soil quality.
description: Viochar is a Danish startup focused on biochar production in Denmark that has entered a strategic partnership with PUHI to identify joint opportunities in production plants and sales of biochar and CDR. The company runs pyrolysis batch reactors to convert biomass into stable biochar for soil amendment and carbon removal.

name: Viridor
tech_note: Post-combustion amine capture (Shell CANSOLV / Technip Energies Canopy) retrofitted to an energy-from-waste incinerator, with captured biogenic CO2 piped to offshore geological storage via the HyNet network.
description: Viridor is a UK waste management and recycling company operating the country's largest fleet of Energy-from-Waste (EfW) facilities. It is developing a large-scale BECCS project at its Runcorn ERF that, once operational, would capture ~900,000 tCO2/yr of which ~450,000 t would be biogenic (negative emissions), connecting to the HyNet/Eni CO2 transport and storage network. The project completed FEED in 2025 but Viridor opted to split delivery into phases rather than submit a single planning application.

name: Vital Chemical
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of sustainably sourced forestry residues and reclaimed construction timbers, sold as a soil amendment and integrated into hydromulch revegetation products.
description: Vital Chemical is a long-established Australian company (based in Darra, QLD) whose main business is erosion control, dust suppression, water treatment, and revegetation products for mining, civil construction, and infrastructure. As part of this portfolio they produce Vital Biochar — pyrolysed from reclaimed construction timber and forestry residues — which they sell as a soil amendment and incorporate into hydromulch products (VE Char-Matt, VE Organic-Matt). They are a foundation member of the ANZ Biochar Industry Group (ANZBIG).

name: Vycarb
tech_note: Vycarb builds modular, sensor-driven hardware/software systems that add alkaline minerals to CO2-rich coastal and industrial waters, converting CO2 into stable bicarbonate via ocean alkalinity enhancement with real-time MRV.
description: Brooklyn-based climate tech startup founded in 2022 by Dr. Garrett Boudinot that deploys modular autonomous OAE systems to permanently store CO2 as bicarbonate in natural waters. Vycarb operates a flagship pilot at Brooklyn Navy Yard on the East River (~100 tCO2/yr) and targets integration with cement, steel, power, bioenergy and port facilities. Closed a $5M seed round in October 2025 led by Twynam with MOL Switch, Hatch Blue, Clocktower Ventures, Idemitsu, SGInnovate, and Shell.

name: Växjö Energi
tech_note: Swedish municipal energy utility developing bioenergy carbon capture and storage (BECCS) at its biomass-fired Sandviksverket CHP plant, targeting ~200,000 t CO2/yr captured and permanently stored (e.g. Greensand, North Sea) from 2028.
description: Växjö Energi AB is a Swedish municipal energy company collaborating with Sumitomo SHI FW on hot potassium carbonate carbon capture at its fully fossil-free CHP plant, aiming to capture approximately 200,000 tonnes of CO2 annually starting in 2028. Forestry residues fuel their bioenergy plant, flue-gas CO2 is separated and liquefied, then transported for permanent storage in the North Sea 2,000–3,000 m below sea level, yielding carbon dioxide removal. A permit application with Mark- och miljödomstolen is in progress, with a scoping consultation held in November 2024.

name: Wakefield BioChar
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of woody biomass and paper mill waste, sold as retail and agricultural soil conditioners.
description: Wakefield BioChar is a US family-owned biochar producer founded in 2014, headquartered in Valdosta, Georgia. It converts low-value woody biomass and paper mill waste into biochar soil conditioners sold through retail channels and for agriculture, sequestering carbon while improving soil health.

name: Waste to Energy
tech_note: Wholesale distributor of biochar (granular and liquid) sourced from virgin wood feedstock for nationwide US markets.
description: Waste to Energy (WTE) is a US-based wholesale distributor of biochar, offering product in granular and liquid forms derived from virgin wood biomass. They are listed on the US Biochar Initiative member directory and describe themselves as the largest wholesale bio carbon provider in the US. Limited recent public signals (news, press, funding) are available.

name: WasteX
tech_note: WasteX manufactures a proprietary small-scale, semi-automated pyrolysis carbonizer that converts agricultural biomass waste (from mills, poultry, rice, corn farms) into biochar for soil application, bundled with carbon credit facilitation.
description: WasteX is a Singapore-based seed-stage company founded in 2022 by Pawel Kuznicki that develops biochar-based fertilizers. The firm provides an end-to-end solution to farms and agricultural producers, helping them convert biomass waste into biochar; it invests, develops, and operates facilities while partner mills provide biomass. It is a VC-backed climate tech startup headquartered in Singapore with operating teams in the Philippines and Indonesia.

name: Waterberg Carbon Co
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of biomass as a carbon-removal pathway, reportedly in partnership with technology providers.
description: Waterberg Carbon Co is described as a South African biochar-focused CDR company that partners with technology providers to produce biochar for carbon removal. Public information is very limited — the company's only online presence appears to be a LinkedIn page with no standalone website, and no recent news, deliveries, or registry listings were surfaced. Its operational status is unclear.

name: Watershed
tech_note: Watershed is an enterprise carbon accounting and sustainability reporting SaaS platform that also operates a vetted carbon removal marketplace connecting corporate buyers to CDR suppliers.
description: Watershed provides enterprise software for measuring, reducing, and reporting corporate emissions, and runs a curated marketplace of scientifically vetted carbon removal projects (DAC, bio-oil, biochar, ERW, reforestation, etc.) that customers can purchase from. The company does not physically remove CO2 itself — it acts as an intermediary/marketplace and accounting platform in the CDR ecosystem, similar to Patch or Supercritical, while its primary business is broader sustainability reporting software.

name: Wonderchar
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis kilns that convert Texas pecan shells (and some softwood) into biochar sold in multiple granular/powder grades as soil amendment, sequestering carbon long-term.
description: Wonderchar INC. is a Texas-based biochar producer that converts waste pecan shells into OMRI-certified biochar products (PecanChar Natural, LG+, Soil+, Powder+, EZ MIX) sold to farmers, nurseries, landscapers and fertilizer manufacturers. Products are offered in bulk bags and sacks for soil, compost, turf and fertilizer blending applications, with carbon sequestration as a co-benefit.

name: Woodcache
tech_note: Buries waste woody biomass from wildfire-risk forests in engineered anaerobic underground pits designed to inhibit decomposition, with MRV via flux chambers and subterranean sensors.
description: Woodcache PBC is a U.S. public benefit corporation that buries waste woody biomass (from wildfire mitigation and forestry thinning) in engineered, cold/dry/anaerobic underground pits for durable CO2 removal. They completed their La Veta, Colorado production-scale project in 2024 with support from a 4 Corners Carbon Removal grant and sell Puro.earth-certified CORCs.

name: Woodtek Biochar
tech_note: Woodtek Engineering designs, manufactures and operates two-stage pyrolysis plants (C1000) that convert woody biomass and waste into EBC-grade biochar while producing heat and power.
description: Woodtek is a UK-based (Powys, Wales) family-run engineering firm that builds pyrolysis units, notably the C1000, and operates its own biochar production at its HQ R&D site. Its equipment underpins multiple UK biochar operations including the Shropshire Council / BioDynamic Carbon joint venture and Brodie Biomass, with output registered on Puro.earth for CORC issuance.

name: Wundergarten
tech_note: Formulates and sells biochar-containing gardening substrates, fertilizers, and seeds using EBC-certified pyrolysis biochar from cocoa shells and herbs.
description: Wundergarten is a German consumer gardening brand founded in 2019 that sells biochar-based soils, fertilizers, and biochar-coated seeds to retail customers via its webshop, Amazon, and selected supermarkets. The biochar is made from cocoa shells and herbs via pyrolysis (EBC-certified), and the company markets CO2 storage in soil as a co-benefit. They function as a biochar product formulator/distributor rather than a credit-issuing CDR project developer.

name: XPRIZE Carbon Removal Competition Page
tech_note: Global incentive-prize competition that funded and validated CDR suppliers across DAC, ERW, biochar, ocean, and biomass pathways; ran 2021–2025 with a $100M purse.
description: XPRIZE Carbon Removal was a $100M incentive competition funded by the Musk Foundation, launched on Earth Day 2021 and concluded in April 2025 when Mati Carbon won the $50M grand prize for enhanced rock weathering. Runners-up included NetZero (biochar), Vaulted Deep (biomass burial), and UNDO Carbon (ERW), with XFACTOR awards to Planetary and Project Hajar. The competition page is run by the XPRIZE Foundation, a nonprofit that designs and operates incentive prizes — not a CDR supplier itself but a major catalyst of the CDR ecosystem.

name: Yale Center for Natural Carbon Capture
Yama
tech_note: Hybrid electrochemical DAC using a non-toxic liquid sorbent with pH and temperature swing desorption, integrating electrodialysis and low-grade heat to cut energy use.
description: Yama is a Paris-based Direct Air Capture startup developing a hybrid electrochemical/thermal desorption technology with a proprietary liquid sorbent to lower DAC energy and cost. The company operates a small pilot near Paris (~25 tCO2/yr) and is targeting a first-of-a-kind commercial plant around 2030, with partnerships including Great Carbon Valley in Kenya and early credit buyers like Klarna via Milkywire.

name: Yellow Duck
tech_note: Develops a floating, wave-powered direct air capture device ("Wave-DAC") that harnesses ocean wave motion to generate electricity, produce hydrogen via seawater electrolysis, and capture CO2 from the atmosphere.
description: Yellow Duck Inc. is a Kobe, Japan cleantech startup, led by CEO Shigeo Nakayama, developing the Wave-DAC — an egg-shaped floating device that tilts with waves to generate power used to drive electrolysis and atmospheric CO2 capture. The company won the Marinetech Grand Prix 2023 Grand Prize and exhibited at Expo 2025 Osaka. Still at early prototype/verification stage.

name: Yggdrasil Trees
tech_note: Pre-seed project developer designing urban-integrated DAC units (targeting ~800 t CO2/unit/year), licensing solid sorbent IP from third-party DAC technology providers.
description: Yggdrasil Trees is developing a decentralized, multi-functional direct air capture (DAC) solution designed for integration into urban environments, aiming to remove 800 tonnes of CO2 per unit per year. The company is positioned as a project developer focusing on licensing sorbent materials from other DAC companies to accelerate deployment. It is a US-based pre-seed startup in the LACI portfolio.

name: Yuanchu Technology
tech_note: Yuanchu uses a chemical-looping reactor (YAM) to mineralize CO2 from flue gas or ambient air with calcium-rich industrial solid waste (carbide slag, steel slag) or silicates, producing stable calcium carbonate for permanent sequestration.
description: Yuanchu Technology is a Beijing-based company founded in 2014 that develops large-scale, low-cost permanent carbon mineralization technology. It is developing direct air mineralization (DAM) technology for removing CO2 from air and permanently sequestering it into solid carbonated material, claiming stability for 1000 years. It was selected as an XPRIZE Carbon Removal finalist in the Rocks category competing for the $50M Musk Foundation prize.

name: ZEN Carbon
tech_note: Injects captured CO₂ into ready-mix concrete during mixing, where it reacts to form stable calcium carbonate minerals, permanently storing CO₂ while reducing cement content and improving strength.
description: ZEN Carbon is a Kenya-based startup whose mineralization technology injects captured CO₂ directly into concrete, cutting cement use and emissions while strengthening the material itself. It sources CO₂ from partners like Octavia Carbon's Direct Air Capture systems and infuses it into concrete during mixing. In late 2025 the company moved from pilot stage to live industrial deployment by partnering with Flamingo Concrete, a ready-mix concrete supplier in Kenya.

name: ZS2
tech_note: Manufactures magnesium-oxide (MgO) cement building products that sequester CO2 via mineralization, paired with a proprietary DAC front-end for CO2 supply.
description: ZS2 Technologies is a Calgary-based manufacturer of magnesium cement building materials (boards, panels, tiles, sheathing) that mineralize CO2 into the cement matrix, reportedly at ~10% by weight. The company also develops a proprietary direct-air-capture process to source CO2 for sequestration, and was a Carbon Removal XPRIZE Milestone 1 top-60 company. In May 2025 it launched its commercially-ready Gen 2 product platform with $9.9M+ in grant backing.

name: ZeoDAC
tech_note: ZeoDAC uses a proprietary amine-free, solid-sorbent DAC process based on commercially available zeolite/molecular sieve materials, capturing both CO2 and water via a temperature-vacuum swing adsorption cycle.
description: Founded in June 2023, the Atlanta-based company was established by Professor Christopher W. Jones (Georgia Tech) and Professor Mark E. Davis (Caltech) to extract carbon dioxide from air using zeolites. Investors include Wilson Hill Ventures, Caltech, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, Freeflow Ventures and Global Brain. Note: captured CO2 may be sequestered or used in beverages/chemicals, so end-use pathway is a mix of CDR and CCU.

name: Zero Carbon Systems
tech_note: Solid-sorbent monolith DAC with low-temperature vacuum adsorption process, inherited and advanced from Global Thermostat technology, targeting megaton-scale deployment.
description: Zero Carbon Systems is a US-based direct air capture company that acquired pioneer Global Thermostat in May 2024, combining Global Thermostat's solid-sorbent DAC technology with Zero Carbon Systems' engineering capabilities. The company plans a 2,500-ton per year demonstration plant by 2025-2026, a 50,000-ton commercial plant two years later, and a million-ton scale plant by 2030. Global Thermostat's DAC technology uses a proprietary solid sorbent embedded on a monolith with a low-temperature vacuum adsorption process.

name: ZeroEx
tech_note: Applies basaltic rock powder from local quarries to agricultural fields in Germany to accelerate silicate weathering and permanently sequester CO2 as bicarbonate, with proprietary in-soil MRV sensors (SIAs).
description: ZeroEx is a German climate tech startup founded in 2022 by Tony Oehm, Hannes Steinle, and Marcel Kuhs, established as one of Europe's leading enhanced rock weathering companies. The company develops ERW projects in Germany using basaltic rock powders derived as a by-product of existing mining operations, having tested over 100 quarries to secure feedstocks with high CDR potential and low heavy-metal concentrations. They are listed as a supplier on both the Puro.earth and Isometric registries.

name: [C]Worthy
tech_note: Nonprofit Focused Research Organization building open-source ocean modeling and MRV software (C-Star) for quantifying marine CDR like ocean alkalinity enhancement.
description: [C]Worthy is a nonprofit research and development organization focused on delivering the core computational technologies needed to support quantitative assessments of ocean-based carbon dioxide removal. They build open-source software, conduct basic research on the efficacy of ocean-based CDR technologies, create and curate publicly available datasets, and promote scientific standards for evaluating the safety and effectiveness of ocean-based CDR activities. They do not themselves remove CO2; they supply MRV modeling infrastructure (C-Star) used by mCDR developers and verifiers like Isometric.

name: agriCARBON/MicroCHAR
tech_note: Pyrolyzes biomass into microgranular biochar and enriches it with organic nutrients, rhizobacteria, and mycorrhizal fungi as a soil conditioner/fertilizer for agricultural carbon sequestration.
description: MicroCHAR is a Czech biochar-based microgranular soil conditioner developed by the BIOUHEL.CZ team in collaboration with Czech University of Life Sciences Prague. The product combines biochar (from biomass pyrolysis) with organic nutrients, rhizobacteria, and mycorrhizal fungi for application in ecological agriculture, positioning itself as both a soil amendment and a carbon sequestration tool.

name: alterBiota
tech_note: alterBiota pyrolyzes sawmill wood residues and chemically exfoliates the product into a liquid hydrous bio-graphene oxide (hBGO) admixture that reduces Portland cement demand while permanently locking biomass-derived carbon into concrete.
description: alterBiota is a Nova Scotia-based green-materials startup making hBGO, a wood-derived biographene concrete admixture that cuts cement use and stores biogenic carbon in concrete infrastructure. It closed a CAD$4M seed round in May 2024 led by Invest Nova Scotia and BDC Capital's Climate Tech Fund to build a commercial-scale plant and run industrial trials. The company operates a pilot plant in Edwardsville, NS and is scaling toward ~2,200 tonnes/year of solid biographene.

name: atdepth
tech_note: MIT spin-off developing a GPU-based, data-assimilating ocean modeling and monitoring system that provides Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) for marine carbon dioxide removal projects.
description: atdepth MRV is a Cambridge, MA-based MIT spin-off providing MRV services to the marine CDR (mCDR) industry. It combines multi-scale ocean and biogeochemical modeling with monitoring data to quantify carbon removal for mCDR project developers. The company received a $2.6M ARPA-E SEA-CO2 grant and has partnered with Deep Sky to monitor direct ocean capture operations in Canada.

name: bionero
tech_note: Produces EBC-certified biochar from organic residues via PYREG pyrolysis technology and markets biochar-amended potting soil and soil products that fix carbon long-term.
description: bionero GmbH is a small biochar producer based in Thurnau, Bavaria (Germany), founded in 2018. They carbonize organic residues using PYREG pyrolysis systems to make EBC-certified biochar, which they incorporate into peat-free potting soils and related products sold to consumers and horticultural markets.

name: corigin
tech_note: Uses vacuum pyrolysis (licensed Pyrovac technology) to convert almond shells and orchard residues into biochar, bio-oil for underground injection, and liquid bio-distillates for agriculture.
description: Corigin Solutions is a US-based company that converts agricultural residues (almond shells, orchard trimmings, nutshells) into biochar and bio-oil via vacuum pyrolysis. Their Corichar biochar is sold as a soil amendment, and their bio-oil is supplied to Charm Industrial for deep geological sequestration. They are a standalone CDR supplier, not a subsidiary.

name: ecoLocked
tech_note: ecoLocked converts waste-biomass biochar into functional concrete admixtures (eLM Zero) that permanently lock biogenic carbon into buildings while replacing cement/aggregates.
description: Berlin-based startup ecoLocked, founded in 2021, is among the few global producers of concrete admixtures utilizing biochar for carbon removal, focusing on eco-friendly building materials. Its flagship product, eLM Zero, is a carbon-negative admixture designed to reduce concrete's net carbon footprint by up to 100%. The company raised €4 million in a seed round led by Matterwave Ventures and Climentum Capital, with proceeds used to expand production, introduce new product lines and grow demand.

name: ecoX
tech_note: Plans to produce biochar from biomass via pyrolysis in Namibia as part of a "Poverty Eradication Franchise" model tied to African Savanna re-wilding, aiming to generate CDR credits.
description: ecoX, LLC is a US-based early-stage biochar developer listed on Puro.earth as a future supplier (ecoX-1) with a planned facility in Namibia. The Puro listing shows 0 CORCs issued and the project is in early-development/feasibility stage. With only 1 employee on LinkedIn and a thin website, the company appears to be a very small, pre-operational venture.

name: enfinium
tech_note: enfinium operates UK energy-from-waste (EfW) plants and is deploying carbon capture and storage across its fleet; because ~50% of the waste feedstock is biogenic, capturing and geologically storing the CO2 produces net carbon removals (WECCS/BECCS).
description: enfinium is a leading UK energy from waste operator with four operational sites in West Yorkshire, Kent and Flintshire, and two in construction, diverting 2.3 million tonnes of unrecyclable waste from landfill. The company is installing CCS technology on its EfW facilities — with active pilots using Kanadevia Inova (HZI) and Nuada at Ferrybridge and Parc Adfer — to turn them into net-negative carbon removal sources. enfinium's Net Zero Transition Plan targets up to 1.2 million tonnes of carbon removals annually by the 2030s, backed by an investment program of up to £1.7 billion.

name: eoc energy ocean
tech_note: Pyrolyzes regional woody biomass into EBC-certified biochar (Pflanzenkohle) in Luthern, Switzerland, with waste heat supplied to the village.
description: eoc energy ocean GmbH is a Lucerne-based biochar producer founded in 2017 that turns untreated regional wood into EBC AgroBio/Futter+ certified Swiss biochar, binding CO2 and delivering process heat to the local village. The company also advises on pyrolysis projects, biomass utilization, and CO2/EBC certification. It won the Albert Koechlin Foundation's 2024 Environment Award.

name: goodcarbon
tech_note: Operates a marketplace/platform connecting nature-based carbon project developers with corporate buyers, offering portfolio curation and due diligence for NbS carbon credits.
description: goodcarbon is a Berlin-based platform that sources, assesses, and sells nature-based solutions carbon credits (reforestation, regenerative agriculture, blue carbon) to corporates building carbon portfolios. It is a marketplace/broker in the CDR ecosystem rather than a physical removal supplier, though it includes some removal projects alongside avoidance credits.

name: greenSand
tech_note: Sources, crushes, and distributes olivine-rich rock as gravel/sand/split products that weather on contact with rainwater to remove atmospheric CO2.
description: greenSand is a Netherlands-based enhanced rock weathering supplier founded in 2009 that sells olivine products sourced from mines in Spain, Norway, Italy and Turkey, replacing conventional sand and stone in gardens, pathways, municipalities and sports fields. They also issue CO2 removal certificates registered with ONCRA, including a certified Uithoornlijn project validated in 2025.

name: myclimate
tech_note: Swiss non-profit foundation that develops, finances and sells carbon offset and removal projects (nature-based, biochar, reduction) and provides climate consulting and education services.
description: myclimate is a Swiss non-profit climate protection foundation, spun out of ETH Zurich in 2002, that co-develops and finances voluntary carbon market projects including afforestation and biochar CDR, while also offering footprinting and consulting services. It acts as a project developer, broker and advisory organisation rather than building removal technology itself. CDR is part of a broader portfolio that includes emissions-reduction offsets.

name: pHathom
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from coastal bioenergy flue gas and converts it using a limestone–seawater reactor into dissolved bicarbonate that is returned to the ocean for long-duration storage.
description: pHathom Technologies is a Halifax, Nova Scotia-based cleantech startup founded in 2024 that captures biogenic CO2 from coastal bioenergy facilities and converts it via a limestone/seawater reactor into stable bicarbonate, which is returned to the ocean for durable storage. The company closed a $4M seed round in February 2026 (led by Propeller Ventures, with Carmeuse Ventures, NBIF and Invest Nova Scotia), bringing total committed capital to over $12M including a lead role in a $16M Ocean Supercluster project, and was selected for Frontier's advance-purchase program (~US$500K). It plans a pilot at Huntsman Marine Science Centre in 2026 and a college biomass-boiler deployment in 2027.

name: pHathom Technologies
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from coastal biomass bioenergy plants and converts it, via a limestone-seawater weathering reactor, into stable bicarbonate that is stored in the ocean.
description: pHathom Technologies is a Halifax, Nova Scotia cleantech startup (founded 2023/24) developing a hybrid BECCS + ocean alkalinity enhancement pathway it calls Bioenergy Carbon Capture and Ocean Storage (BECCOS). It bolts onto coastal biomass power/heat plants, dissolves captured CO2 in seawater with limestone to form bicarbonate, and releases it for durable marine storage. The company closed a $4M seed round led by Propeller Ventures in Feb 2026 (>$12M total committed capital), was selected for Frontier's advance purchase program, and is running a completed pilot at NSCC Lunenburg with a Huntsman Marine Science Centre trial planned for summer 2026.

name: pyropower
tech_note: Designs and manufactures pyrolysis CHP systems (Pyro-ClinX) combining pyrolysis reactors with an externally fired micro gas turbine to convert biogenic residues into biochar, heat and electricity.
description: pyropower GmbH is a German cleantech engineering firm based in Cottbus that develops decentralized pyrolysis combined heat and power systems producing biochar, green electricity and heat from wood and biogenic residues. Their flagship Pyro-ClinX plant pairs pyrolysis with an air-bearing micro gas turbine and has been deployed in reference projects including Darmstadt and Görlitz.

name: renu.earth
tech_note: Renu Earth produces biochar from sawmill wood residues in Southern Africa (KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa) via pyrolysis, generating Puro.earth-certified CORCs and selling biochar to fertilizer manufacturers.
description: Renu Earth is a US-incorporated biochar carbon removal company running its first project with a major sawmill in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, converting sustainable wood residues into biochar and generating certified carbon removal credits through Puro.Earth. Carbonfuture committed to purchase the initial 1,000 CORCs and will broker up to 102,000 CORCs annually, with plans to expand to 10 additional sites generating up to 200,000 CORCs annually by 2027.

name: reverce
tech_note: Provides an end-to-end enhanced rock weathering service — tailored silicate rock material applied to farmland, combined with soil analyses, CO2 efflux measurements, and a proprietary MRV approach.
description: reverce is a German carbon dioxide removal company focused on enhanced rock weathering (ERW), managing the end-to-end process including methodology, tailored rock material composition, land distribution with farmers, and MRV. The company is closely tied to the Carbon Drawdown Initiative and involved in research projects such as Project Carbdown in Germany and the Olivine Project in Greece. Public activity has been quiet, with the most prominent coverage dating to 2023 and a small LinkedIn following.

name: ÖKT Offenhausen
tech_note: Operates NGE T-Cracker pyrolysis plants that convert sewage sludge and organic residues into EBC-certified biochar, with heat integration to the co-located biogas facility.
description: ÖKT Offenhausen is a biogas facility in Offenhausen, Bavaria, Germany that dries up to 30,000 tons of locally sourced sewage sludge annually, with drying units powered by sustainable biogas waste heat and CO2-negative Biomass-to-Biochar heat. The pyrolysis system dries sewage sludge and organic residues to create nutrient-rich biochar as a soil additive, produces pyrolysis gas for thermal energy, and is certified by EBC and EBC Agro-Bio. Carbon Standards International documented ÖKT as a case study creating a carbon sink of approximately 1,937 tons of CO2e.

name: ÖkoMAXX Energiewerke
tech_note: Operates biomass power plants in Austria that co-produce biochar, registered as a carbon sink project under the Global Biochar C-Sink Standard.
description: ÖkoMAXX Energiewerke GmbH is an Austrian company based in Gänserndorf engaged in the generation of electricity and heat, operation of biomass power plants, and trade in goods of all kinds. It is wholly owned by PurEnergy Holding GmbH and has a biochar production site at Altweitra; its biochar project (GCSP1127) was validated under the Global Biochar C-Sink Standard on 2025-06-23, making it an active biochar CDR supplier.

name: Öresundskraft
tech_note: Amine-based carbon capture on flue gas from a waste-fired CHP plant (Filbornaverket), with the biogenic fraction of captured CO2 permanently stored geologically offshore, generating BECCS negative emissions.
description: Öresundskraft is a Swedish municipally owned energy utility developing a first-of-its-kind CCS facility at its Filbornaverket waste-fired CHP plant in Helsingborg, expected to cost approximately SEK 3 billion and capture 200,000 tonnes of CO2 annually. The biogenic fraction of the captured waste-derived CO2 is stored permanently to generate bio-CCS negative emissions. The company has already signed agreements for future purchase of negative emissions certificates with buyers including Wihlborgs and Helsingborgshem.
